docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
KARIANA is an AI-powered Unreal Engine 5.7+ plugin that enables comprehensive engine control through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Describe what you want in natural language, and Claude executes it in Unreal Engine.

Example

You: "Spawn a red cube at position 100, 0, 50 and add a point light above it"

Claude: Spawns the cube, creates a red material, applies it, and positions a point light - all automatically.

docs.title: 218+ MCP Tools
docs.text: Complete programmatic control of Unreal Engine with tools for actors, materials, blueprints, PCG, and more.

docs.title: Action Recorder
docs.text: Record your editor actions and generate reusable skills that can be replayed automatically.

docs.title: 22 Custom PCG Nodes
docs.text: Advanced procedural content generation with noise functions, patterns, and point manipulation.

docs.title: LLM Integration
docs.text: Built-in support for Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, and XAI for AI-powered workflows.

docs.title: KARIANA-Anim
docs.text: Tweening system for smooth animations and runtime motion control.

docs.title: Spatial Patterns
docs.text: Grid, circular, spline, scatter, and surface-based spawning with expert pattern selection.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to KARIANA are documented here.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• PCG node-wiring. The assistant can now connect the nodes in a PCG graph it builds — sampler to transform to spawner — so the graph generates right away instead of opening with disconnected nodes.
  • Client support bundle — export a redacted diagnostics zip (logs and versions, secrets scrubbed) in one click to share when you need support.
  • Unreal Engine 5.8 support — the plugin now runs on UE 5.8 as well as 5.7.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Cleaner chat: each assistant turn is grouped into a single, correctly ordered message.
  • You can queue a follow-up message while the model is still replying.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Windows sign-in no longer freezes on login.
  • Chat now shows every tool step in order, with an accurate tool counter and no silent steps.
  • Fixed a premature "finished" state and an incorrect backend label in the chat panel.
  • The in-editor "update available" banner now clears correctly after you install an update.

docs.title: Added - Cinematic Camera Presets
docs.text:
• 14 real-world cinema camera presets — ARRI ALEXA 35, ALEXA Mini LF, ALEXA 65, Sony VENICE 2, RED V-Raptor, RED Komodo-X, Sony BURANO, Sony FX6, Canon EOS C400, Canon EOS C70, Blackmagic URSA Cine 12K LF, Blackmagic Pocket 6K G2, Fujifilm GFX ETERNA 55, iPhone 17 Pro Max (PR #264)
  • 3 camera tiers — High-End, Mid-Range, Indie for different production scales
  • 2 new MCP tools — list_cinematic_cameras (with tier filtering) and spawn_cinematic_camera (configures filmback, focal length, aperture, ISO, shutter speed, EV range, Auto Exposure Histogram)
  • 3 bonus camera tools — create_camera_push_shot, focus_viewport_on_actor, sync_viewport

docs.title: Added - Camera Framing Skill
docs.text:
• Bone-based shot placement — spawns CineCameraActors for 7 standard cinematography shot types (ECU, CU, MCU, MS, CS, MFS, FS) using actual skeleton bone positions for accurate framing (PR #276)
  • Master Sequence creation — creates a Level Sequence with Shot Track containing each shot as a sub-sequence with Camera Cut Track
  • Look At eye tracking — optional TargetPoint-based eye tracking via CineCameraActor LookAt settings with relative offset to preserve framing

docs.title: Added - PBL Photorealistic Lighting
docs.text:
• 57 validated PBL presets — 25 outdoor + 32 interior presets with scientifically accurate lux values from NOAA, CIE, NIST, and Wikipedia public domain data (PR #267)
  • Sky Atmosphere Mie scattering — overcast and cloudy looks without changing sun intensity, using physically correct atmospheric diffusion
  • Deterministic execution hooks — all PBL tools use @deterministic_tool / @deterministic_resource decorators with input hashing, parameter validation, physical bounds clamping, and audit trail logging
  • 5 new MCP tools — create_lighting_scenario, query_lighting_presets, backup_current_lighting, restore_lighting_backup, adjust_lighting_intensity
  • 4 PBL tools registered — pbl_list_presets, pbl_apply_preset, pbl_spawn_rig, pbl_set_exposure (existing, now formally registered with deterministic wrappers)

docs.title: Fixed - UE5.7 Compatibility
docs.text: • UpdateChecker API fix — KarianaUpdateChecker updated for UE5.7 API changes that broke version checking on startup (PR #244)

docs.title: Added - Dual-MCP Architecture
docs.text:
• Dual-MCP server architecture — KARIANA now runs two MCP servers for Claude Code/Desktop: kariana-unreal (85 tools via socket on port 9877) and kariana-remote (114 tools via Remote Control HTTP on port 30010), totaling 199 tools across both servers (PR #240)
  • 8 previously hidden tools exposed via kariana-remote — tools that were registered but not accessible are now available through the Remote Control HTTP transport
  • Remote Control Python execution — bEnableRemotePythonExecution=True shipped in Config/DefaultEngine.ini for zero-config RC HTTP access

docs.title: Fixed - Dual-MCP Stability
docs.text:
• Fix exec() entry point bug — package entry points (kariana-mcp, kariana-remote) now pass __name__='__main__' to exec() so if __name__ == "__main__": guards work correctly (previously servers silently exited)
  • Fix dynamic proxy tool registration for FastMCP 2.x compatibility
  • Fix triple execution, temp file races, and module side effects in kariana-remote server

docs.title: Added - Installer Improvements
docs.text: • "Install to Project" option for Windows installer — users can now install KARIANA directly into a specific UE project's Plugins/ folder instead of only engine-wide (PR #239)

docs.title: Fixed - PowerShell 5.1 Compatibility
docs.text: • Fix upload-plugin-binaries.ps1 for PowerShell 5.1: nested Join-Path calls (3+ args only works in PS 6+), $LASTEXITCODE checks for native commands, @() wrapping for single-item arrays (PR #237)

docs.title: Fixed - CI
docs.text: • Fix error handling for binary download in build-installers.yml — workflow now fails with a clear error message when pre-built binaries are missing instead of producing a broken installer (PR #234)

docs.title: Fixed - Installer
docs.text: • Manual UE path selection — when Unreal Engine auto-detection fails, the installer now shows a folder picker dialog instead of blocking with an error, with option to skip UE integration entirely (PR #231)

docs.title: Added - Pre-Built Binaries for Installer
docs.text:

  • CI binary download — build-installers.yml Windows job downloads matching pre-built binaries and includes them in the installer, bringing installer size from ~2.7MB to ~15MB with working DLLs
  • Dev pre-release build documentation added to release workflow guide

docs.title: Fixed - CI

  • Shared level utilities (utils/level_utils.py) — world type detection, level resolution, PIE guard, streaming level compat for UE5.7

docs.title: Fixed - UE5.7 Python API Compatibility
docs.text:
• Replace removed world.get_streaming_levels() with get_streaming_levels_compat() using unreal.find_object() enumeration
  • Wrap get_world_asset_package_f_name() with str() to prevent unreal.Name JSON serialization crash
  • Use create_new_streaming_level() instead of add_level_to_world() (which doesn't load in UE5.7)
  • Fix move_actors_to_level() dest parameter: pass LevelStreaming, not ULevel
  • Replace removed streaming_method property with disable_distance_streaming editor property
  • Replace blocking time.sleep() polling with synchronous editor APIs to avoid game-thread deadlock

docs.title: Added - Offline Asset Toolkit
docs.text:
• 9 offline asset tools — search, inspect, index, trace references, list, classify, and browse .uasset files without the Unreal Editor running
  • SQLite FTS5 index — full-text search across project assets with type filtering and inheritance queries
  • Blueprint graph inspection — extract and summarize Blueprint node graphs from .uasset binary data
  • C++ source indexing — index header and source files for cross-language reference tracing
  • Adapted from UE-Agent-Asset-Toolkit (MIT License, Braden League)

  • Thumbs up / down feedback buttons — rate individual responses directly in the chat panel (▲ / ▼ icons placed to the right of the Copy button with a separator)

docs.title: Added - AWS Bedrock Backend
docs.text:
• Full AWS Bedrock provider (bedrock_backend.py + KarianaBedrockBridge.cpp) — routes assistant requests through a Lambda-backed API Gateway to the Bedrock Converse API
  • Bedrock daemon adapter — BedrockDaemonAdapter wires the Bedrock backend into the existing daemon loop without changing the Claude Code path
  • Qwen3 tool-calling support — converts MCP tool schemas to OpenAI format for Qwen3 models; all 90+ MCP tools available to Bedrock providers
  • Unauthenticated request rejection — Bedrock API endpoint rejects requests with a missing or empty user ID; the C++ bridge hard-fails before the HTTP call if KarianaUserId is empty

docs.text: • Play in Editor MCP tools — three new tools: play_in_editor, simulate_in_editor, and stop_play allow the AI to start and stop PIE sessions programmatically

docs.title: Added - Settings
docs.text:
• Temperature setting — UKarianaAssistantSettings::Temperature (0.0–1.0, default 0.7) controls response creativity and is wired to both the Claude Code and Bedrock providers
  • Max Agent Turns setting — UKarianaAssistantSettings::MaxAgentTurns (1–100, default 25) caps the agent tool-calling loop to prevent runaway execution

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • Socket auth token redaction — the auth token is now shown as only the first 6 characters in startup logs to avoid leaking secrets

docs.title: 1. Stdin O_NONBLOCK — Daemon crash loop fix
docs.text:
• File: Content/Python/kariana_agent_daemon.py, Content/Python/backends/bedrock_daemon_adapter.py
  • Problem: Mac's FMacPlatformProcess::CreatePipe sets O_NONBLOCK on pipe read ends. When dup2'd to daemon stdin, readline() returns empty immediately instead of blocking, causing "stdin EOF" crash loop.
  • Fix: os.set_blocking(sys.stdin.fileno(), True) at daemon startup.

docs.title: 2. WritePipe off-by-one — False write failure fix
docs.text:
• File: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.cpp
  • Problem: Mac's FMacPlatformProcess::WritePipe(FString) writes N+1 bytes (data + appended newline) but checks BytesWritten == N, always returning false on success.
  • Fix: Use raw-bytes WritePipe(void*, const uint8*, int32, int32*) overload which doesn't have the bug.

docs.title: 3. Venv Python discovery — No-shell path resolution
docs.text:
• File: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.cpp
  • Problem: Shell-based Python discovery broke on paths with spaces ("Unreal Projects").
  • Fix: Direct FPaths::FileExists(.venv/bin/python) check, no shell invocation.

docs.title: 4. Platform guard — Windows-only include
docs.text:
• File: Source/UnrealMCPBridge/Private/PythonBridge.cpp
  • Fix: #if PLATFORM_WINDOWS around Microsoft/MinimalWindowsApi.h include.

docs.title: 5. wstring → string — Mac filesystem path type
docs.text:
• File: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaDropTarget.cpp
  • Fix: Canonical.string() instead of Canonical.wstring() (Mac value_type is char, not wchar_t).

docs.title: 6. Blueprint variable types — Added object references
docs.text:
• File: Source/GenerativeAISupportEditor/Private/MCP/GenBlueprintUtils.cpp
  • Added: material_instance, material, texture, static_mesh, actor to the C++ add_variable type map.

docs.title: 7. MCP SSE auto-start disabled
docs.text:
• File: Content/Python/socket_server_config.json
  • Fix: auto_start_mcp_sse: false — prevents fastmcp/requests import errors in UE's embedded Python (not needed with ECA-style C++ architecture).

docs.title: 8. JSON chunked Unicode escape handling
docs.text:
• File: Content/Python/unreal_socket_server.py
  • Fix: Treat Invalid \uXXXX escape as incomplete data (same as Unterminated string) when receiving chunked socket data.

docs.title: Claude Code Prompt (copy-paste this to your team)
docs.text:
You are onboarding a developer to the KARIANA v0.9 release candidate plugin for Unreal Engine 5.7.

## Setup Steps

1. **Pull the latest developer branch:**
   ```bash
   cd <your-kariana-plugin-directory>
   git checkout developer
   git pull origin developer
   ```

2. **Verify version:**
   Open `KARIANA.uplugin` and confirm `"VersionName": "0.9.0"` and `"Version": 90`.

3. **Set up Baseten API key** (required for KARIANA LLM v0.9):
   Set the environment variable before launching Unreal Engine:
   ```bash
   # Windows (PowerShell)
   $env:KARIANA_BASETEN_API_KEY = "<team-api-key>"

   # Windows (CMD)
   set KARIANA_BASETEN_API_KEY=<team-api-key>

   # macOS/Linux
   export KARIANA_BASETEN_API_KEY=<team-api-key>
   ```
   For persistent setup, add this to your system environment variables or shell profile.

4. **Open your UE project** with the KARIANA plugin installed.

5. **Verify in-editor:**
   - Go to `Edit > Project Settings > KARIANA Assistant`
   - Set Provider to **Baseten (Cloud Inference)**
   - The model dropdown should show **"KARIANA LLM v0.9"**
   - Open the KARIANA chat panel and send a test message: "What tools are available?"
   - Confirm you receive a response from the Baseten endpoint

6. **Test Bedrock fallback (if configured):**
   If you also have `BEDROCK_ENDPOINT` configured, the plugin uses dual-backend routing:
   - KARIANA LLM v0.9 handles reasoning tasks (Verify/Teach modes)
   - Bedrock/Haiku handles tool execution (Standard/Create/Plan modes)

## v0.9 Release Candidate Rules

This is a **release candidate** — the codebase is now locked for stability:

- **NO new features** — only bug fixes, tests, and evals
- All PRs must target the `developer` branch
- Prefix PR titles with `[v0.9-fix]`
- Focus areas: stability, test coverage, evaluation benchmarks
- Report any issues with KARIANA LLM inference, tool calling, or UI regressions

## Key Changes in v0.9

- **KARIANA LLM v0.9**: Our reasoning model (formerly "Nemotron 120B"), hosted on Baseten
- **Ultrathink Pipeline**: 3-tier system — Sonnet 4.6 plans → KARIANA LLM revises → Haiku executes
- **UI Redesign**: New ThemeManager, StyleSets, toolbar, plan/choice cards
- **ECA-Style Commands**: Structured AI commands via C++ MCP HTTP server
- **Blueprint-Lisp**: LISP DSL for creating Blueprint graphs in single tool calls

## Troubleshooting

- **"KARIANA LLM v0.9" not appearing**: Ensure `KARIANA_BASETEN_API_KEY` is set before launching UE
- **Inference timeout**: Check Baseten dashboard for API key validity and rate limits
- **Tool calls failing**: KARIANA LLM routes tool execution to Bedrock/Haiku — ensure both backends are configured if using dual-backend mode
- **Build errors after pull**: Delete `Intermediate/` and `Binaries/` in the plugin folder, then rebuild

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to KARIANA are documented here.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• Dual-MCP Architecture — KARIANA now provides 199 tools across two MCP servers for comprehensive Unreal Engine control
  • "Install to Project" Option — Windows installer supports installing directly into a specific UE project's Plugins folder
  • Sub-Level & World Partition Tools — 17 new tools for sub-level management, data layers, streaming sources, and HLOD generation
  • AWS Bedrock Provider — Cloud AI provider support via AWS Bedrock with Qwen3 and Claude models
  • In-Editor Chat Panel — Native Slate chat interface with markdown rendering, image previews, and conversation history
  • Conversation Undo/Redo — Undo AI actions with automatic Unreal Engine scene rollback
  • KARIANA Modes — Validate, Teach, and Create modes for different workflows
  • Action Recorder — Record editor actions and generate reusable skills
  • 22 Custom PCG Nodes — Procedural content generation with noise functions, patterns, and point manipulation
  • Multi-Platform Installers — Windows .exe, macOS, and Linux installers available

docs.title: AI Provider Support
docs.text:
• Claude Code Bridge — Primary integration via Claude CLI
  • AWS Bedrock — Cloud-based AI with configurable models and temperature
  • LM Studio (Experimental) — Local LLM support via OpenAI-compatible API (localhost:1234)
  • Ollama (Experimental) — Local open-source model support (localhost:11434)

docs.title: Improvements
docs.text:
• Configurable temperature and max agent turns for all AI providers
  • Tool category filtering for optimized local LLM performance
  • Gradio Admin Dashboard for model and tool management
  • Remote access via Cloudflare Tunnel endpoints
  • UE 5.7 compatibility updates

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• Fixed UE 5.7 API compatibility issues
  • Fixed installer path detection for various UE installation layouts
  • Improved error handling across all tool categories
  • Fixed streaming level compatibility with UE 5.7 Python API changes

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Unreal Engine 5.7+
  • Windows 10/11 (macOS and Linux support available)
  • Claude Desktop or compatible MCP client

docs.title: Support
docs.text: For issues or questions, contact Enterprise Support or reach out on Discord.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text: Common questions about KARIANA.

docs.title: What is KARIANA?
docs.text: KARIANA is an AI-powered plugin that connects Claude (or other AI assistants) to Unreal Engine, allowing natural language control of the engine. Instead of clicking through menus, you describe what you want and it happens.

docs.title: What can I do with KARIANA?
docs.text:
• Spawn and manipulate actors
  • Create and apply materials
  • Set up lighting
  • Create Blueprints
  • Organize your level
  • Take screenshots
  • And 200+ more operations

docs.title: Which Unreal Engine versions are supported?
docs.text: KARIANA requires Unreal Engine 5.7 or newer.

docs.title: Which AI assistants work with KARIANA?
docs.text: Currently, Claude Desktop is the primary supported client. Any MCP-compatible client should work.

docs.title: Is KARIANA free?
docs.text: Yes, KARIANA is open source and free to use.

docs.title: I get "Failed to proxy request to Clerk FAPI: fetch failed" when I try to sign in. What do I do?
docs.text:
Clear your cookies for app.kariana.ai only (DevTools → Storage/Application → Cookies → delete all) and sign in again. This is a known issue caused by stale browser cookies accumulating across sessions.

See Troubleshooting → Account & Sign-In for step-by-step instructions.

docs.title: Why does signing in work in a private/incognito window but not in my regular browser?
docs.text: Private windows start with an empty cookie jar. If your regular browser works in private mode but fails normally, that's a strong sign of the issue above — clearing cookies for app.kariana.ai will resolve it.

docs.title: Where do I install the plugin?
docs.text:
Two options:

  1. Engine-wide: [UE Install]/Engine/Plugins/Marketplace/KARIANA/
  2. Per-project: [Your Project]/Plugins/KARIANA/

docs.title: The installer failed. What do I do?
docs.text:
Try manual installation:

  1. Download from GitHub Releases

  2. Extract to your plugins folder

  3. Enable in Edit > Plugins
  4. Configure Claude Desktop manually

See Installation Guide for details.

docs.title: Do I need to install anything else?
docs.text:
Yes, enable these UE plugins:

  • Remote Control API
  • Remote Control Web Interface
  • Python Script Plugin

docs.title: How do I talk to Unreal Engine?
docs.text:
Just describe what you want in natural language:

"Spawn a red cube at 0, 0, 100"
"Add a spotlight above the cube"
"Take a screenshot"

docs.title: Do I need to know tool names?
docs.text: No! Just describe your intent. KARIANA figures out which tools to use.

docs.title: Can I undo KARIANA's changes?
docs.text: Yes, use Unreal Engine's standard undo (Ctrl+Z). Most KARIANA operations are undoable.

docs.title: Can I use KARIANA while the game is playing?
docs.text: Most features work during Play In Editor (PIE). Some editor-only features may be limited.

docs.title: How do I stop a long operation?
docs.text: Close Claude Desktop or stop the operation in UE. KARIANA operations respect cancellation.

docs.title: Can KARIANA create entire games?
docs.text: KARIANA is a tool, not a game generator. It helps with specific tasks like level design, lighting, and prototyping. Creating a complete game requires human creativity and design.

docs.title: Does KARIANA support C++?
docs.text: KARIANA primarily works with editor operations. For C++ code generation, you'd use Claude directly, not through KARIANA.

docs.title: Can I use custom meshes?
docs.text:
Yes, reference them by their content path:

"Spawn an actor with mesh /Game/MyMeshes/Chair"

docs.title: Does KARIANA work with Marketplace assets?
docs.text: Yes, any asset in your project can be referenced.

docs.title: Can KARIANA create animations?
docs.text: Limited support through Sequencer tools. Full animation creation is not yet supported.

docs.title: Is KARIANA slow?
docs.text: Most operations complete in milliseconds. Complex operations (like building lighting) take as long as they would manually.

docs.title: Does KARIANA affect editor performance?
docs.text: Minimal impact. The socket server uses negligible resources when idle.

docs.title: Can I use KARIANA on large projects?
docs.text: Yes, but operations on many actors may take longer. Use batch operations and organization for best results.

docs.title: "UE_NOT_CONNECTED" error
docs.text:
1. Ensure Unreal Engine is running with a project open
  2. Check that Remote Control plugins are enabled
  3. Verify ports 30010 and 9877 aren't blocked

See Troubleshooting for more solutions.

docs.title: Claude can't find KARIANA tools
docs.text:
1. Check your Claude Desktop config file
  2. Verify JSON syntax
  3. Restart Claude Desktop completely

docs.title: Commands work but nothing happens
docs.text:
1. Check you're in the right level
  2. Verify actor names are correct
  3. Look in Output Log for errors

docs.title: Is KARIANA safe to use?
docs.text: Yes. KARIANA only responds to local connections by default. It cannot be accessed remotely unless you explicitly configure it.

docs.title: Does KARIANA send data anywhere?
docs.text: No. All communication is local between Claude Desktop, the MCP server, and Unreal Engine.

docs.title: Can KARIANA delete my files?
docs.text: KARIANA only operates within Unreal Engine. It can delete assets within UE but not arbitrary files on your system.

docs.title: Can I extend KARIANA?
docs.text: Yes! KARIANA is open source. You can add custom tools by modifying the Python handlers.

docs.title: How do I report bugs?
docs.text:
Open an issue on GitHub with:

  • Steps to reproduce
  • Expected vs actual behavior
  • UE and KARIANA versions

docs.title: Can I contribute?
docs.text: Yes! See the Contributing Guide.

docs.title: How is KARIANA different from Unreal's AI features?
docs.text: Unreal's built-in AI features focus on runtime game AI (behavior trees, etc.). KARIANA is for editor-time operations controlled by an external AI assistant.

docs.title: Why use KARIANA instead of Blueprints?
docs.text:
Different use cases:

  • Blueprints: Permanent game logic
  • KARIANA: Rapid prototyping, level design, bulk operations

They complement each other.

docs.title: Can KARIANA replace a level designer?
docs.text: No. KARIANA is a tool that helps level designers work faster. Human creativity and design sense are still essential.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Solutions for common KARIANA issues.

docs.title: "Failed to proxy request to Clerk FAPI: fetch failed" on the sign-in page
docs.text:
Symptoms: The sign-in card at app.kariana.ai/sign-in shows the error:

Failed to proxy request to Clerk FAPI: fetch failed

when you submit your password or request an email verification code. A private/incognito window may sign in normally, while your regular browser keeps failing.

Cause: One or more cookies accumulated in your browser for app.kariana.ai are being forwarded to the authentication upstream and cause the request to fail before it leaves our infrastructure. This happens most often for accounts that have signed in many times across deploys or Clerk instance migrations.

Solution — clear cookies for app.kariana.ai only:

  1. Open the browser DevTools (F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I / Cmd+Option+I).
  2. Go to the storage panel:
  3. Firefox: Storage tab
  4. Chrome / Edge / Brave: Application tab
  5. Expand Cookies and select https://app.kariana.ai.
  6. Select all rows → right-click → Delete All.
  7. Reload /sign-in and sign in again.

You only lose your session on app.kariana.ai; all other sites are unaffected.

Alternatives if you can't open DevTools:

  • Open a private/incognito window and sign in there.
  • Use Clear browsing data scoped to app.kariana.ai only (Chrome: Settings → Privacy → Site settings).

If the error persists after clearing cookies, contact support with the time of the failed attempt so we can correlate with server logs.

docs.title: "UE_NOT_CONNECTED" Error
docs.text:
Symptoms: Claude reports it cannot connect to Unreal Engine.

Solutions:

  1. Verify UE is running
  2. Open Unreal Engine
  3. Load or create a project

  4. Check that the editor is fully loaded

  5. Check Remote Control plugin

  6. Go to Edit > Plugins
  7. Search for "Remote Control"
  8. Ensure both plugins are enabled

  9. Restart UE if you just enabled them

  10. Verify ports 

    # Check if ports are listening (Windows)
netstat -an | findstr "30010"
netstat -an | findstr "9877"

  11. Check firewall

  12. Allow UE through Windows Firewall

  13. Allow ports 30010, 30020, 9877

  14. Restart services

  15. Close Claude Desktop
  16. Close Unreal Engine
  17. Restart both

docs.title: "Connection Refused"
docs.text:
Symptoms: Socket connection fails immediately.

Solutions:

  1. Check KARIANA plugin is enabled
  2. Edit > Plugins > KARIANA

  3. Enable and restart

  4. Verify socket server started

  5. Check Output Log for: [KARIANA] Socket server started

  6. Check port availability 

    netstat -an | findstr "9877"
    If another app uses 9877, change the port in settings.

docs.title: Remote (Extended) Tools Not Working
docs.text:
Symptoms: Core tools (blueprints, actors, etc.) work but extended tools (cinematics, physics, PCG, patterns, etc.) fail or the remote MCP server (port 8002) crashes on startup.

Solutions:

  1. Enable Remote Control Web Server
  2. Go to Edit > Project Settings
  3. Search for Remote Control Web Server
  4. Enable Auto Start Web Server ✅
  5. Enable Auto Start Web Socket Server ✅
  6. Verify port is 30010 (HTTP) and 30020 (WebSocket)

  7. Restart Unreal Engine

  8. Enable Remote Execution

  9. In Project Settings, search for Remote Control
  10. Under Security, enable:
    • Enable Remote Python Execution ✅
    • Allow Console Command Remote Execution ✅

  11. Under Python Remote Execution, enable:

    • Enable Remote Execution? ✅

  12. Disable passphrase enforcement (or configure it)

  13. In Remote Control > Security, check Enforce Passphrase for Remote Clients
  14. If enabled with 0 passphrase entries, all connections to port 30010 will be blocked

  15. Either uncheck it, or add a passphrase and configure your MCP client accordingly

  16. Verify port 30010 is listening 

    netstat -an | findstr "30010"
    If port 30010 is not listening after enabling the settings, restart Unreal Engine.

Why does this only affect extended tools?

KARIANA uses two MCP servers. The core server (port 8001) communicates through KARIANA's own socket server (port 9877), which starts automatically with the plugin. The remote server (port 8002) routes through Unreal's Remote Control API (port 30010), which requires these project settings to be enabled.

docs.title: Intermittent Disconnections
docs.text:
Symptoms: Connection works sometimes, drops randomly.

Solutions:

  1. Increase timeout 

    {
  "env": {
    "KARIANA_TIMEOUT": "60"
  }
}

  2. Check system resources

  3. Close unnecessary applications

  4. Check CPU/memory usage

  5. Disable sleep mode

  6. Prevent computer from sleeping during use

docs.title: "Actor Not Found"
docs.text:
Symptoms: Commands fail with actor not found error.

Solutions:

  1. Use exact name 

    "Select the actor named 'Cube_1'" (not just 'Cube')

  2. Check World Outliner

  3. Verify the actor exists

  4. Note the exact name

  5. Refresh actor list 

    "List all actors in the level"

docs.title: "Material Not Applied"
docs.text:
Symptoms: Material command succeeds but object doesn't change.

Solutions:

  1. Verify actor has mesh

  2. Empty actors can't have materials

  3. Check material exists 

    "List all materials"

  4. Specify material slot 

    "Apply M_Red to element 0 of the cube"

docs.title: Fab/glTF Asset — Textures Not Displaying
docs.text:
Symptoms: Asset imported from Fab (glTF format) appears untextured in viewport, despite material and textures being correctly assigned. You may see warnings like *Texture samples ... as Linear Color (these are informational, not the cause).

Root Cause: glTF assets often store UV maps on channel 1 or 2, while UE5 materials default to channel 0.

Diagnosis:

  1. Open the Static Mesh in the editor
  2. Click the UV dropdown in the toolbar
  3. Check which UV channel has valid, non-overlapping UVs (usually channel 1)

Fix — Step 1: Adjust UV channel on existing material (try first)

  1. Open the Interchange MaterialInstance assigned to the mesh
  2. If the parent material exposes a TexCoord parameter, change it to the correct UV channel
  3. Recompile and check if textures display

Fix — Step 2: Create standalone material (last resort)

If the Interchange parent material (MI_Default_Opaque_DS / M_Default) won't compile or can't be edited:

  1. Create a new base Material (no Interchange dependency)
  2. Add a TextureCoordinate node with the correct UV channel index
  3. Connect it to the UVs input on ALL texture samplers
  4. Wire textures: BaseColor → Base Color, ORM → R=AO / G=Roughness / B=Metallic, Normal → Normal
  5. Set sampler types: BaseColor=Color, ORM=Linear Color, Normal=Normal
  6. Recompile and assign to the mesh

Tip

Only BaseColor/albedo textures should have sRGB enabled. Normal, Roughness, Metallic, AO, and Height maps should always be Linear (sRGB off).

docs.title: "Blueprint Compilation Failed"
docs.text:
Symptoms: Blueprint operations fail to compile.

Solutions:

  1. Check for errors 

    "Check BP_MyActor for compilation errors"

  2. Verify nodes are connected

  3. Execution pins must be connected

  4. Check variable types

  5. Ensure type compatibility

docs.title: Sending us a support bundle
docs.text:
If KARIANA is misbehaving, create a support bundle — a single zip with logs, versions, and system info, automatically scrubbed of secrets.

From inside the editor: open the KARIANA chat and ask it to export a support bundle.

If the editor will not launch: double-click kariana-support.py in the plugin's Content/Python folder (or run python -m support from that folder).

Either way a file like kariana-support-20260525-101500.zip appears on your Desktop. Email the whole zip to hello@kariana.ai (offline clients can copy it to a USB drive). It never contains your license token or API keys; open summary.txt inside the zip to see exactly what is included.

GitHub Issues

docs.title: Authentication Token System
docs.text: Offline-capable license verification for the KARIANA UE plugin. Users authenticate once online via Clerk, receive a signed token cached locally, then work offline for up to 30 days.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Plugin starts → UKarianaAuthToken::LoadAndVerify() reads %LOCALAPPDATA%/KARiANA/.kariana_token
  2. No token → Auth screen shows "Login to Kariana" + "Setup Local Model" pills
  3. Expired token → Auth screen shows "Your subscription seems expired!" + "Login to Kariana"
  4. Invalid/tampered token → Same as no token (auth screen)
  5. Valid token → Welcome screen with quick-action cards (normal plugin use)

docs.title: Login flow
docs.text:
1. User clicks "Login to Kariana" → browser opens https://app.kariana.ai/sign-in
  2. User authenticates via Clerk (Google or Email)
  3. Clerk callback reaches the K9 daemon with user claims (user_id, email, tier)
  4. Daemon calls token_generator.generate_token() → signs payload with HMAC-SHA256
  5. Daemon saves signed token to %LOCALAPPDATA%/KARiANA/.kariana_token
  6. Plugin polls for the token file every 2 seconds → detects it → switches to welcome screen

docs.title: Setup Local Model flow
docs.text:
1. User clicks "Setup Local Model"
  2. If no token exists (never authenticated) → error: "You need internet connection for the first time"
  3. If token exists (even expired) → opens plugin Project Settings + local model docs

docs.title: Token Format
docs.text:
The token is a JSON file with two fields: a payload and an HMAC-SHA256 signature.

{
  "payload": {
    "user_id": "clerk_user_abc123",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "tier": "solo",
    "issued_at": "2026-03-26T12:00:00Z",
    "expires_at": "2026-04-25T12:00:00Z"
  },
  "signature": "91368c674df621aec225949b0adf31875ed68dd12317995b529f81f1d0018a2d"
}

docs.title: Payload fields
docs.text: Field Type Description user_id string Clerk user ID email string User email tier string "free", "solo", "pro", "enterprise" issued_at ISO 8601 When the token was generated expires_at ISO 8601 When the token expires (default: 30 days)

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
• Algorithm: HMAC-SHA256
  • Input: canonical JSON of the payload (compact, sorted keys, no whitespace)
  • Output: lowercase hex string (64 chars)
  • The signing key is shared between the server (Python) and the plugin (C++, obfuscated with XOR)

docs.title: Token file (per-user, runtime)
docs.text: Platform Path Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\KARiANA\.kariana_token macOS ~/Library/Application Support/KARiANA/.kariana_token Linux ~/.config/KARiANA/.kariana_token

docs.title: Source files
docs.text: File Purpose Source/KARIANARuntime/Public/Secure/KarianaAuthToken.h C++ token model, enums, load/verify/save API Source/KARIANARuntime/Private/Secure/KarianaAuthToken.cpp HMAC-SHA256 implementation, file I/O, expiry logic Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaAuthScreen.h/.cpp Auth gate UI widget Content/Python/licensing/token_generator.py Server-side token generation and verification Content/Python/licensing/test_token_generator.py 24 unit tests

docs.title: Subscription Tiers
docs.text:
Defined in EKarianaSubscriptionTier (C++) and cloud/clerk/types.ts:

Tier Clerk Value Description None — No token / invalid Free "free" Free tier (future) Solo "solo" Solo subscription (active for pre-release) Pro "pro" Pro tier (future) Enterprise "enterprise" Enterprise (contact sales)

docs.title: Auth States
docs.text:
Defined in EKarianaAuthState:

State Meaning UI Shown NoToken No .kariana_token file on disk First-time auth pills Valid Token exists, signature valid, not expired Welcome screen / chat Expired Token exists, signature valid, but past expires_at "Subscription expired!" Invalid Token file exists but signature verification failed First-time auth pills

docs.title: Security Notes
docs.text:
• The token is signed, not encrypted — users can read their tier, but cannot change it without invalidating the signature
  • The signing key is obfuscated in the plugin binary (XOR with a mask) — not true encryption, but sufficient to prevent casual tampering
  • Before shipping to production, replace the placeholder signing key in both:
  • KarianaAuthToken.cpp — OBFUSCATED_KEY[] array (XOR each byte of your real key with 0xA7)
  • token_generator.py — _DEFAULT_KEY (or set KARIANA_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY env var on the server)
  • Constant-time comparison is used for signature verification to prevent timing attacks
  • Token expiry is checked against FDateTime::UtcNow() — clock manipulation is a known limitation (acceptable for this use case)

docs.title: CI/CD Infrastructure
docs.text: KARIANA uses self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on the Tato server (komprtx3090) instead of GitHub-hosted runners. This gives the team unlimited CI/CD minutes at no cost.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Runners authenticate via a GitHub App ("INGIPSA Self-Hosted Runners"), not a Personal Access Token. The private key never expires and tokens are auto-generated -- no manual rotation needed.

docs.title: Server Details
docs.text:
• Machine: komprtx3090 on Tailscale (100.91.158.75), user komp2
  • CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5950X (16 cores / 32 threads)
  • RAM: 96 GB
  • GPU: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation (48 GB VRAM)
  • Storage: C: 476 GB, D: 931 GB, E: 3.7 TB (runner data lives on E:)

docs.title: Resource guardrails
docs.text:
The server also runs Unreal Engine projects, LM Studio, NemoClaw, Huly, and 30+ other Docker containers. To prevent CI from interfering with local work:

  • Linux runners are hard-limited by Docker (4 CPUs, 8 GB RAM each)
  • Windows runner is pinned to cores 0-3 with BelowNormal process priority
  • A scheduled task ("GitHubRunnerGuardrails") enforces limits on every boot

docs.title: File layout on server
docs.text: ``` E:\github-runners\ compose\ docker-compose.yml # Linux runner definitions github-app.pem # GitHub App private key start-runners.ps1 # Start script windows-runner # Native Windows runner apply-guardrails.ps1 watch-guardrails.ps1 cache # Windows tool cache windows-work # Windows workspace general # General runner workspace gpu # GPU runner workspace README.md # Full ops runbook ```

docs.title: macOS builds
docs.text:
There is no macOS runner. macOS desktop builds are cross-compiled from the Linux runner using electron-builder --mac. This produces unsigned builds -- macOS users need to:

  1. Download the .dmg
  2. If blocked: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway

This is standard for pre-alpha software. Code signing will be added when a Mac is available as a self-hosted runner.

docs.title: Check runner status
docs.text: ```bash

docs.title: From your machine (via GitHub API)
docs.text: gh api orgs/INGIPSA/actions/runners --jq '.runners[] | {name, status}'

docs.title: On the server
docs.text: docker ps --filter name=github-runner powershell Get-Service 'actions.runner.INGIPSA.tato-windows' ```

docs.title: Restart runners
docs.text: ```bash

docs.title: SSH into server
docs.text: ssh komprtx3090

docs.title: Linux runners
docs.text: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File E:\github-runners\compose\start-runners.ps1

docs.title: Windows runner
docs.text: powershell Restart-Service 'actions.runner.INGIPSA.tato-windows' ```

docs.title: Update Linux runner image
docs.text:
Docker pulls over SSH don't work (Windows Credential Manager issue). Pull from the server desktop:

``` docker pull myoung34/github-runner:latest ```

Then restart via start-runners.ps1.

docs.title: View logs
docs.text: ```bash

docs.title: Linux runners
docs.text:
docker logs github-runner-general docker logs github-runner-gpu

# Windows runner logs at: E:\github-runners\windows-runner_diag\ ```

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
Self-hosted runners persist between jobs, so:

  • Tool cache (actions/setup-node, etc.): Tools are downloaded once and reused. Stored in /opt/hostedtoolcache (Linux) and E:\github-runners\cache (Windows).
  • Workspace: Unlike GitHub-hosted runners, node_modules and build artifacts persist between runs.
  • actions/cache: Still works (stores on GitHub servers) but is less critical since the workspace persists locally.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Runners are restricted to private repos only (allows_public_repositories: false)
  • Public repos cannot trigger jobs on self-hosted runners
  • GitHub App permissions are scoped to runner management only

docs.title: Epic UE 5.8 MCP Plugins vs. KARIANA K9 — Comparison & Backport Plan
docs.text: Author: KARIANA Team Date: 2026-05-03 Status: Internal — do not distribute

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text: Epic shipped two experimental MCP-related plugins in the UE 5.8 dev tree: a server-side plugin (ModelContextProtocol) that exposes engine tools over HTTP/SSE, and a client-side adapter (MCPClientToolset) that lets the editor consume external MCP servers. KARIANA K9 predates both by roughly a year and covers a much wider tool surface (300+ tools vs. Epic's handful of reflection-derived tools), but it uses a lower-level transport (raw TCP socket on port 9877) and lacks several protocol-layer features that Epic has now standardised. The recommended path for UE 5.8 is a thin FToolset interop shim that feeds KARIANA's existing socket dispatcher through Epic's ToolsetRegistry, letting Epic's HTTP MCP server auto-expose all KARIANA tools with zero schema re-authoring. For the 5.7 production line, a targeted set of backports — primarily MCP protocol-version negotiation, SSE progress streaming, and DNS-rebinding protection — will close the most important reliability gaps at low engineering cost.

docs.title: 2. Side-by-Side Architecture Comparison
docs.text: Dimension Epic ModelContextProtocol (5.8) Epic MCPClientToolset (5.8) KARIANA K9 (5.7) Role MCP server (inbound) MCP client adapter (outbound) MCP server + AI backend bridge Transport HTTP via IHttpRouter, port 8000, path /mcp, Streamable HTTP (MCP 2025-03-26+), SSE on POST Legacy SSE (GET /sse + POST /message) or Streamable HTTP (POST / + session id) Raw TCP socket, port 9877; custom line-delimited JSON Tool registration IModelContextProtocolModule::GetChecked().AddTool(MakeShared<FMyTool>()) + FToolset/IModelContextProtocolTool interface Reads tools from remote MCP servers via UMCPClientToolsetSubsystem Python COMMAND_REGISTRY dict + C++ REGISTER_KARIANA_COMMAND() macro; IModelContextProtocolModule not used Schema source Reflection-driven via FModelContextProtocolLibraryTool (UBlueprintFunctionLibrary metadata); USTRUCT cache for cooked platforms Pulled from remote server tools/list response Hand-authored Python dicts in Content/Python/handlers/; no USTRUCT cache Session model Per-client FModelContextProtocolSession; SSE result streaming + progress heartbeats Per-server FMCPClientToolset instance Single shared command queue (command_queue + response_dict); no per-client session isolation Protocol versions Negotiates: 2024-11-05, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25 Same negotiation on client side No version negotiation; clients must assume a fixed undocumented protocol Auth DNS-rebinding Origin guard (server); server settings only None / Bearer Token / OAuth2 (RFC 8414 discovery, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, RFC 7636 PKCE, refresh token rotation) HMAC-SHA256 offline tokens (KarianaAuthToken.h, token_generator.py); no HTTP-layer auth on socket Resources API IModelContextProtocolResourceProvider; resources/list, resources/read Proxies server resources into ToolsetRegistry Not implemented Structured output outputSchema → structuredContent per MCP spec Passes through from server Not implemented Deferred loading list_toolsets / describe_toolset / load_toolset meta-tools; notifications/tools/list_changed N/A (client, loads eagerly) No deferred loading; all 300+ schemas sent in every tools/list response Blueprint / DSL support None — reflection only; no BP graph authoring None BlueprintLisp DSL (KarianaLispParser, KarianaBlueprintLispConverter); 1-call BP graph creation Multi-backend AI routing Not in scope (tool server only) Connects to any MCP server Backend factory: claude / lmstudio / ollama / bedrock Editor event queue Analytics via FEngineAnalytics only None KarianaEventQueue ring buffer (selection_changed, map_opened, blueprint_compiled) Admin UI ModelContextProtocol.GenerateClientConfig console cmd UMCPToolsetSettings (project user settings) Gradio dashboard at localhost:7860; tool-category filtering, model selection, connection test Analytics FEngineAnalytics integration None Usage analytics pipeline (DynamoDB kariana-usage, kariana-quotas, app.kariana.ai/dashboard/analytics) Config surface UModelContextProtocolSettings (bAutoStartServer=false), CLI -ModelContextProtocolPort=N UMCPToolsetSettings (EditorPerProjectUserSettings), FMCPServerConfig[] Edit > Project Settings > KARIANA Assistant; Python admin_dashboard/config.json

docs.title: 3. What We Adopted into KARIANA 5.8
docs.text: The UE 5.8 port introduces a ToolsetRegistry interop layer that bridges KARIANA's socket dispatcher into Epic's plugin ecosystem without replacing it.

docs.title: The FToolset Shim
docs.text:
A new C++ class UKarianaToolsetDefinition (planned path: Source/KARIANAEditor/Public/Toolsets/KarianaToolsetDefinition.h) will subclass UToolsetDefinition and annotate its callable functions with UFUNCTION(meta=(AICallable)). Internally, each UFUNCTION stub forwards the call synchronously to the existing KARIANA socket dispatcher, waits for the response_dict entry, and returns the JSON result as a FString.

Schema generation is handled by Epic's reflection path — the UPARAM(meta=(AIDescription="...")) macro on each function parameter replaces the hand-authored Python dicts in Content/Python/handlers/. This gives KARIANA cooked-platform schema support (Epic's FModelContextProtocolFunctionMetaData USTRUCT cache) for free.

docs.title: Registration Flow
docs.text:
PostEngineInit
  └─ UKarianaToolsetDefinition::RegisterWithSubsystem()
       └─ UToolsetRegistrySubsystem::RegisterToolset(this)
            └─ IModelContextProtocolModule (ModelContextProtocolEditor adapter)
                 └─ auto-exposes all KARIANA tools via HTTP GET /mcp (port 8000)

UToolsetRegistrySubsystem fires notifications/tools/list_changed when KARIANA tools are hot-reloaded (i.e., when handlers/ Python files change and the daemon restarts), keeping connected clients in sync without a full editor restart.

docs.title: What Is Not Replaced
docs.text: The Python socket server (port 9877), the REGISTER_KARIANA_COMMAND C++ registry, the backend factory, and the Gradio admin dashboard all remain unchanged. The FToolset shim is an additional exposure path, not a replacement. Clients that already connect directly to port 9877 (e.g., the kariana-remote Node.js bridge) continue to work without modification.

docs.title: 4. Recommended Backports to the 5.7 Line
docs.text: Items are prioritised by reliability impact relative to engineering effort. Items that can be implemented entirely in Python or in the existing UnrealMCPBridge module are preferred because they ship without a C++ rebuild.

docs.title: P0 — Critical / Ship Before Next Public Release
docs.text: # Epic Feature KARIANA Files to Touch Effort User-Facing Payoff P0-1 DNS-rebinding Origin guard on the HTTP endpoint Content/Python/mcp_server.py (add Host: header check on every request; reject non-localhost / non-127.0.0.1 Origins) S Closes a known lateral-movement attack vector that Epic explicitly addressed; required for any public-facing Claude Desktop config P0-2 MCP protocol-version negotiation (initialize handshake with protocolVersion field) Content/Python/mcp_server.py — parse protocolVersion in initialize handler; respond with highest mutually supported version; return LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant S Claude Desktop 1.x and Cursor enforce version negotiation; without it, connections silently fail after client upgrades P0-3 SSE progress heartbeats during long-running tool calls Content/Python/mcp_server.py — emit event: progress lines with {"progress": N, "total": N} during multi-step handlers (BlueprintLisp compilation, HLOD generation, navmesh rebuild) M Eliminates client-side timeouts on 30+ second operations; Claude Desktop shows a live progress bar

docs.title: P1 — High Value / Next Sprint
docs.text: # Epic Feature KARIANA Files to Touch Effort User-Facing Payoff P1-1 Deferred tool loading (list_toolsets / load_toolset meta-tools) Content/Python/mcp_server.py + Content/Python/backends/tool_selector.py — expose the 30 existing tool categories as lazy toolsets; send only the active-category subset until load_toolset is called M Reduces tools/list payload from ~120 KB to ~4 KB for small-context models (Qwen3-8B, Haiku); directly improves latency and context-window headroom on every query P1-2 notifications/tools/list_changed broadcast Content/Python/mcp_server.py — watch handlers/ directory via watchdog; emit notification on file change S Clients pick up new KARIANA tools without reconnecting; important during active tool development sessions P1-3 Per-client session isolation Content/Python/mcp_server.py — assign a UUID per connection; scope command_queue entries to session ID; prevents response cross-talk when two AI clients connect simultaneously M Unblocks multi-agent workflows (e.g., one agent doing scene layout while another iterates blueprints)

docs.title: P2 — Nice-to-Have / Backlog
docs.text: # Epic Feature KARIANA Files to Touch Effort User-Facing Payoff P2-1 Structured output schemas (outputSchema → structuredContent) Content/Python/handlers/ (all ~200 handler files) — add output_schema key to each COMMAND_REGISTRY entry; update mcp_server.py response serialiser L Enables AI clients to parse tool results reliably without regex; prerequisite for chain-of-tool automation P2-2 Resources API (resources/list, resources/read) Content/Python/mcp_server.py + new Content/Python/handlers/resources_handler.py — expose UAsset paths and Blueprint source as readable resources M AI can inspect existing project assets (textures, meshes, BPs) without a separate query_assets tool call; improves context richness P2-3 ModelContextProtocol.GenerateClientConfig equivalent New console command or Gradio dashboard button — write .mcp.json snippets for Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code pointing at port 9877 S Reduces onboarding time for new team members; currently documented only in prose P2-4 bAutoStartServer settings toggle (Epic style) Source/UnrealMCPBridge/ — add UKarianaMCPSettings::bAutoStartSocketServer mirroring Epic's pattern; respect it in FUnrealMCPBridgeModule::StartupModule S Lets studios disable the socket server in shipping configs without patching source

docs.title: 5. What KARIANA Does Better Than Epic Today
docs.text:
This is not a criticism of Epic's plugins — they are experimental and deliberately minimal. It is an honest statement of where KARIANA provides value that Epic does not.

Tool breadth. Epic's ModelContextProtocol plugin ships with a small set of reflection-derived tools from existing UBlueprintFunctionLibrary callables. KARIANA has 300+ hand-crafted tools across 30 categories including PCG graph authoring, foliage painting, Take Recorder control, physics simulation triggers, camera rail animation, and World Partition streaming — none of which Epic exposes.

BlueprintLisp DSL. Epic has no equivalent. The KARIANA KarianaLispParser + KarianaBlueprintLispConverter pipeline lets an AI create a complete, compiled Blueprint graph — variables, events, branches, function calls — in a single tool call instead of 25+ sequential add_node / connect_pins calls. This is the single largest latency reduction for Blueprint-heavy workflows.

Multi-backend AI routing. Epic's plugin is transport-only; it has no opinion on which AI model executes the tools. KARIANA's backend factory (Content/Python/backends/factory.py) supports Claude Code Bridge, AWS Bedrock (Qwen3/Claude via Lambda), LM Studio (local OpenAI-compatible), and Ollama — all switchable at runtime from Project Settings with no code changes.

Editor Event Queue. Epic's analytics integration is fire-and-forget. KARIANA's KarianaEventQueue is a thread-safe ring buffer that AI agents can poll to learn what the human editor just did (selection_changed, map_opened, blueprint_compiled), enabling reactive AI assistance without the AI needing to re-query the entire scene state.

Skill recording. KARIANA records multi-step editor workflows into replayable skill files (Content/Python/skills/), which can be triggered by name via a single execute_skill tool call. Epic has no equivalent concept.

Gradio admin dashboard. The Content/Python/admin_dashboard/app.py dashboard provides live tool-category filtering, model selection, and connection testing in a browser UI. Epic's config surface is limited to INI settings and console commands.

docs.title: 6. Coexistence in the Beta58 Project
docs.text:
When the UE 5.8 port runs alongside both Epic plugins in a test project, the resulting topology is:

AI Client (Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code)
        │
        │  HTTP POST /mcp  (port 8000)
        ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Epic ModelContextProtocol plugin (port 8000)          │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  ToolsetRegistry                                 │  │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐   │  │
│  │  │  UKarianaToolsetDefinition (5.8 shim)    │   │  │
│  │  │  → KARIANA socket dispatcher (port 9877) │   │  │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘   │  │
│  │  (+ any other FToolset subclasses Epic ships)   │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Epic MCPClientToolset plugin
  → connects outbound to external MCP servers (e.g. filesystem, web search)
  → feeds their tools back into ToolsetRegistry alongside KARIANA tools
  → same single HTTP endpoint at port 8000 surfaces everything

KARIANA Python socket server (port 9877)
  → still accepts direct connections from kariana-remote Node.js bridge
  → still accepts direct connections from Bedrock daemon / LM Studio / Ollama
  → shim and direct path share the same command_queue / response_dict

There is a single MCP endpoint for AI clients (http://localhost:8000/mcp). All 300+ KARIANA tools appear there via the UKarianaToolsetDefinition shim. Any tools that Epic's MCPClientToolset fetches from external servers also appear at that same endpoint. AI clients do not need to know that two separate plugins and a Python daemon are involved.

Port 9877 remains open for non-HTTP consumers (kariana-remote, daemon backends). No port conflict exists because Epic uses 8000 and KARIANA uses 9877 by default.

The ModelContextProtocol.GenerateClientConfig console command will write a single config block pointing at port 8000 that covers everything, replacing the current need to hand-edit .mcp.json entries for port 9877.

docs.title: 7. Open Questions and Risks
docs.text:
# Question / Risk Severity Notes R-1 ToolsetRegistry API stability. Engine/Plugins/Experimental/Toolsets/ is marked Experimental in 5.8; its public API may change between 5.8 drops before GA. The UKarianaToolsetDefinition shim could break silently. Medium Pin to a specific 5.8 changelist for the Beta58 branch; add a static_assert on the IToolsetRegistry vtable size as a build-time canary. R-2 Schema migration cost for P2-1 (structured output schemas). Adding output_schema to all ~200 handler files is mechanical but risky: a malformed schema silently degrades AI tool-use quality. High Do not ship P2-1 without an automated schema validator in CI (scripts/validate_tool_schemas.py). R-3 Session isolation (P1-3) and the response_dict design. The current response_dict keyed by integer counter will need to be re-keyed by (session_id, command_id) tuple. Any handler that directly reads response_dict by integer (there are several in Content/Python/handlers/) will need updating. Medium Audit all direct response_dict accesses before merging P1-3; it is not a one-file change. R-4 DNS-rebinding guard (P0-1) breaks internal CI runners. If a CI runner hits the MCP server from a non-localhost IP (e.g., a sidecar container), the Origin check will reject it. Low Add a KARIANA_MCP_ALLOW_ORIGINS env var override for CI environments; default to strict localhost-only. R-5 OAuth2 in MCPClientToolset (Epic outbound client) is not yet needed by KARIANA. KARIANA does not currently consume external MCP servers. If the team adds web-search or filesystem MCP servers as context sources, OAuth2 config becomes relevant — but Epic's FMCPServerConfig handling it means KARIANA does not need to implement it. Low Track, do not act. R-6 Dual exposure (port 8000 via shim + port 9877 direct) means tool schemas can diverge. If a Python handler description is updated but the UFUNCTION AIDescription annotation is not, the two surfaces describe the same tool differently. Medium Add a CI check that compares tools/list from both surfaces and fails on any description mismatch. R-7 BlueprintLisp DSL has no equivalent path through Epic's reflection-only schema model. The DSL takes a freeform string, not a typed struct. The shim will need to expose it as UPARAM(meta=(AIDescription="Lisp expression string")) with a hand-written description — which is fine, but it means the DSL tools will not benefit from Epic's USTRUCT cache. Low Acceptable trade-off; document it in the shim header.

End of report. For implementation questions, start with Source/KARIANAEditor/ for the 5.8 shim and Content/Python/mcp_server.py for all 5.7 backports.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Default colors → inline FLinearColor globals in KarianaBrandColors.h (69 colors)
  2. On startup → KarianaBrandTheme::ApplyTheme("KARIANA Dark") reads themes.json
  3. Dispatch table → 69-entry map of JSON key strings to pointers to those inline globals
  4. Overwrites → JSON values replace inline globals in-place (same linear-space format)
  5. Fallback → if themes.json missing, hardcoded defaults remain (always works)
  6. Consumption → two patterns: direct KarianaBrand::XYZ reads, or FKarianaMarkdownStyle::Get() brushes

docs.title: 9.1 Connection States
docs.text:
• Status dot in header: green (StatusConnected), yellow (StatusWarning), red (StatusError)
  • Status overlay icon (orphaned — SKarianaStatusOverlay is never instantiated): gray (TextTertiary=disabled), pink (Pink=processing), green (StatusConnected=ready)

docs.title: 9.2 Processing States
docs.text:
• bIsProcessing flag in ChatInput, ContextBar, StatusOverlay
  • Input: disabled text field, stop icon replaces send icon
  • Context bar: spinner visible, "Processing..." text
  • Steps widget: thinking bubble visible, streaming preview active

Note: bIsProcessing is duplicated across three separate widgets (SKarianaChatInput, SKarianaContextBar, SKarianaStatusOverlay). All three are push-updated by the panel via SetProcessing() from OnStreamingStateChanged. There is no single authoritative processing flag — the panel fans out to each child manually.

docs.title: 9.3 Mode System
docs.text:
• 3 modes: Validate (Plan), Teach, Create (BypassPermissions)
  • Active pill: white bg (BgModeActive), bold black text (TextInverse)
  • Inactive pill: transparent, regular dim text (TextTertiary)
  • Mode accent colors only used for text emphasis in mode selector, not widespread

docs.title: 9.4 Font Scaling
docs.text:
• SDPIScaler wraps entire panel, controlled by FontScale member
  • CTRL+scroll adjusts 1.0-2.0 range, applied per-frame via lambda
  • MarkdownRenderer also has SetFontScale() for its own SDPIScaler

docs.title: 9.5 Streaming
docs.text:
• SKarianaChatMessage::UpdateContent() feeds new text to markdown renderer
  • SKarianaMarkdownRenderer::SetContent(text, isStreaming=true) does incremental render
  • SKarianaStepsWidget shows streaming preview (120 char, word-boundary truncation)
  • Authoritative streaming state lives in FKarianaChatSession::IsStreaming(), broadcast via OnStreamingStateChanged

docs.title: 9.6 Undo/Redo
docs.text:
• Dual stacks: ConversationUndoHistory, ConversationRedoBuffer
  • Conversation-level undo (not individual edits)
  • Separate from UE editor transaction history

docs.title: 9.7 Settings-Gated UI
docs.text:
• Processing log: UKarianaAssistantSettings::bShowProcessingLog
  • Status overlay: UKarianaAssistantSettings::bShowStatusOverlay

                    │ UKarianaAssistant │

                    │ FKarianaChat     │
                    │   Session        │
                    └────────┬─────────┘

                    ┌────────▼─────────┐
                    │ SKarianaChat     │
                    │   Panel (HUB)    │
                    └──┬──┬──┬──┬──┬───┘
          direct calls │  │  │  │  │ direct calls
        ┌──────────────┘  │  │  │  └──────────────┐

docs.title: P1: CRITICAL — SKarianaContextBar Has No Brand Colors
docs.text: File: SKarianaContextBar.cpp Issue: All 3 text labels use hardcoded FLinearColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.2). Does not include KarianaBrandColors.h. Completely bypasses the theme system. Impact: Theme changes have zero effect on the status bar. Fix: Import brand colors, replace with KarianaBrand::TextTertiary or new dedicated color.

docs.title: P2: CRITICAL — 8 Hardcoded Icon Opacity Values
docs.text: Files: SKarianaChatPanel.cpp (5 instances), SKarianaContextBar.cpp (3 instances) Issue: FLinearColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.2) repeated 8 times for icon dimming. Impact: Cannot change icon brightness via theme. Redundant code. Fix: Add KarianaBrand::IconDimmed to the brand namespace and dispatch table.

docs.title: P3: HIGH — Dual Source of Truth (C++ + JSON)
docs.text: Files: KarianaBrandColors.h + themes.json Issue: Same 69 colors defined in both files. Must update both when changing colors. Impact: Forgetting one leads to inconsistency. JSON override masks C++ changes silently. Fix: Designate one as canonical source with the other as override/fallback.

docs.title: P4: HIGH — FKarianaMarkdownStyle Name Is Misleading
docs.text: File: KarianaMarkdownStyle.cpp/.h Issue: Contains ALL chat UI brushes (surfaces, bubbles, pills, inputs, avatars, badges) — not just markdown. Name suggests markdown-only scope. Impact: Developers look for "chat style" or "UI style" and can't find it. New brushes get added to wrong places. Fix: Rename to FKarianaUIStyle or FKarianaChatStyle.

docs.title: P5: HIGH — No Semantic Token Layer
docs.text: Issue: Colors named by appearance (Pink, BgRaised) not by role (AccentPrimary, SurfaceCard). Changing brand accent from pink requires auditing every Pink usage. Impact: Theme customization is brittle. Can't answer "what color is the primary action?" without reading code. Fix: Add KarianaToken namespace with role-based references to brand colors.

docs.title: P6: MEDIUM — Welcome Screen Card Uses Hardcoded Color
docs.text: File: SKarianaWelcomeScreen.cpp:63 Issue: Card brush uses FLinearColor(0.027, 0.027, 0.030) instead of KarianaBrand::BgPrompt (0.065, 0.065, 0.070). Different values. Impact: Welcome cards don't update with theme changes. Color doesn't match the defined BgPrompt. Fix: Use KarianaBrand::BgPrompt or define a new CardBg if the different shade is intentional.

docs.title: P7: MEDIUM — Drop Target Uses Non-Theme Blue
docs.text: File: SKarianaDropTarget.cpp:180 Issue: FLinearColor(0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 0.5) — arbitrary blue that contradicts the dark neutral theme. Impact: Drag-drop highlight looks out of place, can't be themed. Fix: Add KarianaBrand::DropHighlight with a theme-appropriate color (pink accent or neutral).

docs.title: P8: MEDIUM — Input Border Color Hardcoded in StyleSet
docs.text: File: KarianaMarkdownStyle.cpp:304 Issue: FLinearColor(0.851, 0.851, 0.851, 0.09) for input border bypass brand system. Impact: Can't theme the input border. Fix: Add KarianaBrand::InputBorderColor.

docs.title: P9: MEDIUM — Duplicate Header File
docs.text: Files: Private/Widgets/KarianaMarkdownStyle.h AND Public/Widgets/KarianaMarkdownStyle.h Issue: Two copies of the class declaration with slightly different contents. The .cpp includes the Private one. Impact: Public copy is stale. Confusion about which to include. Fix: Delete Public/Widgets/KarianaMarkdownStyle.h.

docs.title: P10: MEDIUM — themes.json in Wrong Location
docs.text: File: installers/gradio-app/themes.json Issue: Theme data buried in installer directory. Path resolved via ResolvePluginRoot() + hardcoded relative path. Impact: Fragile path, semantically wrong location (themes != installers). Fix: Move to Content/Config/themes.json or Config/themes.json.

docs.title: P11: MEDIUM — Linear-Space vs sRGB Confusion in Comments
docs.text: File: KarianaBrandColors.h Issue: Hex comments (e.g., // #1a1a1a) reference sRGB values, but FLinearColor stores linear-space. The hex doesn't match what renders on screen. Impact: Confusion when translating Figma designs (Figma uses sRGB hex). Example: BgBase = (0.040, 0.040, 0.040) renders as ~#363636, not #1A1A1A as commented. Fix: Fix comments to show correct sRGB equivalents, or note gamma conversion.

docs.title: P12: LOW — BgInput Same as BgBase
docs.text: Issue: BgInput(0.040, 0.040, 0.040) is identical to BgBase(0.040, 0.040, 0.040). Impact: Redundant color. No visual distinction between input and base. Fix: Either differentiate (slightly lighter for inputs) or remove the duplicate.

docs.title: P13: LOW — Bunting Color Appears Unused
docs.text: Issue: KarianaBrand::Bunting(0.046, 0.038, 0.190) defined but no widget references it. Impact: Dead code in color namespace. Fix: Remove or document intended future use.

docs.title: P14: LOW — History Panel Uses Constructor Transparent
docs.text: File: SKarianaHistoryPanel.cpp:196 Issue: FLinearColor(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0) instead of FLinearColor::Transparent. Impact: Minor code quality. Same visual result. Fix: Use FLinearColor::Transparent.

docs.title: P15: LOW — Mixed Runtime Theme Update Support
docs.text: Issue: Direct KarianaBrand:: reads are baked at widget construction time. StyleSet brushes are baked at style init time. Neither updates live when theme changes. Reinitialize() requires closing the chat tab. Impact: Theme switching requires full panel teardown and rebuild. Fix: Consider using TAttribute<FSlateColor> bindings for direct reads, or accept the teardown cost.

docs.title: P16: HIGH — bIsProcessing Duplicated Across 3 Widgets
docs.text: Files: SKarianaChatInput.h, SKarianaContextBar.h, SKarianaStatusOverlay.h Issue: Three separate bIsProcessing flags, all push-updated by the panel via SetProcessing(). No single authoritative source — the panel fans out from OnStreamingStateChanged manually. Impact: Easy to miss a widget when adding new processing-dependent behavior. State can drift if a call is missed. Fix: Introduce a shared observable state (e.g., FKarianaUIState struct with OnChanged delegate) that widgets subscribe to, instead of panel pushing to each child.

docs.title: P17: HIGH — ~195 Hardcoded Layout Magic Numbers
docs.text: Files: All 17 widget .cpp files (worst: SKarianaChatPanel.cpp 41, SKarianaUserInputPrompt.cpp 22, SKarianaStepsWidget.cpp 20) Issue: Spacing, sizing, font sizes, radii, and padding are literal numbers scattered across the codebase. No central layout constants. Impact: Changing "toolbar height" means finding the right HeightOverride(32) among 25+ similar calls. AI cannot reliably determine which FMargin(8,4) corresponds to which element. Fix: Create KarianaLayoutConstants.h with named constants (e.g., ToolbarHeight = 32, MessagePadding = FMargin(12,4), IconSizeSmall = FVector2D(16,16)).

docs.title: P18: MEDIUM — FOnHistoryPanelClosed Delegate Declared But Never Wired
docs.text: File: SKarianaHistoryPanel.h Issue: The FOnHistoryPanelClosed delegate is declared but never bound at the construction site in SKarianaChatPanel.cpp. Impact: Dead delegate. If history panel close behavior is needed, the infrastructure appears present but is non-functional. Fix: Either wire it or remove the declaration.

docs.title: P19: MEDIUM — Hub Overload in SKarianaChatPanel
docs.text: File: SKarianaChatPanel.cpp Issue: The panel is the sole hub for ~14 inbound delegates and ~10 outbound direct-call targets. It handles session management, undo/redo, message rendering, streaming, mode switching, history, attachments, and plan approval — all in one class. Impact: The file is large and difficult to navigate. Adding any new feature requires modifying this single bottleneck file. Fix: Consider extracting sub-controllers (e.g., FKarianaMessageController, FKarianaSessionController) that the panel delegates to, keeping the panel as a thin wiring layer.

docs.title: Change a color value
docs.text:
1. Edit KarianaBrandColors.h — change the inline FLinearColor default
  2. Edit themes.json — change the matching [R, G, B] array
  3. Rebuild in Rider
  4. If the color is used in a KarianaMarkdownStyle brush, close and reopen the chat panel

docs.title: Add a new color
docs.text:
1. Add inline FLinearColor NewColor(R, G, B); to KarianaBrandColors.h
  2. Add Table.Add(TEXT("NewColor"), &KarianaBrand::NewColor); to dispatch table in KarianaBrandTheme.cpp
  3. Add "NewColor": [R, G, B] to themes.json
  4. Use in widgets: KarianaBrand::NewColor or create a brush in KarianaMarkdownStyle.cpp

docs.title: Add an icon
docs.text:
1. Place PNG at Content/Slate/Icons/YourIcon.png
  2. Add to KarianaMarkdownStyle.cpp Create(): 
    Style->Set("Kariana.Icon.YourIcon", new FSlateImageBrush(
    FPaths::Combine(IconsDir, TEXT("YourIcon.png")), FVector2D(W, H)));
  3. Use in widget: FKarianaMarkdownStyle::Get().GetBrush("Kariana.Icon.YourIcon")

The C++ reflection toolset port from UE 5.8's ToolsetRegistry is fully working in UE 5.7. The demo UKarianaBlueprintToolset.CreateBlueprint and .CompileBlueprint are reachable over port 9877 from any MCP client; a real UBlueprint asset gets authored end-to-end through the reflection layer with zero hand-written schema. Time path of a successful KarianaBlueprintToolset.CreateBlueprint call:

  1. MCP client sends {"type":"KarianaBlueprintToolset.CreateBlueprint","params":{...}} to 127.0.0.1:9877
  2. Content/Python/unreal_socket_server.py:_try_cpp_registry (extended in §3 below) sees the . in the type, asks unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.KarianaToolsetSubsystem) whether the toolset exists, and if so calls subsys.execute_tool_blocking(...)
  3. C++ UKarianaToolsetSubsystem::ExecuteToolBlocking waits on the future from ExecuteTool, which delegates to Kariana::Reflection::FFunctionLibraryToolset::ExecuteToolInternal
  4. That looks up the FObjectFunctionToolCall, packs JSON params into the function's frame memory via KarianaToolsetJson::JsonDataToStruct, sets up an FFrame, and calls UFunction::Invoke
  5. UKarianaBlueprintToolset::CreateBlueprint runs as ordinary editor C++, creates the package, calls FKismetEditorUtilities::CreateBlueprint(ParentClass, Package, Name, BPTYPE_Normal, UBlueprint::StaticClass(), UBlueprintGeneratedClass::StaticClass())
  6. Return value is read out of the frame memory via KarianaToolsetJson::PropertyToJsonData, wrapped in {"returnValue": ...}, and shipped back through the same chain in reverse

docs.title: 2. What did NOT initially work — and how it was fixed
2.1 Symptom
docs.text:
$ python scripts/_probe_kariana_reflection_toolset.py
[1/3] tools/list ...
     payload: 57 bytes
     0 tools surfaced
     FAIL — no KarianaBlueprintToolset.* tools found
     names seen: []

Direct socket inspection:

>>> # send {"command": "tools/list"} on port 9877
>>> response
{"success": false, "error": "Unknown command type: None"}

docs.title: 2.2 Root cause
docs.text:
There are two socket servers in this codebase, listening on different ports:

Listener Implemented in Port Used by C++ FMCPSocketServer Source/UnrealMCPBridge/Private/MCPSocketServer.cpp:17 (Port(9000)) 9000 Currently nothing routes here; appears to be dormant Python unreal_socket_server.py Content/Python/unreal_socket_server.py 9877 All MCP clients (Claude Code, kariana-remote, Bedrock daemon, etc.)

When I wired the reflection bridge into FPythonBridge::PreDispatchHook, I assumed FPythonBridge::ExecuteCommand was the entry point for port-9877 traffic. It is not. The Python socket server reads requests directly and dispatches via its own _try_cpp_registry path (unreal_socket_server.py:503), which calls unreal.KarianaCommandRegistryBPLib.has_command(...) — a separate C++ registry from our reflection toolsets.

Additionally:

  • The Python socket server reads command["type"], not command["command"]. The _probe_kariana_reflection_toolset.py probe used command and got "Unknown command type: None".
  • No code path on port 9877 ever calls FPythonBridge::ExecuteCommand for ordinary tool dispatch.

docs.title: 2.3 What the data shows
docs.text: Metric Value Interpretation tools/list payload as computed by C++ subsystem 1,656 bytes, 2 tools Full reflection schema is correctly generated server-side tools/list payload over port-9877 wire 57 bytes Python returns an "unknown command type" error; never sees our hook LogKarianaToolsetBridge: KarianaToolsetBridge ready Present Module + hook installed correctly Pre-dispatch hook called during probe No (would log otherwise) Hook is in the wrong code path

docs.title: 3. The gap is small — closing path
docs.text: Two changes, both ~10 lines:

docs.title: 3.1 Expose UKarianaToolsetSubsystem to Python via UFUNCTION
docs.text:
Source/KarianaToolsetBridge/Public/Reflection/KarianaToolsetSubsystem.h — add UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable) to two methods:

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Kariana|Reflection")
FString GetToolsListJson() const;

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Kariana|Reflection")
FString ExecuteToolBlocking(const FString& QualifiedToolName, const FString& JsonInput);

ExecuteToolBlocking is a thin sync wrapper around the existing ExecuteTool(...) future — Python doesn't need futures.

docs.title: 3.2 Extend Python dispatcher
docs.text:
Content/Python/unreal_socket_server.py:503 — the existing _try_cpp_registry already probes unreal.KarianaCommandRegistryBPLib. Add a second probe for the reflection toolset:

def _try_cpp_registry(self, command_type, command):
    # Existing path: KarianaCommandRegistryBPLib...
    if unreal.KarianaCommandRegistryBPLib.has_command(command_type):
        ...
        return cpp_result

    # NEW: reflection toolset probe (matches "<Toolset>.<tool>")
    if "." in command_type:
        subsys = unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.KarianaToolsetSubsystem)
        if subsys:
            params_json = json.dumps(command.get("params", {}))
            result_json = subsys.execute_tool_blocking(command_type, params_json)
            if result_json:
                return json.loads(result_json)
    return None

docs.title: 3.3 Update _probe_kariana_reflection_toolset.py
docs.text:
Send {"type": tool_name, ...} instead of {"command": ..., ...}. Already mismatched today regardless of the bridge.

Total estimate: ~30 min of work + one rebuild + one editor restart.

docs.title: 7. Recommendation
docs.text:
Port complete. The §3 Python integration landed and the smoke probe passes all three checks (see §1.4 for the live trace). Next decisions:

  1. Which existing tools to migrate first. Strongest candidates: blueprint authoring (create_blueprint, add_node_to_blueprint, connect_blueprint_nodes, compile_blueprint), UMG widget creation, PCG graph editing — anywhere the hand-authored Python schema dict is large or where return shapes are USTRUCTs.
  2. Whether to broaden UKarianaBlueprintToolset. The current demo exposes only CreateBlueprint + CompileBlueprint. Adding AddNode, ConnectPins, AddVariable would put the schema-quality benefit in front of the same workflows BlueprintLisp targets.
  3. Async return support. Currently dropped from the v1 port (sync only). Add when an async tool actually needs it; the rewiring is local to KarianaObjectFunctionToolCall::Execute and UKarianaToolsetSubsystem::ExecuteToolBlocking.
  4. Deprecate the dead FPythonBridge::PreDispatchHook. It's installed but never fires — port 9877 traffic doesn't pass through C++ ExecuteCommand. Either repurpose it for the C++ FMCPSocketServer (port 9000) when that listener is brought back, or remove it. Low priority.

Time spent on this work: roughly one focused session including the planning, comparison report, port plan, vendoring + KARIANA-original substitutes for the 5.7 gaps, fixing two real bugs (load-order, fast-path inversion) caught only at runtime, and the Python integration. The 5.7-vs-5.8 API delta findings are saved as project memory for the next time someone backports an experimental Epic plugin.

docs.title: Reflection-Driven Toolset Port — UE 5.8 → KARIANA on UE 5.7
docs.text:
Status: Phases 1–3 complete; build green against UE 5.7 on 2026-05-10. Live editor smoke test pending (user-initiated). Goal: Bring Epic's reflection-driven AI toolset infrastructure (the engine that powers UToolsetDefinition + UFUNCTION(meta=(AICallable))) into KARIANA on UE 5.7, so future MCP tools can be authored as plain C++ static functions instead of hand-written Python schema dicts.

This plan supersedes the v0.1 dispatch shim in Source/KarianaToolsetBridge/ and the speculative design in toolset-registry-interop-design.md. The earlier comparison report (epic-mcp-comparison.md) remains accurate as background.

docs.title: 1. Why this is the right backport
docs.text:
The 5.8 Toolsets/ plugins (UMGToolSet, GASToolsets, PCGToolset, etc.) all share a single pattern:

UCLASS(BlueprintType)
class UUMGToolSet : public UToolsetDefinition
{
    GENERATED_BODY()
public:
    UFUNCTION(meta = (AICallable), Category = "UMG|Creation")
    static UWidgetBlueprint* CreateWidgetBlueprint(
        const FString& FolderPath,
        const FString& AssetName,
        TSubclassOf<UUserWidget> ParentClass,
        TSubclassOf<UWidget> RootWidgetClass = nullptr);
    // ...
};

That's it. No JSON schema authored by hand. FFunctionLibraryToolset reflects over the UClass at registration time, generates the MCP tools/list schema from FProperty metadata, and dispatches tools/call through FFrame/UFunction::Invoke. Every body is plain editor C++ (FKismetEditorUtilities::CreateBlueprint, UWidgetBlueprint, etc.) that already exists in 5.7.

KARIANA today has 200+ Python handler files where each tool has a hand-written schema dict. Porting the reflection layer lets us migrate hot tools (especially blueprint authoring, where schemas are large and fiddly) to C++ at our own pace.

Renamed namespace: UE::ToolsetRegistry → Kariana::Reflection (avoids future symbol collision when 5.8 lands and we can swap to Epic's official version).
