docs.title: 3. Subsystem & socket integration
docs.text:
5.8 ships a UToolsetRegistrySubsystem (UEditorSubsystem) that holds an FToolsetRegistry instance and exposes a TValueOrError<TObjectPtr<UToolsetRegistrySubsystem>, FString> Get() accessor. We mirror this:

UCLASS()
class UKarianaToolsetSubsystem : public UEditorSubsystem
{
    Kariana::Reflection::FToolsetRegistry ToolsetRegistry;
public:
    static UKarianaToolsetSubsystem* Get();
};

FUnrealMCPBridge (Source/UnrealMCPBridge/Private/) is KARIANA's TCP socket server on port 9877. Today it dispatches to Python handlers. We add a thin C++ pre-dispatch step:

On incoming command:
  1. If type == "tools/list":
       merge subsystem->ToolsetRegistry.GetToolsetJsonSchemas()
       with python_tool_schemas() → respond
  2. If type == "tools/call" and name starts with a registered toolset prefix:
       dispatch to subsystem->ToolsetRegistry.ExecuteTool()
       → return future result
  3. Else: existing Python dispatch path (unchanged)

Backwards-compatible: Python clients see a richer tools/list and can call C++ tools by name, but every existing tool keeps working.

docs.title: 4. Demo: UKarianaBlueprintToolset
docs.text:
Phase-3 deliverable. A single UCLASS exposing 3–4 functions that today require multiple Python tool calls:

UCLASS()
class UKarianaBlueprintToolset : public UKarianaToolsetDefinition
{
    GENERATED_BODY()
public:
    UFUNCTION(meta = (AICallable, AIDescription="Create a new Blueprint asset and return the asset path."))
    static FSoftObjectPath CreateBlueprint(
        const FString& FolderPath,
        const FString& AssetName,
        TSubclassOf<UObject> ParentClass);

    UFUNCTION(meta = (AICallable))
    static bool CompileBlueprint(UBlueprint* Blueprint);

    UFUNCTION(meta = (AICallable))
    static bool AddVariableToBlueprint(UBlueprint* Blueprint, FName VarName, FEdGraphPinType PinType);
};

Implementation reuses FKismetEditorUtilities::CreateBlueprint exactly as 5.8's UMG toolset does (verified at E:\ue5.8-dev\...\UMGToolSet.cpp:194). Existing KARIANA Python create_blueprint handler stays in place; this is an additional, faster, schema-better path.

docs.title: 5. Risks tracked
docs.text: ID Risk Mitigation P-1 UE 5.7 lacks some TStrongObjectPtr / TWeakObjectPtr::Pin() ergonomics used by FFunctionLibraryToolset. Verified TWeakObjectPtr::Pin() exists in 5.7 since 5.0. If a specific overload is missing, replace with TWeakObjectPtr::Get() + nullptr check. P-2 meta=(AICallable) is a project-defined metadata key. UHT in 5.7 may emit a warning about unknown meta. Add it to Build.cs MetaDataKeysAllowed or live with the warning — it's non-fatal. P-3 UFunction::Invoke script execution requires a CDO instance for static functions. 5.8 uses GetMutableDefault<UToolsetDefinition>() — port verbatim. P-4 Output USTRUCTs serialize via the registered FToolsetJsonConverter chain — we're skipping converters in Phase 1. Phase 1 exposes only primitive returns + FString/FName. UStruct returns flagged for Phase 4. P-5 KARIANA ships closed-source; vendoring Epic's MIT-licensed engine sources is fine but each file needs the Epic copyright preserved. Keep // Copyright Epic Games, Inc. All Rights Reserved. header on every vendored file. Add a NOTICES line in KARIANA.uplugin.

docs.title: 6. Timeline (delivered)
docs.text:
• Session 1 (2026-05-09 / 2026-05-10): Phases 1, 2, 3 + compile all delivered in one push.
  • Phase 1 foundation (8 files): Toolset, ToolsetDefinition, JsonSchema, JsonConversion, JsonValueOrError, ValueOrErrorFuture, PropertyAccessors, DelegateHandle.
  • Phase 2 reflection dispatcher (4 files): ToolsetJson (KARIANA-original schema generator + FJsonObjectConverter delegating data converter), ObjectFunctionToolCall (sync-only), FunctionLibraryToolset, ToolCallExceptionHandler (5.7-adapted).
  • Phase 3 demo + socket wire-in: UKarianaToolsetSubsystem, UKarianaBlueprintToolset, FPythonBridge::PreDispatchHook.
  • 5.7 build: green.
  • Pending user action:
  • Run scripts/_probe_kariana_reflection_toolset.py against a running editor to confirm round-trip.
  • Decide on async-result support (currently dropped) and whether to port more 5.8 example toolsets (UMG, GAS, Niagara, PCG).

docs.title: 6a. Substitutions made for 5.7 compatibility
docs.text: 5.8 facility KARIANA replacement Reason JsonUtilitiesEditor module + FJsonSchemaGenerator (1,492 LOC engine code) KarianaToolsetJson.{h,cpp} (~400 LOC, KARIANA-original) Whole subsystem is 5.8-only. We hand-rolled enough reflection-to-JSON-Schema for common UFUNCTION shapes. FScopedScriptExceptionHandler (thread-local script error handler) Global FBlueprintCoreDelegates::OnScriptException only 5.7 only ships the global multicast. Functional regression: errors raised on non-game-thread tools won't be captured (acceptable — tools run on game thread). UKismetSystemLibrary::RaiseScriptError (declared but not exported in 5.7) Kariana::Reflection::RaiseToolScriptError 5.7 omits ENGINE_API decorator on the engine version, so the symbol can't be linked from another module. We replicate the function locally using FBlueprintCoreDelegates::ThrowScriptException directly. UToolCallAsyncResult + FutureHandler async return path Dropped from v1 — all returns are sync Simplification. KARIANA tools are sync today. Re-add when an async tool lands. Custom FToolsetJsonConverter chain for type-overrides (FToolsetReference, etc.) Not yet ported Phase 4 if needed. The current schema treats UObject* / UClass* as path strings.

docs.title: Stripe Licensing Setup Guide
docs.text: This document covers the one-time Stripe configuration needed to power KARIANA's licensing system.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
User → kariana.ai/pricing → Stripe Checkout → Webhook → Lambda → DynamoDB
                                                         ↓
                                                   API Key + Email → User
                                                         ↓
UE Plugin → POST /v1/validate (Bearer sk_live_xxx) → Lambda → DynamoDB lookup
                                                         ↓
                                                   { valid, plan, seats, entitlements }

docs.title: 1. Create Products
docs.text:
In the Stripe Dashboard, create these products:

Product Metadata kariana_plan Monthly Price Yearly Price KARIANA Solo solo $159/seat/mo $1,590/seat/yr KARIANA Pro pro Custom Custom KARIANA Enterprise enterprise Custom Custom

Important: Set the kariana_plan metadata key on each product — the webhook reads this to determine the license tier.

Each price should use per-seat (metered) pricing with usage_type: licensed.

docs.title: 2. Create Entitlement Features
docs.text:
Using the Stripe CLI or API:

# Core features
stripe entitlements features create --name="AI Assistant Access" --lookup-key=ai_assistant
stripe entitlements features create --name="Blueprint Lisp DSL" --lookup-key=blueprint_lisp
stripe entitlements features create --name="Team Management" --lookup-key=team_management
stripe entitlements features create --name="NDA Mode" --lookup-key=nda_mode
stripe entitlements features create --name="Priority Support" --lookup-key=priority_support

Then attach features to products:

# Solo gets ai_assistant + blueprint_lisp
stripe products create_feature prod_SOLO --entitlement-feature=feat_ai_assistant
stripe products create_feature prod_SOLO --entitlement-feature=feat_blueprint_lisp

# Pro gets all Solo features + team_management + nda_mode
stripe products create_feature prod_PRO --entitlement-feature=feat_ai_assistant
stripe products create_feature prod_PRO --entitlement-feature=feat_blueprint_lisp
stripe products create_feature prod_PRO --entitlement-feature=feat_team_management
stripe products create_feature prod_PRO --entitlement-feature=feat_nda_mode

# Enterprise gets everything
stripe products create_feature prod_ENTERPRISE --entitlement-feature=feat_ai_assistant
stripe products create_feature prod_ENTERPRISE --entitlement-feature=feat_blueprint_lisp
stripe products create_feature prod_ENTERPRISE --entitlement-feature=feat_team_management
stripe products create_feature prod_ENTERPRISE --entitlement-feature=feat_nda_mode
stripe products create_feature prod_ENTERPRISE --entitlement-feature=feat_priority_support

Note: lookup_key cannot be changed after creation. Plan feature assignments carefully.

docs.title: 3. Configure Customer Portal
docs.text:
In Stripe Dashboard > Settings > Billing > Customer Portal:

  • Subscription updates: Enable, allow price and quantity changes
  • Proration behavior: Create prorations (charge immediately on upgrade)
  • Products: Add Solo, Pro, Enterprise with their monthly/yearly prices
  • Quantity limits: Set min=1, max=100 seats
  • Subscription cancellation: Enable, set to cancel at period end
  • Invoice history: Enable

docs.title: 4. Set Up Webhook
docs.text:
In Stripe Dashboard > Developers > Webhooks:

Endpoint URL: https://api.kariana.ai/v1/webhooks/stripe (This is the API Gateway URL from terraform output webhook_url)

Events to listen for: - checkout.session.completed - customer.subscription.created - customer.subscription.updated - customer.subscription.deleted - invoice.paid - invoice.payment_failed - entitlements.active_entitlement_summary.updated

Copy the webhook signing secret (whsec_...) for the Terraform deployment.

docs.title: 5. Deploy Infrastructure
docs.text:
cd infrastructure/licensing

# Install dependencies and build
npm install
npm run package

# Deploy with Terraform
cd terraform
terraform init
terraform apply \
  -var="stripe_secret_key=sk_live_..." \
  -var="stripe_webhook_secret=whsec_..." \
  -var="resend_api_key=re_..." \

docs.title: Security Notes
docs.text:
• API keys are stored as SHA-256 hashes in DynamoDB — raw keys are never persisted server-side
  • The raw key is shown to the user exactly once (in the welcome email)
  • Webhook signature verification prevents spoofed events
  • API Gateway uses HTTPS only
  • DynamoDB has point-in-time recovery enabled
  • The UE plugin stores the API key in Config/DefaultEditor.ini (plaintext) — ensure this file is in .gitignore

docs.title: Coexistence with Clerk Auth
docs.text:
The Stripe API key flow coexists with the existing Clerk OAuth flow:

  • Clerk auth: User signs in via browser → daemon generates signed token → offline for 30 days
  • Stripe API key: User pastes key in Project Settings → plugin validates via HTTP → caches as offline token

Both flows produce the same local .kariana_token file for offline use. The Stripe flow is preferred for new users; Clerk remains for backward compatibility.

docs.title: Swap Manifest v1
docs.text:
The KARIANA editor writes a swap manifest to <LocalAppData>/KARiANA/swap-manifest.json immediately before exiting for an auto-update. The bootstrapper (tools/update-bootstrapper/) reads this file as its single source of truth — no command-line state, no environment lookups beyond what the JSON tells it.

Both sides MUST stay in sync. C++ writer: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Updates/KarianaSwapManifest.cpp. Rust reader: tools/update-bootstrapper/src/manifest.rs.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
{
  "schema": 1,
  "editor_pid": 12345,
  "plugin_dir": "C:/Users/aristide/MyProject/Plugins/KARIANA",
  "staged_zip": "C:/Users/aristide/AppData/Local/KARiANA/pending-update/0.10.4.zip",
  "expected_sha256": "abc123...",
  "rename_suffix": ".old-20260430-153012",
  "relaunch": {
    "enabled": true,
    "executable": "C:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.7/Engine/Binaries/Win64/UnrealEditor.exe",
    "args": ["C:/Users/aristide/MyProject/MyProject.uproject"],
    "working_dir": "C:/Users/aristide/MyProject"
  },
  "log_path": "C:/Users/aristide/AppData/Local/KARiANA/bootstrapper.log",
  "rollback_marker": "C:/Users/aristide/AppData/Local/KARiANA/last-good-version.txt",
  "from_version": "0.10.3",
  "to_version": "0.10.4"
}
Field Required Meaning schema yes Always 1 for this version. Bootstrapper refuses unknown schemas. editor_pid yes Editor process ID. Must be > 0 (zero on POSIX matches the whole process group, would silently turn into a guaranteed 30 s timeout). Bootstrapper waits up to 30 s for it to exit before swapping. plugin_dir yes Absolute path to the existing Plugins/KARIANA dir to be replaced. Must be a real directory (not a symlink — refused). staged_zip yes Absolute path to the verified update zip. Compression methods supported: deflate, bzip2, zstd. expected_sha256 yes Exactly 64 lowercase hex characters — SHA-256 of staged_zip. Bootstrapper re-verifies before doing anything destructive. rename_suffix yes Suffix appended to old plugin dir. Must start with .old- (both writer and reader enforce this; the prefix is what the plugin's next-launch sweep matches). relaunch.enabled yes If true, bootstrapper spawns executable after a successful swap. relaunch.executable conditional Required when relaunch.enabled is true. Absolute path. relaunch.args conditional Argument list (excluding executable). relaunch.working_dir optional If empty, the spawned process inherits the bootstrapper's CWD. log_path yes Bootstrapper appends progress to this file. Always written even on success. rollback_marker yes On success, bootstrapper writes to_version here. Plugin's next-launch sweep reads this to know the swap completed cleanly. from_version informational For logs only. to_version informational For logs and rollback_marker content.

docs.title: Failure codes
docs.text:
The bootstrapper exits non-zero on any failure. Each variant of SwapError corresponds to one of these conditions:

Variant When it fires State after Manifest(...) Manifest file unreadable, malformed JSON, schema != 1, any field validation rejection (zero pid, malformed sha, non-absolute path, ...). Pre-destructive. No rename has happened. Plugin dir intact. EditorDidNotExit editor_pid was still alive after 30 s. Pre-destructive. StagedZipMissing staged_zip no longer exists when the bootstrapper goes to read it. Pre-destructive. ShaMismatch Re-computed SHA-256 of staged_zip doesn't match expected_sha256. Pre-destructive. ZipSlip Any zip entry has an absolute path, .. segment, drive-letter prefix, or symlink mode. Pre-destructive. PluginDirMissing plugin_dir does not exist (orchestrator should never produce this — defensive). Pre-destructive. PluginDirIsSymlink plugin_dir is a symlink (developer setup). Refused so the swap can't follow the link to an unintended target. Pre-destructive. UpluginMissingAfterExtract After extraction, KARIANA.uplugin not present. Post-rename, rollback fired. Old dir renamed back to plugin_dir. Io(...) Any underlying I/O error during rename, extract, marker write, or relaunch. Mostly post-rename — rollback attempted; check log for which step. Zip(...) Zip parse error during validate or extract (e.g., truncated archive). Pre- or post-rename depending on when it fires. Rollback attempted if post.

docs.title: Bootstrapper algorithm
docs.text:
1. Parse + validate manifest. Reject schema != 1, reject any path containing .., reject relative paths.
  2. Wait for editor exit. Poll editor_pid up to 30 s. If it never exits, abort with editor_did_not_exit (no destructive action taken).
  3. Re-verify SHA-256 of staged_zip against expected_sha256. Mismatch → abort with sha_mismatch.
  4. Validate zip entries without extracting. Reject any entry where the relative path:
  5. Is absolute (starts with /, \, or contains a drive-letter :)
  6. Contains .. segments after normalization
  7. Is a symlink (zip entry external attributes flag the symlink mode bit) These three checks together are the zip-slip guard — sufficient to guarantee no entry can escape the eventual extraction root.
  8. Rename every direct child of plugin_dir to <name><rename_suffix>. If plugin_dir itself is the rename target (typical), rename the whole dir to <plugin_dir><rename_suffix> and recreate plugin_dir empty.
  9. Extract zip into plugin_dir's parent.
  10. Verify the extracted result contains a parseable KARIANA.uplugin. If missing → rollback.
  11. On success:
  12. Write to_version to rollback_marker.
  13. Append OK line to log_path.
  14. If relaunch.enabled, spawn the editor process detached and exit 0.
  15. On any failure between steps 5 and 7:
  16. Delete the partial extraction.
  17. Rename <plugin_dir><rename_suffix> back to plugin_dir.
  18. Append FAIL <reason> to log_path.
  19. Do NOT touch rollback_marker.
  20. Exit non-zero.

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
The bootstrapper does NOT delete the renamed .old-* files. Doing so would race with any UE process that might still be reading them (Windows file locks released on process exit, but the bootstrapper might run before all handles close). Instead:

  • Plugin KarianaUpdateChecker::Initialize runs a sweep on the next editor launch: anything matching <PluginParentDir>/KARIANA<rename_suffix_glob> is deleted.
  • Stale .old-* is harmless except for disk-space; the sweep is best-effort.

docs.title: Rollback semantics
docs.text:
If the plugin's first launch after a swap reads rollback_marker and finds it does NOT match the just-loaded KARIANA.uplugin's VersionName, it logs a warning and triggers a telemetry POST (Phase 4). The plugin still loads — we don't bail an editor session over a marker mismatch.

If the plugin's first launch finds NO rollback_marker but does find a .old-* sibling, it assumes the bootstrapper crashed mid-swap, runs the rename-back recovery, and POSTs a telemetry failure.

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• Zip integrity: SHA-256 of staged_zip is the only integrity check in v1. A CDN compromise that substitutes a malicious zip with a matching SHA-256 (preimage attack — infeasible in practice for SHA-256) would defeat this. Future hardening: cosign / Authenticode signature verification.
  • Manifest authenticity: The manifest JSON itself is not signed or MAC'd in v1. An attacker with write access to the user's <LocalAppData>/KARiANA/ directory can substitute a crafted manifest pointing the bootstrapper at an arbitrary zip. The SHA-256 still validates the zip body, so the attacker would need both a malicious zip AND its hash, but they could redirect to a zip from any URL the editor reaches. Accepted tradeoff for v1 (local-privilege user, same security boundary as the rest of <LocalAppData>). Future hardening: HMAC the manifest with a per-install key.
  • No elevation: the bootstrapper does not run with elevated privileges. Plugin install paths that require elevation (engine installs) are blocked at FKarianaInstallContext::CanAutoUpdate time and never reach this flow.
  • Write surface: the bootstrapper writes only to plugin_dir, plugin_dir's parent, log_path, and rollback_marker. All other paths are read-only.

docs.title: KARIANA ToolsetRegistry Interop — Architecture Design
docs.text: Target: expose KARIANA's 300+ MCP tools through Epic's UE 5.8 official ModelContextProtocol HTTP server (port 8000, /mcp) by registering a single FToolset subclass with the ToolsetRegistry plugin.

docs.title: 1. New Module Recommendation: KarianaToolsetBridge
docs.text:
Recommendation: create a new Editor module, LoadingPhase: PostEngineInit.

Rationale for not reusing an existing module:

  • UnrealMCPBridge loads at phase Default. UToolsetRegistrySubsystem is a UEditorSubsystem and is not guaranteed initialized until PostEngineInit. Calling RegisterToolset from Default phase will crash on subsystem lookup.
  • GenerativeAISupportEditor already owns the C++ FKarianaCommandRegistry. Adding a ToolsetRegistry concern there violates SRP and creates a circular-dependency risk if KarianaToolsetBridge later depends on UnrealMCPBridge (socket reuse).
  • A dedicated module isolates the Epic API surface. If Epic changes FToolset between UE 5.8 minor versions, only KarianaToolsetBridge.Build.cs updates.
  • The module can be conditionally compiled (#if WITH_EDITOR) and excluded from cooked targets without touching any runtime module.
Field Value Module name KarianaToolsetBridge Type Editor Loading phase PostEngineInit uplugin entry New entry after UnrealAssistantIntegration

docs.title: 2.1 FKarianaToolset : public FToolset
docs.text:
File: Source/KarianaToolsetBridge/Public/FKarianaToolset.h

FString CachedSchemaJson          // populated once at construction, immutable after
FCriticalSection PendingLock      // guards PendingPromises map
TMap<FString, TSharedPtr<TPromise<TValueOrError<FString,FString>>>> PendingPromises

Toolset name exposed to Epic is "kariana", making descriptors kariana.<tool_name>.

docs.title: 2.2 GetJsonSchemaInternal() — Recommended: Python via IPythonScriptPlugin, cached at construction
docs.text:
Option A (recommended): At construction time, call IPythonScriptPlugin::Get()->ExecPythonCommandEx() to import tool_schema and call extract_tool_schemas(). Translate from KARIANA's OpenAI-function-call format ({type: function, function: {name, description, parameters}}) into the MCP tools/list shape ({tools: [{name, description, inputSchema}]}) inside the same Python invocation. Store the serialized string in CachedSchemaJson. GetJsonSchemaInternal() returns it directly — zero allocation on repeat calls.

Option B: Derive schemas from FKarianaCommandRegistry::GetAllCommands(). Rejected: the C++ registry only covers high-frequency operations; ~270 Python-only tools would be missing.

Caching/invalidation: Static for the editor session. Console command kariana.RefreshToolsetSchema re-runs Python extraction and re-registers the toolset for development workflows.

docs.title: 2.3 ExecuteToolInternal(FString ToolName, FString JsonInput) — Two-tier dispatch
docs.text:
Returns TFuture<TValueOrError<FString, FString>>.

Tier 1 (C++ fast path): If FKarianaCommandRegistry::Get().HasCommand(ToolName), execute via ExecuteCommandJson(ToolName, JsonInput) synchronously. Wrap in a fulfilled TPromise, return its future immediately.

Tier 2 (Python socket): Else write {"type": ToolName, "params": <parsed>, "request_id": <guid>} to KARIANA's TCP server on port 9877. Steps:

  1. Generate RequestId = FGuid::NewGuid().ToString().
  2. Insert TSharedPtr<TPromise> into PendingPromises[RequestId] under PendingLock.
  3. Non-blocking socket write (any thread).
  4. Socket reader thread (existing FMCPSocketServer worker) matches incoming request_id, fulfills promise, removes from map.
  5. Return future to caller.

Timeout: 30 seconds (configurable via UKarianaAssistantSettings::ToolExecutionTimeoutSeconds); a periodic FTSTicker fulfills stale promises with an error.

docs.title: 3. Module Startup Wiring
docs.text:
void FKarianaToolsetBridgeModule::StartupModule()
{
    FCoreDelegates::OnPostEngineInit.AddRaw(this, &FKarianaToolsetBridgeModule::OnPostEngineInit);
}

void FKarianaToolsetBridgeModule::OnPostEngineInit()
{
    auto* Subsystem = GEditor->GetEditorSubsystem<UToolsetRegistrySubsystem>();
    if (!Subsystem) return;
    TSharedRef<FKarianaToolset> Toolset = MakeShared<FKarianaToolset>();
    Subsystem->ToolsetRegistry.RegisterToolset(Toolset);
    RegisteredToolset = Toolset;
}

Optionally, also call IModelContextProtocolModule::GetChecked().OnRefreshTools() to re-add when Epic's MCP module asks for refresh.

docs.title: 4. Build.cs and uplugin
docs.text:
PublicDependencyModuleNames: Core, CoreUObject, Engine, Json, JsonUtilities

PrivateDependencyModuleNames: UnrealEd, ToolsetRegistry, PythonScriptPlugin, Sockets, Networking, GenerativeAISupportEditor, UnrealMCPBridge, Settings

KARIANA.uplugin changes:

{ "Name": "KarianaToolsetBridge", "Type": "Editor",
  "LoadingPhase": "PostEngineInit",
  "PlatformAllowList": ["Win64","Mac","Linux"] }

Plugin deps: 

{ "Name": "ToolsetRegistry", "Enabled": true, "Optional": true },
{ "Name": "ModelContextProtocol", "Enabled": true, "Optional": true }

Optional: true means a missing experimental plugin gracefully no-ops via the null-subsystem guard.

docs.title: 5. Deferred Tool Loading Option (kariana_dispatch)
docs.text:
Single meta-tool with tool_name + payload parameters, mirroring Epic's list_toolsets/describe_toolset/load_toolset deferred pattern.

Pros: minimal schema payload; immune to KARIANA tool churn; matches existing tool_schema.py:get_deferred_loading_discovery_tools(). Cons: destroys discoverability — Epic's UI and any AI client lose tool descriptions. Hides KARIANA's capability from the broader MCP ecosystem.

Verdict: ship it as a fallback, not the default. When Python schema extraction returns < 50 tools, register kariana_dispatch instead. Setting bForceDispatchMode = true opts in for minimal-footprint deployments.

docs.title: 6. Coexistence with KARIANA's Existing Socket Server
docs.text:
Both transports run simultaneously:

Transport Port Client KARIANA TCP socket 9877 Claude Code Bridge daemon, LM Studio, Ollama, Bedrock backends, kariana-remote Epic MCP HTTP 8000 Epic's MCP clients, third-party MCP tools

FKarianaToolset is an internal client of port 9877 (persistent socket preferred for latency).

Settings flags on UKarianaAssistantSettings:

UPROPERTY(config, EditAnywhere, Category = "MCP Integration")
bool bEnableToolsetRegistryBridge = true;

UPROPERTY(config, EditAnywhere, Category = "MCP Integration")
bool bEnableSocketServer = true;

UPROPERTY(config, EditAnywhere, Category = "MCP Integration")
bool bForceDispatchMode = false;

UPROPERTY(config, EditAnywhere, Category = "MCP Integration")
float ToolExecutionTimeoutSeconds = 30.0f;

docs.title: 7. Test Strategy
docs.text:
New Editor module KarianaToolsetBridgeTests, WITH_AUTOMATION_TESTS only.

Test A — Schema validation (FToolsetSchemaTest): Construct FKarianaToolset, parse GetJsonSchemaInternal(), assert tools array length > 50, every entry has name/description/inputSchema, get_project_info present.

Test B — Round-trip execution (FToolExecuteRoundTripTest, [Slow]): Requires socket server. Calls get_project_info (no params) and handshake_test (single string), asserts non-error futures and expected response fields.

Test C — Integration (FMCPHttpToolsListTest, [RequiresNetwork][Slow]): Requires Epic's MCP server. POST http://localhost:8000/mcp with tools/list, assert at least one tool name starts with kariana., kariana.get_project_info is present.

docs.title: 9. Risks
docs.text:
R1 — FToolset API surface uncertainty (high impact, medium probability) — design built from header summaries; full method signatures need verification against E:\ue5.8-dev source before implementation. Mitigation: pin to a concrete commit hash, add static_assert confirming the base class.

R2 — Circular module deps (high, low) — KarianaToolsetBridge depends on GenerativeAISupportEditor and UnrealMCPBridge. Reverse direction must remain forbidden. Mitigation: singleton-only access; no headers of KarianaToolsetBridge are included from those modules; document the one-way arrow in Build.cs comments.

R3 — Python schema extraction timing (medium, medium) — IPythonScriptPlugin may not have unreal module fully ready at PostEngineInit. tool_schema.py:_get_fallback_schemas() activates as fallback. Mitigation: detect fallback (count < 50), log warning, retry after 5s via FTicker.

R4 — Cooked-platform stripping (low, low) — Editor type module is correctly excluded; verify .uplugin matches pattern of existing Editor modules.

R5 — Promise fulfillment race on shutdown (medium, low) — unfulfilled TPromise triggers Debug check on destruction. Mitigation: ShutdownModule iterates pending map, fulfills each with "Shutdown" error before socket close.

R6 — Schema divergence between socket and MCP surfaces — Python tool_schema.py is the single source of truth; if a tool is added but the Python registry isn't refreshed, MCP clients see stale data. Mitigation: console command to re-extract.

R7 — CI Origin-guard breakage — Epic's DNS-rebinding guard rejects non-localhost Origins. Test C HTTP integration test must use 127.0.0.1 not a hostname.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        COLOR SOURCES                                 |
|                                                                      |
|  KarianaBrandColors.h          themes.json                           |
|  (69 inline FLinearColor)      (69 colors, JSON arrays)              |
|  DEFAULT values                 OVERRIDE values                      |
|  LINEAR-SPACE                   LINEAR-SPACE [R,G,B] or [R,G,B,A]   |
+----------+------------------------------+---------------------------+
           |                              |
           |    +-------------------------+|
           +--->|  KarianaBrandTheme.cpp   ||
                |  ApplyTheme()           ||
                |  - 69-entry dispatch    |<+
                |    table maps JSON      |
                |    keys -> ptrs         |
                |  - Overwrites inline    |
                |    globals in-place     |
                +-----------+-------------+
                            |
            +---------------+---------------+
            |                               |
            v                               v
+-----------------------+     +--------------------------+
| DIRECT CONSUMPTION    |     | STYLE SET CONSUMPTION    |
|                       |     |                          |
| Widgets read          |     | KarianaMarkdownStyle.cpp |
| KarianaBrand::XYZ     |     | Creates FSlateStyleSet   |
| directly in Construct |     | with named brushes &     |
|                       |     | text styles from brand   |
| 15 of 21 widgets      |     | colors at init time      |
| use this pattern      |     |                          |
+-----------------------+     +--------------------------+

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Default colors -> inline FLinearColor globals in KarianaBrandColors.h (69 colors)
  2. On startup -> KarianaBrandTheme::ApplyTheme("KARIANA Dark") reads themes.json
  3. Dispatch table -> 69-entry map of JSON key strings to pointers to those inline globals
  4. Overwrites -> JSON values replace inline globals in-place (same linear-space format)
  5. Fallback -> if themes.json missing, hardcoded defaults remain (always works)
  6. Consumption -> two patterns: direct KarianaBrand::XYZ reads, or FKarianaMarkdownStyle::Get() brushes

docs.title: Python IP Protection — Cython Compilation Pipeline
docs.text:
For Claude: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

Goal: Compile all sensitive Python sources to native .pyd/.so extensions and enforce per-client Ed25519-signed licenses so distributed plugin binaries reveal no methodology and cannot be shared or forged.

Architecture: Cython converts .py → C → native extensions. Ed25519 asymmetric signing — private key stays with KARIANA, public key is embedded in the compiled binary so clients cannot forge licenses even if they disassemble it. The daemon auto-discovers the license from OS standard paths — no configuration needed from clients or team members. CI targets Windows (shipped in pre-alpha) with Mac/Linux matrix ready for future delivery.

Tech Stack: Cython 3.x, setuptools, cryptography (Ed25519), GitHub Actions (windows-latest + macos-latest + ubuntu-latest matrix), Python 3.11 (UE 5.7 embedded version)

docs.title: Task 1: Generate Ed25519 Keypair (One-Time KARIANA Setup)
docs.text:
Files: - Create: tools/generate_keypair.py - Modify: .gitignore

Step 1: Install cryptography on your dev machine

pip install cryptography

Step 2: Create tools/generate_keypair.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
One-time Ed25519 keypair generation for KARIANA license signing.
Run ONCE on a secure machine. Never run again unless rotating keys.

    python tools/generate_keypair.py

Outputs:
    licenses/private_key.pem           — NEVER commit. Store in 1Password immediately.
    Content/Python/licensing/public_key.pem  — safe to commit (public half only)

After running, paste the printed DER_B64 value into Content/Python/licensing/core.py
"""
import base64
from pathlib import Path

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import (
    Encoding, PrivateFormat, PublicFormat, NoEncryption,
)


def main():
    private_key = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    public_key = private_key.public_key()

    private_pem = private_key.private_bytes(Encoding.PEM, PrivateFormat.PKCS8, NoEncryption())
    public_pem = public_key.public_bytes(Encoding.PEM, PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo)
    public_der = public_key.public_bytes(Encoding.DER, PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo)
    public_der_b64 = base64.b64encode(public_der).decode("ascii")

    Path("licenses").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    Path("licenses/private_key.pem").write_bytes(private_pem)
    Path("Content/Python/licensing/public_key.pem").write_bytes(public_pem)

    print("=" * 60)
    print("KEYPAIR GENERATED")
    print("=" * 60)
    print()
    print(">>> STEP 1: Save licenses/private_key.pem to 1Password NOW <<<")
    print()
    print(">>> STEP 2: Paste this line into Content/Python/licensing/core.py <<<")
    print()
    print(f'_PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64 = "{public_der_b64}"')
    print()
    print("Public key file: Content/Python/licensing/public_key.pem (commit this)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Step 3: Run it

python tools/generate_keypair.py

Expected output: A _PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64 = "..." line printed. Copy it — you'll need it in Task 2.

Step 4: Immediately save licenses/private_key.pem to 1Password

This is the only copy. If lost, all existing licenses become unverifiable. Do this before continuing.

Step 5: Add to .gitignore

# Ed25519 private signing key — NEVER commit under any circumstances
licenses/private_key.pem
licenses/*.lic

# Cython compiled extensions (platform binaries — built by CI at release time)
Content/Python/**/*.pyd
Content/Python/**/*.so
Content/Python/**/*.c
Content/Python/build/

Step 6: Commit (public key file + generator + .gitignore, NOT private key)

git add tools/generate_keypair.py Content/Python/licensing/public_key.pem .gitignore
git commit -m "feat: add Ed25519 keypair generator and commit public key"

docs.title: Task 2: Replace HMAC with Ed25519 in licensing/core.py
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: Content/Python/licensing/core.py

Context: The current file uses HMAC-SHA256 with an embedded string key. That key is visible to anyone who reads the .pyd binary with a hex editor. Ed25519 asymmetric signing means only the holder of the private key (KARIANA) can create valid signatures. The public key embedded in the .pyd can only verify, never forge.

Step 1: Read the current file

cat Content/Python/licensing/core.py

Step 2: Write the failing test

# Content/Python/tests/test_licensing_ed25519.py
import json
import pytest
from unittest.mock import patch

# ---- helpers to generate a real keypair in tests ----
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import (
    Encoding, PublicFormat, PrivateFormat, NoEncryption,
)
import base64


def make_test_keypair():
    """Returns (private_key, public_der_b64) for test use."""
    priv = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    pub_der = priv.public_key().public_bytes(Encoding.DER, PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo)
    return priv, base64.b64encode(pub_der).decode("ascii")


def sign_test_license(data: dict, private_key) -> dict:
    """Sign a license dict with the given private key. Returns dict with signature."""
    filtered = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k != "signature"}
    payload = json.dumps(filtered, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
    sig = private_key.sign(payload)
    return {**data, "signature": base64.b64encode(sig).decode("ascii")}


VALID_LICENSE_DATA = {
    "license_id": "KAR-TEST-001",
    "client": "Test Studio",
    "type": "pre_alpha_enterprise",
    "seats": 1,
    "issued": "2026-01-01",
    "expires": "2028-01-01",
    "features": ["all"],
}


def test_valid_license_passes(tmp_path):
    priv, pub_b64 = make_test_keypair()
    signed = sign_test_license(VALID_LICENSE_DATA, priv)

    # Patch the embedded public key constant
    with patch("licensing.core._PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64", pub_b64):
        from licensing.core import validate_license
        info = validate_license(signed)

    assert info.client == "Test Studio"
    assert info.license_id == "KAR-TEST-001"
    assert info.has_feature("all")
    assert not info.is_expired


def test_tampered_license_fails():
    priv, pub_b64 = make_test_keypair()
    signed = sign_test_license(VALID_LICENSE_DATA, priv)
    signed["seats"] = 999  # tamper after signing

    with patch("licensing.core._PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64", pub_b64):
        from licensing.core import validate_license, LicenseError
        with pytest.raises(LicenseError, match="signature"):
            validate_license(signed)


def test_wrong_key_fails():
    priv1, _ = make_test_keypair()
    _, pub_b64_of_different_key = make_test_keypair()
    signed = sign_test_license(VALID_LICENSE_DATA, priv1)

    with patch("licensing.core._PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64", pub_b64_of_different_key):
        from licensing.core import validate_license, LicenseError
        with pytest.raises(LicenseError, match="signature"):
            validate_license(signed)


def test_expired_license_fails():
    priv, pub_b64 = make_test_keypair()
    expired_data = {**VALID_LICENSE_DATA, "expires": "2020-01-01"}
    signed = sign_test_license(expired_data, priv)

    with patch("licensing.core._PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64", pub_b64):
        from licensing.core import validate_license, LicenseError
        with pytest.raises(LicenseError, match="expired"):
            validate_license(signed)


def test_missing_signature_fails():
    priv, pub_b64 = make_test_keypair()
    unsigned = dict(VALID_LICENSE_DATA)  # no signature key

    with patch("licensing.core._PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64", pub_b64):
        from licensing.core import validate_license, LicenseError
        with pytest.raises(LicenseError, match="signature"):
            validate_license(unsigned)


def test_load_and_validate_from_file(tmp_path):
    priv, pub_b64 = make_test_keypair()
    signed = sign_test_license(VALID_LICENSE_DATA, priv)
    lic_file = tmp_path / "test.lic"
    lic_file.write_text(json.dumps(signed))

    with patch("licensing.core._PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64", pub_b64):
        from licensing.core import load_and_validate
        info = load_and_validate(str(lic_file))

    assert info.client == "Test Studio"

Step 3: Run tests to confirm they fail

cd D:/Developer/KARIANA/KARIANA
python -m pytest Content/Python/tests/test_licensing_ed25519.py -v

Expected: All FAIL (current core.py uses HMAC, not Ed25519).

Step 4: Replace Content/Python/licensing/core.py entirely

Take the _PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64 value printed by Task 1 Step 3 and paste it in:

"""
License validation for KARIANA Enterprise.

Ed25519 asymmetric signing: private key stays with KARIANA, public key is
embedded here. Clients cannot forge licenses even with full binary access.

Usage:
    from licensing.core import validate_license, load_and_validate, LicenseInfo

    info = load_and_validate("path/to/license.lic")
"""
import base64
import json
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidSignature
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import load_der_public_key


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Embedded public key — DER encoded, base64. Generated by tools/generate_keypair.py
# The private key never lives here. Extracting this only gives you the verifier half.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64 = "__PASTE_VALUE_FROM_generate_keypair.py_OUTPUT_HERE__"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Required license fields
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_REQUIRED_FIELDS = frozenset({
    "license_id", "client", "type", "seats", "issued", "expires", "features",
})


class LicenseError(Exception):
    """Raised when license validation fails."""


@dataclass
class LicenseInfo:
    license_id: str
    client: str
    license_type: str
    seats: int
    issued: date
    expires: date
    features: List[str]
    raw: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)

    def has_feature(self, name: str) -> bool:
        return "all" in self.features or name in self.features

    @property
    def is_expired(self) -> bool:
        return date.today() > self.expires

    @property
    def days_remaining(self) -> int:
        return (self.expires - date.today()).days


def _canonical_payload(data: Dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    """Deterministic bytes for signature verification — excludes the signature field."""
    filtered = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k != "signature"}
    return json.dumps(filtered, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")


def _public_key():
    der = base64.b64decode(_PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64)
    return load_der_public_key(der)


def validate_license(data: Dict[str, Any]) -> LicenseInfo:
    """Validate a license dict. Raises LicenseError on any failure."""
    missing = _REQUIRED_FIELDS - set(data.keys())
    if missing:
        raise LicenseError(f"License missing required fields: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")

    sig_b64 = data.get("signature")
    if not sig_b64:
        raise LicenseError("License signature is missing")

    try:
        sig_bytes = base64.b64decode(sig_b64)
        _public_key().verify(sig_bytes, _canonical_payload(data))
    except InvalidSignature:
        raise LicenseError("License signature verification failed — license may be tampered or invalid")
    except Exception as e:
        raise LicenseError(f"License verification error: {e}")

    try:
        issued = date.fromisoformat(data["issued"])
        expires = date.fromisoformat(data["expires"])
    except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
        raise LicenseError(f"Invalid date format in license: {exc}")

    if date.today() > expires:
        raise LicenseError(f"License expired on {expires.isoformat()}")

    return LicenseInfo(
        license_id=data["license_id"],
        client=data["client"],
        license_type=data["type"],
        seats=data["seats"],
        issued=issued,
        expires=expires,
        features=list(data["features"]),
        raw=dict(data),
    )


def load_and_validate(path: str) -> LicenseInfo:
    """Load a JSON license file from *path* and validate it."""
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        raise LicenseError(f"License file not found: {path}")
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
        raise LicenseError(f"Failed to parse license file: {exc}")
    return validate_license(data)

Step 1: Create the script

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate a signed KARIANA enterprise license file.

Usage:
    python tools/generate_license.py \
        --client "Acme Studios" \
        --type pre_alpha_enterprise \
        --seats 5 \
        --expires 2027-02-25 \
        --features all \
        --key licenses/private_key.pem \
        -o licenses/acme-studios.lic

License ID is auto-generated (KAR-YYYYMM-NNN). Use --id to set manually.
"""
import argparse
import base64
import json
import random
import string
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import load_pem_private_key


def _canonical_payload(data: dict) -> bytes:
    filtered = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k != "signature"}
    return json.dumps(filtered, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")


def generate_license(client, license_type, seats, expires, features, private_key_path,
                     license_id=None):
    with open(private_key_path, "rb") as f:
        private_key = load_pem_private_key(f.read(), password=None)

    if license_id is None:
        suffix = "".join(random.choices(string.digits, k=3))
        license_id = f"KAR-{date.today().strftime('%Y%m')}-{suffix}"

    data = {
        "license_id": license_id,
        "client": client,
        "type": license_type,
        "seats": seats,
        "issued": date.today().isoformat(),
        "expires": expires,
        "features": features,
    }

    sig_bytes = private_key.sign(_canonical_payload(data))
    data["signature"] = base64.b64encode(sig_bytes).decode("ascii")
    return data


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a signed KARIANA license file")
    parser.add_argument("--client", required=True, help="Client name or company")
    parser.add_argument("--type", default="pre_alpha_enterprise",
                        help="License type (default: pre_alpha_enterprise)")
    parser.add_argument("--seats", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--expires", required=True, help="Expiry date YYYY-MM-DD")
    parser.add_argument("--features", nargs="+", default=["all"],
                        help="Feature flags (default: all)")
    parser.add_argument("--id", dest="license_id", default=None,
                        help="Override auto-generated license ID")
    parser.add_argument("--key", default="licenses/private_key.pem",
                        help="Path to Ed25519 private key (default: licenses/private_key.pem)")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", required=True, help="Output .lic file path")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if not Path(args.key).exists():
        print(f"ERROR: Private key not found at {args.key}")
        print("Run tools/generate_keypair.py first and restore from 1Password.")
        raise SystemExit(1)

    lic = generate_license(
        client=args.client,
        license_type=args.type,
        seats=args.seats,
        expires=args.expires,
        features=args.features,
        private_key_path=args.key,
        license_id=args.license_id,
    )

    Path(args.output).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    Path(args.output).write_text(json.dumps(lic, indent=2))

    print(f"License generated: {args.output}")
    print(f"  License ID : {lic['license_id']}")
    print(f"  Client     : {lic['client']}")
    print(f"  Type       : {lic['type']}")
    print(f"  Seats      : {lic['seats']}")
    print(f"  Expires    : {lic['expires']}")
    print(f"  Features   : {lic['features']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Content/Python/tests/test_generate_license.py
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import (
    Encoding, PrivateFormat, PublicFormat, NoEncryption,
)
import base64


@pytest.fixture
def test_keypair(tmp_path):
    """Generate a real test keypair and return (priv_key_path, pub_der_b64)."""
    priv = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    pub_der = priv.public_key().public_bytes(Encoding.DER, PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo)
    priv_path = tmp_path / "test_private.pem"
    priv_path.write_bytes(priv.private_bytes(Encoding.PEM, PrivateFormat.PKCS8, NoEncryption()))
    return str(priv_path), base64.b64encode(pub_der).decode("ascii")


def test_generate_license_creates_valid_signed_file(tmp_path, test_keypair):
    priv_key_path, pub_b64 = test_keypair
    output = str(tmp_path / "client.lic")

    result = subprocess.run([
        sys.executable, "tools/generate_license.py",
        "--client", "Acme Studios",
        "--type", "pre_alpha_enterprise",
        "--seats", "5",
        "--expires", "2028-01-01",
        "--features", "all",
        "--key", priv_key_path,
        "-o", output,
    ], capture_output=True, text=True)

    assert result.returncode == 0, f"Script failed: {result.stderr}"

    lic = json.loads(Path(output).read_text())
    assert lic["client"] == "Acme Studios"
    assert lic["seats"] == 5
    assert "signature" in lic
    assert lic["license_id"].startswith("KAR-")

    # Verify signature validates with the matching public key
    with patch("licensing.core._PUBLIC_KEY_DER_B64", pub_b64):
        from licensing.core import validate_license
        info = validate_license(lic)
    assert info.client == "Acme Studios"


def test_generate_license_fails_without_private_key(tmp_path):
    result = subprocess.run([
        sys.executable, "tools/generate_license.py",
        "--client", "Whoever",
        "--expires", "2028-01-01",
        "--key", "licenses/nonexistent_key.pem",
        "-o", str(tmp_path / "out.lic"),
    ], capture_output=True, text=True)

    assert result.returncode != 0

docs.text:
Files: - Modify: Content/Python/kariana_agent_daemon.py (around lines 1113-1150)

Context: Currently the daemon reads --license flag but falls through on error. New behavior: auto-discover license from standard OS paths, hard-exit if not found or invalid. No --license flag required by default — clients and team members just place the file in the right location. The installer handles this for clients.

License search order: 1. --license CLI arg (explicit override) 2. KARIANA_LICENSE_PATH env var (CI / advanced users) 3. %APPDATA%\KARIANA\license.lic (Windows clients and team) 4. ~/.config/kariana/license.lic (Mac/Linux) 5. Same directory as kariana_agent_daemon.py (dev fallback)

# Content/Python/tests/test_daemon_license_discovery.py
"""
Tests for daemon license auto-discovery and enforcement.
Runs the daemon as a subprocess and checks its JSON output + exit code.
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import (
    Encoding, PrivateFormat, PublicFormat, NoEncryption,
)
import base64

DAEMON_PATH = "Content/Python/kariana_agent_daemon.py"


def make_signed_license(tmp_path):
    """Generate a real keypair, sign a license, return (lic_path, pub_b64)."""
    priv = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    pub_der = priv.public_key().public_bytes(Encoding.DER, PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo)
    pub_b64 = base64.b64encode(pub_der).decode("ascii")
    priv_pem = priv.private_bytes(Encoding.PEM, PrivateFormat.PKCS8, NoEncryption())

    # Sign the license using generate_license directly
    priv_key_file = tmp_path / "priv.pem"
    priv_key_file.write_bytes(priv_pem)

    import base64 as _b64, json as _json
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import load_pem_private_key
    priv_obj = load_pem_private_key(priv_pem, password=None)

    data = {
        "license_id": "KAR-TEST-001",
        "client": "Test Client",
        "type": "pre_alpha_enterprise",
        "seats": 1,
        "issued": "2026-01-01",
        "expires": "2028-01-01",
        "features": ["all"],
    }
    payload = _json.dumps(
        {k: v for k, v in data.items()}, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True
    ).encode("utf-8")
    sig = priv_obj.sign(payload)
    data["signature"] = _b64.b64encode(sig).decode("ascii")

    lic_file = tmp_path / "test.lic"
    lic_file.write_text(_json.dumps(data))
    return str(lic_file), pub_b64


def run_daemon(extra_args=None, env=None, timeout=5):
    """Run daemon as subprocess, capture stdout lines as parsed JSON."""
    cmd = [sys.executable, DAEMON_PATH] + (extra_args or [])
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, env=env)
    messages = []
    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith("{"):
            try:
                messages.append(json.loads(line))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                pass
    return result.returncode, messages


def test_daemon_exits_without_license():
    """No license anywhere → daemon exits non-zero with clear error message."""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env.pop("KARIANA_LICENSE_PATH", None)
    # Point APPDATA to a temp dir with no license
    env["APPDATA"] = "C:\\nonexistent_test_path_kariana"
    env["HOME"] = "/nonexistent_test_path_kariana"

    returncode, messages = run_daemon(env=env)
    assert returncode != 0, "Daemon should exit non-zero without license"
    types = [m.get("type") for m in messages]
    assert "error" in types, f"Expected error message, got: {messages}"


def test_daemon_exits_with_invalid_license(tmp_path):
    """Tampered license → daemon exits non-zero."""
    bad_lic = tmp_path / "bad.lic"
    bad_lic.write_text('{"license_id": "FAKE", "client": "Hacker", "signature": "invalid"}')
    returncode, messages = run_daemon(["--license", str(bad_lic)])
    assert returncode != 0
    types = [m.get("type") for m in messages]
    assert "error" in types


def test_daemon_discovers_license_via_env_var(tmp_path):
    """KARIANA_LICENSE_PATH env var is used when --license is not passed."""
    lic_path, pub_b64 = make_signed_license(tmp_path)
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["KARIANA_LICENSE_PATH"] = lic_path

    # Patch the embedded public key so our test license validates
    # This requires the daemon to use our test pub key — skip if not feasible in subprocess
    # Instead, verify the daemon starts past the license check (not just fails with no-license error)
    returncode, messages = run_daemon(env=env, timeout=3)
    types = [m.get("type") for m in messages]
    # Should NOT have "no license found" error — may still fail for other reasons
    error_messages = [m.get("message", "") for m in messages if m.get("type") == "error"]
    assert not any("license not found" in m.lower() for m in error_messages), \
        f"Daemon should find license via env var, got: {messages}"

def _find_license_path(explicit_path=None):
    """Search for license file in order of preference."""
    import sys as _sys
    # 1. Explicit --license flag
    if explicit_path:
        return explicit_path
    # 2. Environment variable
    env_path = os.environ.get("KARIANA_LICENSE_PATH")
    if env_path and os.path.isfile(env_path):
        return env_path
    # 3. OS standard config path
    if _sys.platform == "win32":
        appdata = os.environ.get("APPDATA", "")
        candidate = os.path.join(appdata, "KARIANA", "license.lic")
    else:
        home = os.path.expanduser("~")
        candidate = os.path.join(home, ".config", "kariana", "license.lic")
    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
        return candidate
    # 4. Same directory as this script (dev fallback)
    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    local = os.path.join(script_dir, "license.lic")
    if os.path.isfile(local):
        return local
    return None

"""
Cython build configuration for KARIANA IP protection.
Compiles protected .py sources to native extensions (.pyd on Windows, .so on Mac/Linux).

Run from the Content/Python/ directory:
    python setup_compile.py build_ext --inplace
"""
import glob
import os
from setuptools import setup
from Cython.Build import cythonize

PROTECTED_FILES = (
    # Root-level daemon and servers
    ["kariana_agent_daemon.py", "mcp_server.py", "unreal_socket_server.py"]
    # All handler implementations
    + glob.glob("handlers/*.py")
    # Sensitive backends
    + [
        "backends/openai_compat_backend.py",
        "backends/bedrock_backend.py",
        "backends/bedrock_daemon_adapter.py",
        "backends/tool_schema.py",
        "backends/tool_executor.py",
    ]
    # License core
    + ["licensing/core.py"]
)

# Never compile __init__.py — these must stay as .py for package imports
PROTECTED_FILES = [f for f in PROTECTED_FILES if "__init__" not in f]

setup(
    ext_modules=cythonize(
        PROTECTED_FILES,
        compiler_directives={
            "language_level": "3",
            "always_allow_keywords": True,
        },
        nthreads=4,
        quiet=False,
    )
)

docs.text:
Files: - Create: .github/workflows/build-release.yml

Design: - Windows ships in pre-alpha (required). Mac/Linux compile in CI for future — artifacts uploaded but NOT included in pre-alpha release zip. - Triggered on version tags (v*) and manual workflow_dispatch. - Smoke tests run after compilation on each platform.

Step 1: Create .github/workflows/build-release.yml

name: Build Release Binaries

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  compile:
    name: Compile Python extensions (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            artifact_name: compiled-windows
            ext: "*.pyd"
            ship_in_prealpha: true
          - os: macos-latest
            artifact_name: compiled-macos
            ext: "*.so"
            ship_in_prealpha: false   # future — compiles but not shipped yet
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            artifact_name: compiled-linux
            ext: "*.so"
            ship_in_prealpha: false   # future — compiles but not shipped yet
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python 3.11
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      - name: Install build tools
        run: pip install "cython>=3.0" setuptools wheel

      - name: Install runtime dependencies (required for smoke tests)
        run: pip install anthropic mss pillow fastmcp cryptography pytest

      - name: Compile Python to native extensions
        working-directory: Content/Python
        run: python setup_compile.py build_ext --inplace

      - name: List compiled files
        working-directory: Content/Python
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "=== Compiled extensions ==="
          find . \( -name "*.pyd" -o -name "*.so" \) | grep -v __pycache__ | sort

      - name: Run smoke tests
        working-directory: Content/Python
        run: python -m pytest tests/test_compiled_imports.py -v

      - name: Upload compiled artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.artifact_name }}
          path: |
            Content/Python/**/*.pyd
            Content/Python/**/*.so
          if-no-files-found: error

  package:
    name: Package Pre-Alpha Release (Windows only)
    needs: compile
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Download Windows artifacts only
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: compiled-windows
          path: compiled-artifacts/compiled-windows/

      - name: Package Windows release
        run: python tools/package_release.py --artifacts compiled-artifacts/ --output release/ --platforms windows

      - name: Upload release package
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: KARIANA-release
          path: release/

Step 2: Commit

git add .github/workflows/build-release.yml
git commit -m "feat: add GitHub Actions Cython build workflow — Windows ships, Mac/Linux ready"

docs.title: Task 8: Smoke Tests with unreal Module Mock
docs.text:
Files: - Create: Content/Python/tests/conftest.py - Create: Content/Python/tests/test_compiled_imports.py

Context: All handlers have import unreal at module level. Cython compiles them fine. But when the CI smoke tests import the compiled .pyd files, Python executes import unreal — which fails because UE is not present. The conftest.py mock runs before any test module is loaded, so sys.modules['unreal'] is pre-populated with a MagicMock before any import chain hits it.

Step 1: Create Content/Python/tests/conftest.py

"""
pytest conftest — runs before any test file.
Mocks the `unreal` module so compiled extensions that have
`import unreal` at module level can be imported in CI (no UE present).
"""
import sys
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

if "unreal" not in sys.modules:
    # Create a deeply recursive MagicMock so attribute chains like
    # unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_asset() don't raise AttributeError
    sys.modules["unreal"] = MagicMock()

Step 2: Create Content/Python/tests/test_compiled_imports.py

"""
Smoke test: verify all protected compiled modules import without errors.
Must run AFTER Cython compilation — requires .pyd/.so files to exist.
conftest.py mocks `unreal` before this file is loaded.
"""
import importlib
import pytest


COMPILED_MODULES = [
    "kariana_agent_daemon",
    "mcp_server",
    "unreal_socket_server",
    "handlers.actor_commands",
    "handlers.blueprint_commands",
    "handlers.basic_commands",
    "handlers.pcg_commands",
    "handlers.physics_commands",
    "handlers.organization_commands",
    "handlers.spatial_commands",
    "handlers.ui_commands",
    "backends.openai_compat_backend",
    "backends.tool_schema",
    "backends.tool_executor",
    "licensing.core",
]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("module_name", COMPILED_MODULES)
def test_compiled_module_imports(module_name):
    """Every compiled module must be importable — no import errors."""
    mod = importlib.import_module(module_name)
    assert mod is not None


def test_licensing_core_api_accessible():
    """After compilation, the licensing API surface must be intact."""
    from licensing.core import LicenseInfo, validate_license, load_and_validate
    assert callable(validate_license)
    assert callable(load_and_validate)
    assert hasattr(LicenseInfo, "has_feature")
    assert hasattr(LicenseInfo, "is_expired")
    assert hasattr(LicenseInfo, "days_remaining")

Step 3: Verify locally (after Task 6 compilation)

cd Content/Python
python -m pytest tests/test_compiled_imports.py -v

Expected: All 16+ tests PASS. If any fail with ModuleNotFoundError, the module name is wrong or the .pyd wasn't built — recheck Task 6.

Step 4: Commit

git add Content/Python/tests/conftest.py Content/Python/tests/test_compiled_imports.py
git commit -m "test: add compiled module smoke tests with unreal mock for CI"

docs.title: Task 9: Release Packaging Script
docs.text:
Files: - Create: tools/package_release.py

Step 1: Create the script

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Package KARIANA plugin for distribution.

Usage:
    python tools/package_release.py \
        --artifacts compiled-artifacts/ \
        --output release/ \
        --platforms windows          # or: windows macos linux (space-separated)

Produces:
    release/KARIANA-Win64.zip        (when --platforms includes windows)
    release/KARIANA-macOS.zip        (future)
    release/KARIANA-Linux.zip        (future)

Each zip contains:
  - All non-protected source files (.py files that are safe to expose)
  - Compiled extensions (.pyd/.so) for that platform
  - NO protected .py sources (handlers/, licensing/, backends secrets, daemon)
"""
import argparse
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path


PROTECTED_PY_FILES = {
    "kariana_agent_daemon.py",
    "mcp_server.py",
    "unreal_socket_server.py",
}

PROTECTED_PY_DIRS = {"handlers", "licensing"}

PROTECTED_BACKEND_FILES = {
    "openai_compat_backend.py",
    "bedrock_backend.py",
    "bedrock_daemon_adapter.py",
    "tool_schema.py",
    "tool_executor.py",
}

PLATFORM_MAP = {
    "windows": ("Win64", ".pyd", "compiled-windows"),
    "macos": ("macOS", ".so", "compiled-macos"),
    "linux": ("Linux", ".so", "compiled-linux"),
}


def is_protected_py(path: Path, repo_root: Path) -> bool:
    """Return True if this .py file must be excluded from the release zip."""
    try:
        rel = path.relative_to(repo_root)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    parts = rel.parts

    # e.g. Content/Python/kariana_agent_daemon.py
    if (len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "Content" and parts[1] == "Python"
            and parts[2] in PROTECTED_PY_FILES):
        return True

    # e.g. Content/Python/handlers/blueprint_commands.py
    if (len(parts) >= 4 and parts[0] == "Content" and parts[1] == "Python"
            and parts[2] in PROTECTED_PY_DIRS):
        return True

    # e.g. Content/Python/backends/bedrock_backend.py
    if (len(parts) == 4 and parts[0] == "Content" and parts[1] == "Python"
            and parts[2] == "backends" and parts[3] in PROTECTED_BACKEND_FILES):
        return True

    return False


def build_platform_zip(repo_root: Path, artifact_dir: Path,
                        platform_name: str, ext: str, output_dir: Path):
    zip_path = output_dir / f"KARIANA-{platform_name}.zip"
    print(f"\nPackaging {platform_name} → {zip_path}")
    protected_skipped = 0
    files_added = 0

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        # Walk the full repo and include non-protected files
        for src in sorted(repo_root.rglob("*")):
            if not src.is_file():
                continue
            rel = src.relative_to(repo_root)
            str_rel = str(rel)

            # Skip git, __pycache__, build artifacts, compiled binaries
            if any(part.startswith(".") for part in rel.parts):
                continue
            if "__pycache__" in str_rel or str_rel.endswith(".pyc"):
                continue
            if "build/" in str_rel or str_rel.endswith((".c", ".pyd", ".so")):
                continue

            # Skip protected .py sources — they ship as compiled extensions only
            if src.suffix == ".py" and is_protected_py(src, repo_root):
                protected_skipped += 1
                continue

            zf.write(src, rel)
            files_added += 1

        # Add compiled extensions for this platform
        compiled_count = 0
        for compiled in sorted(artifact_dir.rglob(f"*{ext}")):
            rel_in_artifact = compiled.relative_to(artifact_dir)
            zf.write(compiled, rel_in_artifact)
            compiled_count += 1
            print(f"  + {rel_in_artifact}")

    size_mb = zip_path.stat().st_size / 1024 / 1024
    print(f"  {files_added} source files + {compiled_count} compiled extensions")
    print(f"  {protected_skipped} protected .py files stripped")
    print(f"  Done → {zip_path.name} ({size_mb:.1f} MB)")


def verify_no_protected_sources(zip_path: Path):
    """Fail-safe: assert no protected .py files leaked into the zip."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as zf:
        names = zf.namelist()
    leaked = [
        n for n in names
        if n.endswith(".py") and any(x in n for x in [
            "handlers/", "licensing/", "kariana_agent_daemon",
            "mcp_server.py", "unreal_socket_server",
            "bedrock_backend", "tool_executor", "tool_schema",
        ])
    ]
    if leaked:
        print(f"SECURITY VIOLATION — protected .py files in {zip_path.name}:")
        for f in leaked:
            print(f"  {f}")
        raise SystemExit(1)
    print(f"  Security check PASSED — no protected .py sources in {zip_path.name}")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Package KARIANA for distribution")
    parser.add_argument("--artifacts", required=True,
                        help="Directory containing downloaded CI artifacts")
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True,
                        help="Output directory for release zips")
    parser.add_argument("--platforms", nargs="+", default=["windows"],
                        choices=["windows", "macos", "linux"],
                        help="Platforms to package (default: windows)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    repo_root = Path(__file__).parent.parent
    artifact_root = Path(args.artifacts)
    output_dir = Path(args.output)
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    for platform_key in args.platforms:
        platform_name, ext, artifact_subdir = PLATFORM_MAP[platform_key]
        artifact_dir = artifact_root / artifact_subdir
        if not artifact_dir.exists():
            print(f"WARNING: No artifacts for {platform_name} at {artifact_dir} — skipping")
            continue
        build_platform_zip(repo_root, artifact_dir, platform_name, ext, output_dir)
        verify_no_protected_sources(output_dir / f"KARIANA-{platform_name}.zip")

    print("\n=== Release packages ===")
    for z in sorted(output_dir.glob("*.zip")):
        print(f"  {z.name}  ({z.stat().st_size / 1024 / 1024:.1f} MB)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Step 2: Verify locally (after Task 6 compilation)

cp Content/Python/handlers/*.pyd /tmp/fake-artifacts/compiled-windows/ 2>/dev/null || true
cp Content/Python/licensing/*.pyd /tmp/fake-artifacts/compiled-windows/ 2>/dev/null || true

python tools/package_release.py \
  --artifacts /tmp/fake-artifacts \
  --output /tmp/kariana-release \
  --platforms windows

Expected: Security check PASSED printed. No SECURITY VIOLATION.

git commit -m "feat: add release packaging script — strips .py sources, bundles per-platform compiled extensions"

docs.title: Task 10: Generate Team and Client Licenses
docs.text:
Context: With Task 4 complete, the daemon requires a license. The team needs licenses immediately to keep working. Each team member and client gets their own unique license.

Step 1: Restore the private key from 1Password

The private key was backed up in Task 1. Restore it to licenses/private_key.pem on your machine. Never commit it.

Step 2: Generate team licenses

Generate one per team member. Use names that identify the person if a license ever leaks.

python tools/generate_license.py \
  --client "KARIANA Dev — Aristide" \
  --type internal_dev \
  --seats 99 \
  --expires 2028-12-31 \
  --features all \
  -o licenses/team/aristide.lic

python tools/generate_license.py \
  --client "KARIANA Dev — [Team Member Name]" \
  --type internal_dev \
  --seats 99 \
  --expires 2028-12-31 \
  --features all \
  -o licenses/team/[name].lic

Step 3: Place team licenses at the auto-discovery path

Each team member does this on their machine:

# Windows (PowerShell):
mkdir -Force "$env:APPDATA\KARIANA"
copy licenses/team/aristide.lic "$env:APPDATA\KARIANA\license.lic"

# Mac/Linux:
mkdir -p ~/.config/kariana
cp licenses/team/yourname.lic ~/.config/kariana/license.lic

After this, opening Unreal Engine starts the daemon and it finds the license automatically. No configuration in UE required.

Step 4: Verify the daemon finds the license

python Content/Python/kariana_agent_daemon.py

Expected first JSON output line: {"type": "license_valid", "client": "KARIANA Dev — ...", ...}

Step 5: Generate client pre-alpha licenses

For each of the ~10 pre-alpha clients:

python tools/generate_license.py \
  --client "Acme Studios" \
  --type pre_alpha_enterprise \
  --seats 5 \
  --expires 2027-06-30 \
  --features all \
  -o licenses/clients/acme-studios.lic

Email licenses/clients/acme-studios.lic to the client with installation instructions (see below).

Client installation instructions (include in the email):

1. Save the attached license.lic file
2. Place it at: C:\Users\<YourName>\AppData\Roaming\KARIANA\license.lic
   (Create the KARIANA folder if it doesn't exist)
3. Open Unreal Engine — KARIANA will activate automatically

If you see a license error in the KARIANA panel, check the file path above.
For help: home@kariana.ai

Step 6: Commit .gitignore update only (licenses stay off git)

git add .gitignore
git commit -m "chore: ensure generated license files are excluded from source control"

docs.title: Security Properties of This Design
docs.text: Threat How It's Handled Client shares plugin with non-client License is client-named and unique — KARIANA can identify who leaked it Client forges a license Ed25519: impossible without the private key, which only KARIANA holds Client extracts HMAC key from binary No HMAC key. Extracting the embedded public key from the .pyd only gives the verifier half — useless for creating signatures Client reverse-engineers methodology Cython-compiled .pyd requires disassembly with IDA/Ghidra — significantly raises the bar for a pre-alpha client Private key lost Restore from 1Password. Rotation requires new keypair + reissue all licenses (plan this ahead of time) Client changes machines License is NOT hardware-bound — they copy the .lic file to the new machine. No friction.

docs.title: Known Risks & Mitigations
docs.text: Risk Impact Mitigation UE 5.7 ships a different CPython ABI than standard 3.11 .pyd fails to load inside UE Test loading one .pyd inside UE before first client delivery — if broken, compile inside UE's own Python FastMCP decorators behave differently when compiled mcp_server.py tools not registered Smoke test catches import errors; if @mcp.tool() fails, keep mcp_server.py as a thin .py launcher that imports the compiled module cryptography library not available in UE's Python licensing/core.py fails to import Installer must run pip install cryptography into UE's embedded Python — verify this in the installer script Intel Mac clients (if any) ARM .so won't load Add macos-13 runner to CI matrix for x86 build; ask clients their architecture Private key rotation (if key is ever compromised) Must reissue all licenses Generate new keypair, recompile plugin with new public key, reissue all client licenses — plan a comms process for this

docs.title: KARIANA Assistant Window UI Redesign
docs.text:
For Claude: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

Goal: Redesign the KARIANA Assistant Window to match the Figma design (file key JG6nAlfSv1UgLXqsmU6Mwa), covering header, toolbar, welcome screen, chat messages, mode selector, input, history panel, log bar, model dropdown, and a new options/choice cards feature.

Architecture: Modify existing Slate widgets in Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/. The layout restructure is primarily in SKarianaChatPanel::Construct() and BuildHeader(). Most changes are visual/layout — widget classes stay the same, but their internal construction changes. One new widget class (SKarianaChoiceCards) is added for the options/choice feature.

Tech Stack: Unreal Engine 5.7 Slate UI (C++), KarianaBrand color system, FKarianaMarkdownStyle brushes.

Figma Reference: https://www.figma.com/design/JG6nAlfSv1UgLXqsmU6Mwa/KARIANA-UI — use get_screenshot with specific node IDs when visual reference is needed during implementation.

Verification: After each task, build in Rider (Build > Build Solution) and visually verify in UE editor. No automated UI tests exist for Slate widgets.

docs.title: Task 1: Header Redesign
docs.text:
Goal: Replace the current header (status dot + "KARIANA" + connection text + model selector + settings/history buttons) with the Figma design: hamburger menu left | "Claude - Opus 4.5" centered with chevron | provider label + status dot right.

Figma reference: Node 23:530 (TOP BAR component), visible in MAIN screenshot node 6:2.

docs.title: Step 1: Redesign BuildHeader()
docs.text:
Replace the current BuildHeader() method. The new header is a single horizontal row:

[≡ hamburger] ---- [Model Name ∨] ---- [Provider Status●]

Left: Hamburger button (≡) that triggers OnToggleHistory() (replaces the old history toggle button).

Center: Model display text + chevron-down icon. Clicking opens model selector dropdown (Task 9). Use existing ModelComboBox but restyle it as a flat text button with chevron.

Right: Provider label (e.g. "AWS", "Claude", "Local") + colored status dot. The provider comes from Proxy->GetCurrentProvider() or settings. The status dot uses existing StatusConnected/StatusWarning/StatusError colors based on connection state.

Implementation notes: - Remove the old enable checkbox (EnableCheckBox), "KARIANA" brand label, clear chat button, and settings button from the header — these move to the toolbar (Task 2) - Header height: ~40px, dark background (BgBase or BgRaised) - Hamburger icon: Use text "≡" (U+2261) in a 24x24 button, or create a simple 3-line icon via FSlateBrush - Status dot: 8x8 rounded ellipse, colored by connection state - Provider label: Small text (TextSecondary, 9pt), right-aligned before status dot

docs.title: Step 2: Add provider/status tracking members
docs.text:
Add to SKarianaChatPanel.h: - TSharedPtr<STextBlock> ProviderLabel — displays "AWS", "Claude", etc. - TSharedPtr<SBorder> StatusDot — colored connection indicator - FText GetProviderDisplayText() const — returns current provider name - FSlateColor GetStatusDotColor() const — returns color based on bridge connection state

The status dot color logic: - Green (StatusConnected): Bridge exists and IsProcessReady() returns true - Yellow (StatusWarning): Bridge exists but not ready (connecting/initializing) - Red (StatusError): No bridge or bridge reports disconnected

docs.title: Step 3: Remove old header elements
docs.text: Remove from BuildHeader(): - The EnableCheckBox (toggle assistant on/off) — consider keeping it accessible elsewhere or removing entirely if the Figma doesn't show it - The "KARIANA" brand text - The SettingsButton — moves to toolbar - The ToggleHistoryButton — replaced by hamburger - The ClearChatButton — moves to toolbar or removed (New Chat button in toolbar serves same purpose)

docs.title: Step 4: Build and verify
docs.text: Build in Rider. Open KARIANA Assistant panel in UE. Verify: - Hamburger button visible on left, opens/closes history - Model name centered with chevron - Provider + status dot on right, correct color

docs.title: Step 1: Build toolbar in Construct()
docs.text:
Add a new BuildToolbar() method that returns TSharedRef<SWidget>. Insert it in the main vertical layout between the header and the content area.

Layout (SHorizontalBox, 32px height, BgRaised background):

[+NewChat] [↶Undo] [↷Redo] |separator| [⊙Rec] |separator| ---spacer--- [🐛BugReport] [📊Dashboard] [⚙Settings]

Button actions: - New Chat (+): Calls existing OnNewChat() — clears session, starts fresh conversation - Undo (↶): Calls existing OnConversationUndoClicked() - Redo (↷): Calls existing OnConversationRedoClicked(). Note: the Figma shows the redo icon as a mirrored undo icon - Record (⊙): Calls existing recording widget toggle. Use SKarianaRecordingWidget or its delegate - Bug Report (🐛): Opens bug report URL or dialog. Can use FPlatformProcess::LaunchURL() to open GitHub issues page - Dashboard (📊): Opens Gradio admin dashboard URL (http://localhost:7860) via FPlatformProcess::LaunchURL() - Settings (⚙): Opens Project Settings to KARIANA Assistant section via FModuleManager::LoadModuleChecked<ISettingsModule>("Settings").ShowViewer("Project", "KARIANA", "Assistant")

Separators: 1px wide vertical lines, BorderSubtle color, ~28px tall (centered in 32px row)

docs.title: Step 2: Style toolbar buttons
docs.text:
Each button is 32x32, transparent background, icon centered. Use FAppStyle or custom FSlateBrush icons where available. For icons not available as brushes, use Unicode text characters as placeholder: - + for New Chat - ↶ / ↷ for Undo/Redo (or use existing undo icon instances referenced in Figma) - ⊙ for Record - Existing Slate icons for Settings (FAppStyle::GetBrush("Icons.Settings"))

Buttons should have hover highlight (BgHover) and be disabled/dimmed when not applicable (e.g., Undo disabled when !IsConversationUndoEnabled()).

// In header:
TSharedPtr<SButton> ActionButton;
