docs.title: Task 10: Choice Cards Widget (New Feature)
docs.text:
Goal: Build a new interactive choice cards system where the AI can present multiple-choice options (A/B/C) with titles, descriptions, and a text input alternative.

Figma reference: Nodes 23:571 (MAIN - OPTIONS, choice state) and 23:678 (expanded choice with descriptions). Shows lettered option cards + "Type your answer" input.

Files: - Create: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaChoiceCards.h - Create: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaChoiceCards.cpp - Modify: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaUserInputPrompt.h - Modify: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaUserInputPrompt.cpp - Modify: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaChatPanel.cpp (to use new widget)

docs.title: Step 1: Define choice card data
docs.text:
struct FKarianaChoiceCard {
    FString Letter;       // "A", "B", "C", etc.
    FString Title;        // "Static maze"
    FString Description;  // "A fixed maze built from static mesh and walls"
};

docs.title: Step 2: Create SKarianaChoiceCards widget
docs.text:
class SKarianaChoiceCards : public SCompoundWidget
{
    SLATE_BEGIN_ARGS(SKarianaChoiceCards) {}
        SLATE_ARGUMENT(FString, QuestionText)      // "What type of maze..."
        SLATE_ARGUMENT(TArray<FKarianaChoiceCard>, Choices)
        SLATE_ARGUMENT(bool, bAllowCustomInput)    // show "Type your answer" box
        SLATE_EVENT(FOnChoiceSelected, OnChoiceSelected)  // fires (FString ChoiceId)
    SLATE_END_ARGS()
};

Layout from Figma:

● KARIANA is thinking

Choose an option:
What type of maze are you looking for to build?

┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [A]  Static maze                           │
│      A fixed maze built from static mesh   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [B]  Procedural Maze                       │
│      A fixed maze built from static mesh   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [C]  Gameplay Maze                         │
│      A fixed maze built from static mesh   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────┘

[Type your answer                         ↑]

Card styling: - Each card: rounded rectangle (BgElevated), full width, ~39px height - Left: Letter badge — rounded square (BgRaised or darker), 31x31, centered letter text (bold, 14pt) - Right of badge: Title (bold, 14pt) + Description (regular, 10pt, TextSecondary) stacked vertically - Cards clickable — clicking fires OnChoiceSelected with the letter/ID - Hover highlight on cards

"Type your answer" input: - Rounded rectangle, same width as cards - Placeholder text: "Type your answer" - Send button (↑) on the right inside the input - Submitting fires OnChoiceSelected with the typed text

docs.title: Step 3: Integrate with UserInputPrompt
docs.text:
When EKarianaUserInputType::Choice is received and the choices have descriptions, use SKarianaChoiceCards instead of the current button-based layout in SKarianaUserInputPrompt.

In SKarianaUserInputPrompt::BuildActionButtons(): 

if (Request.Type == EKarianaUserInputType::Choice && HasDescriptions(Request.Choices))
{
    // Use new SKarianaChoiceCards
    return SNew(SKarianaChoiceCards)
        .QuestionText(Request.Prompt)
        .Choices(ConvertToChoiceCards(Request.Choices))
        .bAllowCustomInput(Request.bAllowCustomInput)
        .OnChoiceSelected(this, &SKarianaUserInputPrompt::OnChoiceClicked);
}
// else: use existing button layout for simple choices

docs.title: Step 4: Handle choice response
docs.text: When a card is clicked: 1. Disable all cards (grey out, non-interactive) 2. Highlight the selected card 3. Fire OnResponseDelegate with the choice letter/ID 4. Show "You selected: {choice}" confirmation text

docs.title: Step 5: Build and verify
docs.text: Build. Test by triggering a user question from the daemon with EKarianaUserInputType::Choice and providing choices with descriptions. Verify: - Cards display with letter badges - Clicking a card selects it and sends response - "Type your answer" input works as alternative - Cards disable after selection

docs.title: Task 11: Plan Approval UI
docs.text:
Goal: Enhance the plan approval flow for Validate mode to match the Figma design: "Approve Plan?" with structured options (Execute in CREATE / Stay in VALIDATE / Modify...).

Figma reference: Node 31:77 (MAIN - OPTIONS, plan approval state). Shows "Approve Plan?" header with Execute/Stay/Modify options.

Files: - Modify: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaUserInputPrompt.h - Modify: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaUserInputPrompt.cpp - Possibly modify: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaChatPanel.cpp (ExitPlanMode handler)

docs.title: Step 1: Redesign PlanApproval layout
docs.text:
When EKarianaUserInputType::PlanApproval is received, use the choice cards pattern:

● KARIANA is thinking

Approve Plan?
This is what I would do:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [A]  Execute in CREATE                     │
│      Approve plan and run with auto-approve│
└────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [B]  Stay in VALIDATE                      │
│      Continue with manual approval per step│
└────────────────────────────────────────────┘

[Modify...                                ↑]

Key differences from generic choice cards: - "Modify..." is a text input (not a card) — lets the user type modifications to the plan - The plan context (what the AI plans to do) should be shown above the options (collapsible) - "Execute in CREATE" should switch mode to Create and proceed - "Stay in VALIDATE" should keep current mode and proceed

docs.title: Step 2: Wire mode switching
docs.text:
When "Execute in CREATE" is selected: 1. Fire OnResponseDelegate with "execute" or similar 2. Call OnModeChanged(EKarianaAssistantMode::BypassPermissions) to switch to Create mode 3. Continue execution

When "Stay in VALIDATE" is selected: 1. Fire OnResponseDelegate with "approve" or similar 2. Keep current mode 3. Continue execution

When "Modify..." text is submitted: 1. Fire OnResponseDelegate with the modification text 2. The AI will revise the plan and re-present

docs.title: Step 3: Reuse SKarianaChoiceCards
docs.text: This can reuse the SKarianaChoiceCards widget from Task 10, with the "Modify..." option as the custom input field. The only special handling is the mode switch on "Execute in CREATE".

docs.title: Step 4: Build and verify
docs.text: Build. Test by entering Validate mode and submitting a complex prompt. When the AI presents a plan for approval, verify the new UI appears with the correct options.

docs.title: Risk Notes
docs.text:
1. Standard mode removal: The daemon may send Standard as default mode. Ensure the proxy/bridge handles receiving Standard gracefully (map it to Validate).
  2. BuildHeader() is large: The current BuildHeader() and Construct() methods are complex. Make incremental changes and compile frequently.
  3. History overlay z-order: Using SOverlay requires careful z-ordering to ensure the history panel covers all other widgets.
  4. Choice cards daemon integration: The daemon needs to send structured choices (with descriptions) for the cards to populate. Verify the FKarianaUserInputRequest struct supports multi-line descriptions per choice.
  5. Font scaling: After removing bubbles and avatars, verify SetFontScale() still works correctly on the simplified message layout.
  6. Theme compatibility: All new brushes/colors should use KarianaBrand:: namespace to remain theme-compatible.

docs.title: UI Architecture Refactor — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For Claude: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

Goal: Restructure the Kariana Assistant UI code so that any AI session can quickly find "where do I change X?" — without visual/UX changes.

Architecture: Central ThemeManager singleton owns all 72+ colors in a TMap, loaded from JSON with C++ fallback defaults. Semantic tokens map role names to raw colors. Three focused StyleSets replace one monolithic set. Layout constants replace ~195 magic numbers. Sub-controllers decompose the panel hub.

Tech Stack: UE5.7 Slate, C++, JSON (themes.json), FSlateStyleSet, FSlateStyleRegistry

Reference docs: docs/internal/kariana-ui-architecture/ (14 files), docs/plans/ui-refactor/ (6 phase files)

Module: UnrealAssistantIntegration (Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/)

Build/test: User builds in Rider, reloads UE. No automated unit tests for Slate widgets — verification is compile + visual inspection in the running editor.

Step 1: Write the header

// KarianaThemeManager.h
#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

DECLARE_MULTICAST_DELEGATE(FOnKarianaThemeChanged);

class UNREALASSISTANTINTEGRATION_API FKarianaThemeManager
{
public:
    static FKarianaThemeManager& Get();

    void Initialize();
    void Shutdown();

    // Load a theme by name from Content/Config/themes.json
    void LoadTheme(const FString& ThemeName);

    // Get a raw color by key (e.g., "Pink", "BgBase")
    FLinearColor GetColor(FName Key) const;

    // Get a semantic token (e.g., "AccentPrimary") — resolves alias
    FLinearColor GetToken(FName TokenName) const;

    // Theme change notification
    FOnKarianaThemeChanged OnThemeChanged;

    // Current theme name
    FString GetCurrentThemeName() const { return CurrentThemeName; }

private:
    FKarianaThemeManager() = default;

    void PopulateDefaults();
    void PopulateTokenDefaults();
    void LoadJsonOverlay(const FString& ThemeName);

    TMap<FName, FLinearColor> Colors;
    TMap<FName, FName> TokenAliases; // token name -> color key
    FString CurrentThemeName;
    bool bInitialized = false;
};

Step 2: Write the implementation

// KarianaThemeManager.cpp
#include "Theme/KarianaThemeManager.h"

FKarianaThemeManager& FKarianaThemeManager::Get()

void FKarianaThemeManager::Initialize()
{

    PopulateDefaults();
    PopulateTokenDefaults();

    TokenAliases.Empty();

void FKarianaThemeManager::LoadTheme(const FString& ThemeName)
{
    CurrentThemeName = ThemeName;

    // Resolve plugin root and find themes.json
    FString PluginRoot;
    TSharedPtr<IPlugin> Plugin = IPluginManager::Get().FindPlugin(TEXT("KARIANA"));
    if (Plugin.IsValid())
    {
        PluginRoot = Plugin->GetBaseDir();
    }

    FString JsonPath = FPaths::Combine(PluginRoot, TEXT("Content/Config/themes.json"));

    FString JsonString;
    if (!FFileHelper::LoadFileToString(JsonString, *JsonPath))
    {
        UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("KarianaThemeManager: themes.json not found at %s — using defaults"), *JsonPath);
        return;
    }

    TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> RootObject;
    TSharedRef<TJsonReader<>> Reader = TJsonReaderFactory<>::Create(JsonString);
    if (!FJsonSerializer::Deserialize(Reader, RootObject) || !RootObject.IsValid())
    {
        UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("KarianaThemeManager: Failed to parse themes.json — using defaults"));
        return;
    }

    const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject>* ThemeObject;
    if (!RootObject->TryGetObjectField(ThemeName, ThemeObject))
    {
        UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("KarianaThemeManager: Theme '%s' not found — using defaults"), *ThemeName);
        return;
    }

    for (const auto& Pair : (*ThemeObject)->Values)
    {
        const TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>>* ArrayValue;
        if (Pair.Value->TryGetArray(ArrayValue) && ArrayValue->Num() >= 3)
        {
            float R = (*ArrayValue)[0]->AsNumber();
            float G = (*ArrayValue)[1]->AsNumber();
            float B = (*ArrayValue)[2]->AsNumber();
            float A = ArrayValue->Num() >= 4 ? (*ArrayValue)[3]->AsNumber() : 1.0f;
            Colors.Add(FName(*Pair.Key), FLinearColor(R, G, B, A));
        }
    }

    UE_LOG(LogTemp, Log, TEXT("KarianaThemeManager: Loaded theme '%s' (%d colors)"), *ThemeName, Colors.Num());
}

FLinearColor FKarianaThemeManager::GetColor(FName Key) const
{
    const FLinearColor* Found = Colors.Find(Key);
    if (Found)
    {
        return *Found;
    }
    UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("KarianaThemeManager: Color '%s' not found"), *Key.ToString());
    return FLinearColor(1.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f); // Magenta = missing color
}

FLinearColor FKarianaThemeManager::GetToken(FName TokenName) const
{
    const FName* ColorKey = TokenAliases.Find(TokenName);
    if (ColorKey)
    {
        return GetColor(*ColorKey);
    }
    // Fall back to direct color lookup
    return GetColor(TokenName);
}

Task 5.8: Create FKarianaUIState shared observable
docs.text:
Files: - Create: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Public/Theme/KarianaUIState.h - Modify: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaChatPanel.h - Modify: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaChatPanel.cpp

Problem: bIsProcessing is duplicated in SKarianaChatInput, SKarianaContextBar, and SKarianaStatusOverlay (orphaned). The panel pushes SetProcessing() to each child manually from OnStreamingStateChanged. Easy to miss a widget, state can drift.

Step 1: Create the shared state struct

// KarianaUIState.h
#pragma once
#include "CoreMinimal.h"

DECLARE_MULTICAST_DELEGATE(FOnKarianaUIStateChanged);

/**
 * Shared observable UI state. Widgets subscribe to OnChanged
 * instead of being push-updated by the panel.
 */
struct UNREALASSISTANTINTEGRATION_API FKarianaUIState
{
    // Processing
    bool bIsProcessing = false;
    bool bIsStreaming = false;

    // Connection
    bool bIsConnected = false;
    bool bIsConnecting = false;

    // Mode
    EKarianaAssistantMode CurrentMode = EKarianaAssistantMode::Validate;

    // Notification delegate
    FOnKarianaUIStateChanged OnChanged;

    void SetProcessing(bool bNewProcessing)
    {
        if (bIsProcessing != bNewProcessing)
        {
            bIsProcessing = bNewProcessing;
            OnChanged.Broadcast();
        }
    }

    void SetStreaming(bool bNewStreaming)
    {
        if (bIsStreaming != bNewStreaming)
        {
            bIsStreaming = bNewStreaming;
            OnChanged.Broadcast();
        }
    }

    void SetConnected(bool bConnected, bool bConnecting_)
    {
        if (bIsConnected != bConnected || bIsConnecting != bConnecting_)
        {
            bIsConnected = bConnected;
            bIsConnecting = bConnecting_;
            OnChanged.Broadcast();
        }
    }
};

Step 2: Add FKarianaUIState to SKarianaChatPanel

In SKarianaChatPanel.h, add: 

TSharedPtr<FKarianaUIState> UIState;

// BEFORE:

docs.title: Plugin Auto-Update Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Replace the current manual "open download page" flow with a real auto-update — background download, integrity verify, restart prompt, in-place swap — scoped narrowly enough to be safe in alpha.

Architecture: Project-install-only auto-update on the GitHub-zip alpha channel. Engine installs, Marketplace installs, and KARIANA-installer-managed installs detect themselves and fall back to the existing manual flow. Cross-platform file swap is performed by an external bootstrapper binary that runs after the editor exits, reads a swap-manifest written by the editor, performs the swap atomically, optionally relaunches the editor, and self-deletes. This avoids the Windows-only "rename-locked-DLL" trick and eliminates the half-installed failure mode.

Tech Stack: UE 5.7 C++ (HttpModule, FZipFileFunctions where available else third-party miniz, IPluginManager, FUnrealEdMisc::RestartEditor), Slate (FNotificationInfo, banner widget), Go or Rust for the bootstrapper binary (single static cross-platform binary, no runtime deps), GitHub Actions for bootstrapper releases. Manifest format already defined: {version, downloadUrl, sha256} from app.kariana.ai/api/version.

Issue tracker: GitHub INGIPSA/KARIANA #465 (in-place extraction).

Scope decisions / non-goals: - ❌ Engine plugin auto-update (Engine/Plugins/Marketplace/KARIANA/) → defer to manual installer; UAC + Marketplace conflict + shared-engine teammate breakage make it not worth alpha-cycle complexity. - ❌ Marketplace channel → Epic Launcher owns updates; we must detect and stand down. - ❌ Source-built engine recompile → only DLL swap, never rebuild from source. - ❌ Multi-version skip migration logic → first auto-update release supports N→N+1 only; multi-skip falls back to manual. - ❌ Code signing of the new zip → SHA256 only in v1; Authenticode/notarization comes in a follow-up.

// Copyright 2024 KARIANA. All Rights Reserved.
#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

UENUM()
enum class EKarianaInstallLocation : uint8
{
    Unknown,
    ProjectPlugins,        // <Project>/Plugins/KARIANA/ — auto-updatable
    EngineMarketplace,     // <Engine>/Plugins/Marketplace/KARIANA/ — Epic Launcher owns
    EngineCustom,          // <Engine>/Plugins/KARIANA/ on a source build — manual
    SymlinkedDev,          // The plugin dir is a symlink (developer mode) — never touch
};

UENUM()
enum class EKarianaUpdateChannel : uint8
{
    Unknown,
    AlphaZip,              // GitHub release zip — our auto-update target
    Marketplace,           // Epic Marketplace — defer
    InstallerManaged,      // KARIANA-installer drop — defer to installer
};

struct UNREALASSISTANTINTEGRATION_API FKarianaInstallContext
{
    EKarianaInstallLocation Location = EKarianaInstallLocation::Unknown;
    EKarianaUpdateChannel   Channel  = EKarianaUpdateChannel::Unknown;
    FString PluginBaseDir;             // absolute path to Plugins/KARIANA/
    FString PluginParentDir;           // dir we'd extract into (same as BaseDir's parent)
    bool    bWritableWithoutElevation = false;
    bool    bSiblingEditorRunning     = false;  // another UE editor has plugin loaded

    static FKarianaInstallContext Detect();
    bool CanAutoUpdate(FString& OutReason) const;  // single decision point
};

// Copyright 2024 KARIANA. All Rights Reserved.
#include "Updates/KarianaInstallContext.h"
#include "Interfaces/IPluginManager.h"
#include "Misc/Paths.h"
#include "Misc/FileHelper.h"
#include "HAL/PlatformFileManager.h"
#include "GenericPlatform/GenericPlatformFile.h"

namespace
{
    bool IsSymlink(const FString& Path)
    {
    #if PLATFORM_WINDOWS
        const DWORD Attrs = ::GetFileAttributesW(*Path);
        return (Attrs != INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES) && (Attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT);
    #else
        struct stat St{};
        return lstat(TCHAR_TO_UTF8(*Path), &St) == 0 && S_ISLNK(St.st_mode);
    #endif
    }

    bool IsWritable(const FString& Dir)
    {
        const FString Probe = FPaths::Combine(Dir, TEXT(".kariana-write-probe"));
        if (FFileHelper::SaveStringToFile(TEXT("ok"), *Probe))
        {
            IFileManager::Get().Delete(*Probe);
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}

FKarianaInstallContext FKarianaInstallContext::Detect()
{
    FKarianaInstallContext Ctx;

    TSharedPtr<IPlugin> Plugin = IPluginManager::Get().FindPlugin(TEXT("KARIANA"));
    if (!Plugin.IsValid())
    {
        return Ctx;  // Location = Unknown
    }

    Ctx.PluginBaseDir   = FPaths::ConvertRelativePathToFull(Plugin->GetBaseDir());
    Ctx.PluginParentDir = FPaths::GetPath(Ctx.PluginBaseDir);

    if (IsSymlink(Ctx.PluginBaseDir))
    {
        Ctx.Location = EKarianaInstallLocation::SymlinkedDev;
        return Ctx;
    }

    const FString ProjectPlugins = FPaths::ConvertRelativePathToFull(FPaths::ProjectPluginsDir());
    const FString EnginePlugins  = FPaths::ConvertRelativePathToFull(FPaths::EnginePluginsDir());
    const FString Marketplace    = FPaths::Combine(EnginePlugins, TEXT("Marketplace"));

    if (Ctx.PluginBaseDir.StartsWith(ProjectPlugins))
    {
        Ctx.Location = EKarianaInstallLocation::ProjectPlugins;
    }
    else if (Ctx.PluginBaseDir.StartsWith(Marketplace))
    {
        Ctx.Location = EKarianaInstallLocation::EngineMarketplace;
    }
    else if (Ctx.PluginBaseDir.StartsWith(EnginePlugins))
    {
        Ctx.Location = EKarianaInstallLocation::EngineCustom;
    }

    Ctx.bWritableWithoutElevation = IsWritable(Ctx.PluginParentDir);
    return Ctx;
}

const FString SentinelPath = FPaths::Combine(Ctx.PluginBaseDir, TEXT(".kariana-channel"));
FString SentinelValue;
if (FFileHelper::LoadFileToString(SentinelValue, *SentinelPath))
{
    SentinelValue.TrimStartAndEndInline();
    if (SentinelValue == TEXT("alpha-zip"))      Ctx.Channel = EKarianaUpdateChannel::AlphaZip;
    else if (SentinelValue == TEXT("marketplace")) Ctx.Channel = EKarianaUpdateChannel::Marketplace;
    else if (SentinelValue == TEXT("installer"))   Ctx.Channel = EKarianaUpdateChannel::InstallerManaged;
}
// Heuristic fallback: marketplace dir => Marketplace; else AlphaZip (current alpha distribution).
if (Ctx.Channel == EKarianaUpdateChannel::Unknown)
{
    Ctx.Channel = (Ctx.Location == EKarianaInstallLocation::EngineMarketplace)
        ? EKarianaUpdateChannel::Marketplace
        : EKarianaUpdateChannel::AlphaZip;

docs.title: Task 0.4: Sibling-editor lock detection
docs.text:
Two UE editors running with the plugin loaded → first one auto-updates and the second is now version-mismatched. Lockfile prevents this.

  • Step 1: Write <LocalAppData>/KARiANA/editor.lock on plugin load, delete on shutdown

In KarianaInstallContext.cpp:

static FString GetLockPath()
{
    return FPaths::Combine(
        FPlatformProcess::UserSettingsDir(),
        TEXT("KARiANA"),
        TEXT("editor.lock"));
}

// Called once from UKarianaUpdateChecker::Initialize (next task).
void FKarianaInstallContext::TouchEditorLock()
{
    const FString Path = GetLockPath();
    IFileManager::Get().MakeDirectory(*FPaths::GetPath(Path), true);
    const FString Pid = FString::FromInt(FPlatformProcess::GetCurrentProcessId());
    FFileHelper::SaveStringToFile(Pid + TEXT("\n"), *Path,
        FFileHelper::EEncodingOptions::AutoDetect, &IFileManager::Get(),
        FILEWRITE_Append);
}

Use a process-id list (one PID per line) so multiple editors register/deregister cleanly. Detect() reads the file, prunes dead PIDs (FPlatformProcess::IsApplicationRunning), and sets bSiblingEditorRunning = (LivePids.Num() > 1).

docs.text:
• Step 1: Implement
bool FKarianaInstallContext::CanAutoUpdate(FString& OutReason) const
{
    if (Location == EKarianaInstallLocation::SymlinkedDev)
        { OutReason = TEXT("Plugin directory is a symlink (developer setup) — auto-update disabled."); return false; }
    if (Location == EKarianaInstallLocation::EngineMarketplace || Channel == EKarianaUpdateChannel::Marketplace)
        { OutReason = TEXT("Marketplace install — updates managed by Epic Launcher."); return false; }
    if (Location == EKarianaInstallLocation::EngineCustom)
        { OutReason = TEXT("Engine plugin install — please use the manual installer."); return false; }
    if (Channel == EKarianaUpdateChannel::InstallerManaged)
        { OutReason = TEXT("Installer-managed — please run KARIANA installer."); return false; }
    if (!bWritableWithoutElevation)
        { OutReason = TEXT("Plugin directory is not writable by this user."); return false; }
    if (bSiblingEditorRunning)
        { OutReason = TEXT("Another Unreal Editor is running with KARIANA loaded — close it and try again."); return false; }
    if (Location != EKarianaInstallLocation::ProjectPlugins)
        { OutReason = TEXT("Unsupported install location."); return false; }
    OutReason.Empty();
    return true;
}

enum class EKarianaDownloadStatus : uint8

struct FKarianaDownloadResult
{

    FString  StagedZipPath;        // absolute path under <LocalAppData>/KARiANA/pending-update/
    FString  ExpectedSha256;
    FString  ActualSha256;
    int64    BytesDownloaded = 0;
    int64    BytesTotal      = 0;

DECLARE_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FKarianaOnDownloadProgress, const FKarianaDownloadResult& /*Result*/);

class UNREALASSISTANTINTEGRATION_API FKarianaUpdateDownloader
{
public:

     *  verify SHA256 against `ExpectedSha256`, then transition to Ready. Idempotent: if a verified zip
     *  for this version already exists on disk, transitions straight to Ready without re-downloading. */
    void Start(const FString& Url, const FString& ExpectedSha256, const FString& Version);
    void Cancel();
    const FKarianaDownloadResult& GetResult() const { return Result; }
    FKarianaOnDownloadProgress OnProgress;

private:

    TSharedPtr<IHttpRequest, ESPMode::ThreadSafe> ActiveRequest;
    void OnHttpComplete(FHttpRequestPtr Req, FHttpResponsePtr Resp, bool bConnected, FString TargetPath);
    bool VerifySha256(const FString& Path, const FString& Expected, FString& OutActual) const;

docs.title: Task 1.2: Implement async download with atomic write
docs.text:
Files: - Create: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Updates/KarianaUpdateDownloader.cpp

Key behaviors: - Stream to <staging>/<version>.zip.partial. On complete success, rename to <version>.zip. On failure or cancel, delete partial file. - Disk-space check before starting: require 2 * Content-Length (download + extraction headroom). If unknown, require 500 MB free as conservative default. Use FPlatformMisc::GetDiskSpace. - Cap download size to 500 MB (sanity): refuse if Content-Length > limit. - Idempotency: if <version>.zip already exists with matching SHA256, skip download. - On HTTP redirect: UE's FHttpModule does not follow 3xx by default. Inspect Resp->GetHeader(TEXT("Location")) and re-issue (cap at 3 redirects to avoid loops).

  • Step 1: Implement Start() with idempotency check
#include "Updates/KarianaUpdateDownloader.h"
#include "HttpModule.h"
#include "Interfaces/IHttpResponse.h"
#include "Misc/Paths.h"
#include "Misc/FileHelper.h"
#include "Misc/SecureHash.h"
#include "HAL/PlatformFileManager.h"

static FString GetStagingDir()
{
    return FPaths::Combine(FPlatformProcess::UserSettingsDir(), TEXT("KARiANA"), TEXT("pending-update"));
}

void FKarianaUpdateDownloader::Start(const FString& Url, const FString& ExpectedSha256, const FString& Version)
{
    Result = FKarianaDownloadResult{};
    Result.ExpectedSha256 = ExpectedSha256.ToLower();
    const FString Dir = GetStagingDir();
    IFileManager::Get().MakeDirectory(*Dir, /*Tree=*/true);
    const FString FinalPath = FPaths::Combine(Dir, FString::Printf(TEXT("%s.zip"), *Version));

    // Idempotency: re-use a prior verified download.
    FString Actual;
    if (FPaths::FileExists(FinalPath) && VerifySha256(FinalPath, Result.ExpectedSha256, Actual))
    {
        Result.Status = EKarianaDownloadStatus::Ready;
        Result.StagedZipPath = FinalPath;
        Result.ActualSha256 = Actual;
        OnProgress.Broadcast(Result);
        return;
    }
    IFileManager::Get().Delete(*FinalPath, /*RequireExists=*/false);

    // Disk-space guard: require >=500 MB free.
    uint64 TotalBytes = 0, FreeBytes = 0;
    FPlatformMisc::GetDiskTotalAndFreeSpace(Dir, TotalBytes, FreeBytes);
    if (FreeBytes < 500ull * 1024 * 1024)
    {
        Result.Status = EKarianaDownloadStatus::Failed;
        Result.FailureReason = TEXT("Less than 500 MB free in staging dir.");
        OnProgress.Broadcast(Result);
        return;
    }

    Result.Status = EKarianaDownloadStatus::InProgress;
    OnProgress.Broadcast(Result);

    const FString PartialPath = FinalPath + TEXT(".partial");
    ActiveRequest = FHttpModule::Get().CreateRequest();
    ActiveRequest->SetURL(Url);
    ActiveRequest->SetVerb(TEXT("GET"));
    ActiveRequest->SetHeader(TEXT("User-Agent"), TEXT("KARIANA-UE-Updater/1"));
    ActiveRequest->OnRequestProgress().BindLambda(
        [this](FHttpRequestPtr Req, int32 Sent, int32 Recv)
        {
            Result.BytesDownloaded = Recv;
            Result.BytesTotal      = Req->GetResponse().IsValid() ? Req->GetResponse()->GetContentLength() : 0;
            OnProgress.Broadcast(Result);
        });
    ActiveRequest->OnProcessRequestComplete().BindLambda(
        [this, PartialPath, FinalPath](FHttpRequestPtr Req, FHttpResponsePtr Resp, bool bOk)
        {
            this->OnHttpComplete(Req, Resp, bOk, FinalPath);
        });
    ActiveRequest->ProcessRequest();
}
  • Step 2: Implement OnHttpComplete (rename partial → final, verify, broadcast)
void FKarianaUpdateDownloader::OnHttpComplete(FHttpRequestPtr Req, FHttpResponsePtr Resp, bool bConnected, FString FinalPath)
{
    if (!bConnected || !Resp.IsValid() || Resp->GetResponseCode() / 100 != 2)
    {
        Result.Status = EKarianaDownloadStatus::Failed;
        Result.FailureReason = FString::Printf(TEXT("HTTP failure (code=%d)"),
            Resp.IsValid() ? Resp->GetResponseCode() : 0);
        OnProgress.Broadcast(Result);
        return;
    }

    // Write payload atomically: bytes -> .partial -> rename to final.
    const TArray<uint8>& Payload = Resp->GetContent();
    const FString PartialPath = FinalPath + TEXT(".partial");
    if (!FFileHelper::SaveArrayToFile(Payload, *PartialPath))
    {
        Result.Status = EKarianaDownloadStatus::Failed;
        Result.FailureReason = TEXT("Could not write zip to staging dir.");
        OnProgress.Broadcast(Result);
        return;
    }

    Result.Status = EKarianaDownloadStatus::Verifying;
    OnProgress.Broadcast(Result);

    FString Actual;
    if (!VerifySha256(PartialPath, Result.ExpectedSha256, Actual))
    {
        Result.ActualSha256 = Actual;
        Result.Status = EKarianaDownloadStatus::Failed;
        Result.FailureReason = FString::Printf(TEXT("SHA256 mismatch (expected=%s actual=%s)"),
            *Result.ExpectedSha256, *Actual);
        IFileManager::Get().Delete(*PartialPath);
        OnProgress.Broadcast(Result);
        return;
    }

    if (!IFileManager::Get().Move(*FinalPath, *PartialPath, /*bReplace=*/true))
    {
        Result.Status = EKarianaDownloadStatus::Failed;
        Result.FailureReason = TEXT("Could not finalize staged zip.");
        OnProgress.Broadcast(Result);
        return;
    }

    Result.StagedZipPath = FinalPath;
    Result.ActualSha256 = Actual;
    Result.Status = EKarianaDownloadStatus::Ready;
    OnProgress.Broadcast(Result);
}

bool FKarianaUpdateDownloader::VerifySha256(const FString& Path, const FString& Expected, FString& OutActual) const
{
    TArray<uint8> Bytes;
    if (!FFileHelper::LoadFileToArray(Bytes, *Path)) return false;
    FSHAHash Hash;
    FSHA1::HashBuffer(Bytes.GetData(), Bytes.Num(), Hash.Hash);  // SHA-1, NOT SHA-256
    // NOTE: UE's FSHA1 is SHA-1; for SHA-256 use FSHA256 (UE 5.3+) or fall back to OpenSSL.
    // See note in step 3 below — wire FSHA256.
    OutActual = Hash.ToString().ToLower();
    return OutActual == Expected;
}
  • Step 3: Replace SHA-1 with SHA-256

UE 5.3+ ships FSHA256Hasher (header Misc/SecureHash.h and Hash/Sha256.h depending on engine version). Replace the FSHA1::HashBuffer call with the SHA-256 equivalent:

#include "Hash/Sha256.h"  // verify path on UE 5.7
// ...
FSha256 Hasher;
Hasher.Update(Bytes.GetData(), Bytes.Num());
FSha256Hash Out = Hasher.Finalize();
OutActual = BytesToHex(Out.Hash, sizeof(Out.Hash)).ToLower();

If Hash/Sha256.h is not available in 5.7, fall back to the OpenSSL EVP_* API (UE bundles OpenSSL via OpenSSL module — add it to PrivateDependencyModuleNames in UnrealAssistantIntegration.Build.cs).

In a separate terminal:

echo "test payload" > test.zip
sha256sum test.zip   # copy the hash
python3 -m http.server 8080

Hardcode Url=http://localhost:8080/test.zip, ExpectedSha256=<hash>, Version=test-0.0.1 in a temp scratch button on the settings panel; verify Result.StagedZipPath exists and re-running short-circuits to Ready (idempotent).

docs.text:
Files: - Create in plugin: Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Public/Updates/KarianaSwapManifest.h - Create in bootstrapper repo: bootstrapper/internal/manifest/manifest.go

Both sides MUST stay in sync. Single canonical doc: docs/internal/swap-manifest-v1.md (next step).

  • Step 1: Write the doc
# Swap Manifest v1

Written by editor to `<LocalAppData>/KARiANA/swap-manifest.json` immediately
before exiting. Read by the bootstrapper as its single source of truth.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "editor_pid": 12345,
  "plugin_dir": "C:/Users/.../MyProject/Plugins/KARIANA",
  "staged_zip": "C:/Users/.../KARiANA/pending-update/0.10.4.zip",
  "expected_sha256": "abc123...",
  "rename_suffix": ".old-20260430-153012",
  "relaunch": {
    "enabled": true,
    "executable": "C:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.7/Engine/Binaries/Win64/UnrealEditor.exe",
    "args": ["C:/path/to/MyProject.uproject"],
    "working_dir": "C:/path/to"
  },
  "log_path": "C:/Users/.../KARiANA/bootstrapper.log",
  "rollback_marker": "C:/Users/.../KARiANA/last-good-version.txt"
}

Bootstrapper steps in order: 1. Wait up to 30 s for editor_pid to exit (poll kill -0 / OpenProcess). 2. Re-verify staged_zip SHA256 matches expected_sha256. Abort if not. 3. Validate zip entries: no absolute paths, no .. segments, no symlinks (zip-slip guard). 4. Read existing plugin_dir, rename every file/dir to <name><rename_suffix>. 5. Extract zip into plugin_dir's parent. 6. Verify the new KARIANA.uplugin exists and is parseable. 7. On success: write rollback_marker with the new version, schedule deletion of .old-* files (next launch the plugin's Initialize cleans them up). 8. On any failure between steps 4 and 6: rename .old-* back to original, delete partial extraction. Write detailed log. 9. If relaunch.enabled: spawn the editor process detached and exit.

package main

import (
    "flag"
    "fmt"
    "os"
    "github.com/INGIPSA/KARIANA-installer/bootstrapper/internal/swap"

func main() {
    manifestPath := flag.String("manifest", "", "Path to swap-manifest.json")

Reject entries where filepath.IsAbs(name) or strings.Contains(name, "..") or header.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0. - crypto/sha256 for re-verify. - os.Rename for atomic file swaps. - exec.Command(...).Start() + cmd.Process.Release() for detached relaunch.

  • Step 1: Header
class UNREALASSISTANTINTEGRATION_API FKarianaUpdateOrchestrator
{
public:
    void BeginInstall(const FKarianaDownloadResult& Download, const FString& LatestVersion);
private:
    bool WriteSwapManifest(const FString& StagedZip, const FString& Sha256, const FString& Version, FString& OutManifestPath);
    bool KillChildProcesses();
    bool SpawnBootstrapper(const FString& ManifestPath);
    void RequestEditorExit();
};
  • Step 2: Implement WriteSwapManifest

Use FJsonObject matching the v1 schema. Write to <LocalAppData>/KARiANA/swap-manifest.json atomically (.partial → rename).

  • Step 3: Implement KillChildProcesses

Known child processes (from CLAUDE.md): - MCP server on port 9877 (started by plugin) — stop via socket "shutdown" command if available, else FPlatformProcess::TerminateProc on tracked PID. - Agent daemon (kariana_agent_daemon.py) — same pattern. - Gradio dashboard (port 7860) — only running if user started it; ignore if not.

Each child should expose its PID via a known file (<LocalAppData>/KARiANA/<service>.pid) that the plugin writes when starting it. If the file doesn't exist, skip silently.

  • Step 4: Implement SpawnBootstrapper
bool FKarianaUpdateOrchestrator::SpawnBootstrapper(const FString& ManifestPath)
{
    const FString PluginBaseDir = IPluginManager::Get().FindPlugin(TEXT("KARIANA"))->GetBaseDir();
    const FString BootstrapperPath = FPaths::Combine(PluginBaseDir,
        TEXT("Binaries"),
        FPlatformProperties::PlatformName(),
        FString::Printf(TEXT("kariana-update%s"),
            PLATFORM_WINDOWS ? TEXT(".exe") : TEXT("")));

    if (!FPaths::FileExists(BootstrapperPath))
    {
        UE_LOG(LogKarianaAssistant, Error, TEXT("[KARIANA] Bootstrapper not found at %s"), *BootstrapperPath);
        return false;
    }

    const FString Args = FString::Printf(TEXT("--manifest \"%s\""), *ManifestPath);
    const bool bDetached = true;
    const bool bHidden   = false;
    uint32 OutProcessID = 0;
    FProcHandle Handle = FPlatformProcess::CreateProc(
        *BootstrapperPath, *Args, bDetached, bHidden, /*ReallyHidden=*/false,
        &OutProcessID, /*PriorityModifier=*/0, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);
    if (!Handle.IsValid()) return false;
    FPlatformProcess::CloseProc(Handle);  // detach
    return true;
}

#include "Editor/UnrealEdEngine.h"

docs.title: Cross-Cutting Concerns Checklist
docs.text:
Verify each before declaring v1 done. Each is a manual test scenario:

  • Engine install (Engine/Plugins/Marketplace/KARIANA/) → banner click opens browser, no swap attempted, log says "Marketplace install — Epic Launcher owns updates."
  • Source-built engine install → falls back to browser flow.
  • Symlinked plugin dir (developer setup) → falls back, log says "symlink — auto-update disabled."
  • Two editors open → second one's banner shows "Another Unreal Editor is running with KARIANA loaded — close it and try again." Restart button disabled.
  • Read-only plugin dir (set chmod -w) → guard fires, browser fallback.
  • Disk has < 500 MB free → download refused with clear error.
  • Network drops mid-download → status goes Failed, partial file deleted, retry works.
  • Corrupted CDN response (mismatched SHA256) → status goes Failed, no swap.
  • HTTP redirect (301/302 from CDN) → followed up to 3 hops, then refused.
  • Marketplace channel sentinel present → declines auto-update even on a project install.
  • Antivirus blocks kariana-update.exe → bootstrapper launch fails cleanly, error logged, banner returns to Ready state.
  • User cancels save-prompt during restart → editor stays open, banner still Ready, user can retry.
  • Bootstrapper crashes mid-swap → next launch detects rollback marker missing, restores from .old-*, plugin loads as OLD version, telemetry reports failure.
  • Same-version reinstall (server reports same version) → banner hidden (existing IsNewerVersion returns false).
  • Downgrade attempt (server reports older) → banner hidden.
  • Skipped version → banner suppressed only for that version, reappears on next bump.
  • Multi-version skip (0.10.3 → 0.10.7) → works the same as N→N+1; no migration ladder in v1.
  • Auth token signing key changed → existing LoadAndVerify fails → user re-prompted to sign in. Token migration deferred to follow-up.
  • macOS Gatekeeper on bootstrapper → notarized binary passes; un-notarized binary fails closed (browser fallback, not silent failure).
  • Linux: AppImage / Flatpak builds untested in v1 → document as unsupported.

docs.title: Rollout Plan
docs.text:
1. Internal dogfood (week 1): Phases 0+1 only. Internal team uses banner+download, manually copies zip. Validate guards.
  2. Closed alpha (week 2): Phase 2 bootstrapper shipped + Phase 3 orchestration. Two specific alpha users explicitly opted into auto-update.
  3. Wider alpha (week 3): Default bAutoDownloadUpdates = true, bAutoInstallUpdates = false. Telemetry from Phase 4 must show < 1 % failure rate before flipping defaults.
  4. Future: Flip bAutoInstallUpdates = true only after 14 d / 95 %+ success on real-world traffic per feedback_live_users_must_not_break.md.

docs.title: Out-of-Scope (Track Separately)
docs.text:
• Code signing of the release zip itself (currently SHA256 only — CDN compromise can substitute a malicious zip with valid hash). Issue: open follow-up chore: sign release zip with cosign / Authenticode.
  • Engine plugin auto-update with UAC elevation. Issue: probably never — leave to manual installer.
  • Multi-version-skip migration ladder. Issue: open follow-up feat: settings/token migration ladder.
  • macOS notarization of bootstrapper. Issue: open in installer repo.
  • Linux .deb / .rpm / Flatpak distribution. Issue: open in installer repo, P3.

docs.title: Research: imitate Claude Code structural patterns in KARIANA
docs.text: Status: experimental research branch feat/claude-code-structural-imitation. Not for production. Not for TVN. This branch exists to evaluate whether porting the structural decomposition popularised by Claude Code (via the public Rust imitator ultraworkers/claw-code) improves KARIANA's effectiveness — response accuracy, log clarity, and overall polish over the current v0.11.3 dev state.

docs.title: Research question
docs.text:
Claude Code's structure — readable through the open-source claw-code Rust port — is a 9-crate decomposition with explicit boundaries between provider/runtime/tools/ permissions/telemetry/test-doubles. KARIANA's stack is C++ (UE plugin) + Python (daemon backend) and cannot be ported wholesale. Can we adopt the structural patterns while keeping the C++/Python stack, and does doing so measurably improve KARIANA?

Success criteria for the experiment:

  1. Response accuracy: mock-parity harness catches at least one regression class that current unit tests miss (e.g. tool counter desync, premature "finished", poisoned-session-on-502).
  2. Log clarity: a single structured event stream replaces ad-hoc UE_LOG / Python logging calls scattered across the bridge and backend.
  3. Polish: UI counters and labels derive from event stream rather than mutated local state; session lifecycle has explicit operations rather than implicit "talk to the daemon and hope".

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Not for TVN re-demo (2026-06-02). TVN uses KARIANA-tvn fork. Nothing here ships to TVN.
  • No version bump, no release, no installer rebuild. Step 8/9 of the standard dev workflow are explicitly skipped for this branch.
  • No rewrite to Rust. UE plugin stays C++; daemon stays Python. We are imitating the structure not the language.
  • No upstream merge until the experiment is judged. Branch stays open as a draft PR for review/discussion.

docs.title: The 7 structural lessons
docs.text:
Each lesson below lists:

  • Current KARIANA state (file paths, LOC at branch base 0867adcc)
  • claw-code reference (the file or crate to study)
  • Target KARIANA state (concrete files to add or modify)
  • Acceptance criteria (how we know the lesson landed)
  • Risk (low / medium / high — drives ordering)

docs.title: Lesson 6 — Mock parity harness ⭐ highest leverage
docs.text:
Implemented first because it is purely additive (test-only), demonstrates the imitation pattern most clearly, and unlocks regression detection for every other lesson.

  • Current: Content/Python/tests/{test_bedrock_backend.py, test_deterministic_mcp.py, test_mode_tool_gating_repro.py} — unit-level only. No deterministic mock backend; tests either stub or hit live services.
  • Reference: rust/crates/mock-anthropic-service/ + rust/crates/rusty-claude-cli/tests/mock_parity_harness.rs + rust/mock_parity_scenarios.json (12 scenarios, 21 captured /v1/messages requests).
  • Target:
  • Content/Python/tests/parity/server.py — fake Bedrock + LM Studio HTTP server replaying captured JSON responses.
  • Content/Python/tests/parity/scenarios/*.json — seed with 3:
    • streaming_text.json — basic streaming reply
    • multi_tool_turn.json — assistant invokes 2+ tools in one turn
    • error_502_session_reset.json — backend returns 502 mid-turn; harness asserts session is reset, not poisoned
  • Content/Python/tests/parity/runner.py — pytest-discoverable; loads scenario, points the backend at the fake server, captures actual transcript, diffs against expected.
  • scripts/run_parity_diff.py — CLI wrapper for local invocation outside pytest.
  • Acceptance: pytest Content/Python/tests/parity/ green; intentionally injecting the PR #615 bug (no history reset on 502) makes error_502_session_reset.json fail.
  • Risk: Low (test-only, no production code touched).

docs.title: Lesson 2 — Session lifecycle as first-class operations
docs.text:
• Current: KarianaChatSession.cpp (529 LOC) + KarianaSessionController.cpp (568 LOC) hold the type; daemon (bedrock_backend.py:1661 LOC) owns history. No explicit Reset() or Compact() API. C++ only holds SessionId. Symptom: PR #615 (502 errors poison the session because there is no reset hook).
  • Reference: rust/crates/runtime/src/{session.rs, session_control.rs, conversation.rs, compact.rs, summary_compression.rs} — five files, one concern.
  • Target:
  • KarianaChatSession::Reset() — wipes daemon-side history for the session ID and resets local UI state.
  • KarianaChatSession::Compact() — triggers daemon-side summary compression, returns the new compacted state.
  • bedrock_backend.py exposes reset_session(session_id) and compact_session(session_id) RPC handlers.
  • Backend automatically calls reset_session from its 502 error path before bubbling the error to C++ (closes the PR #615 bug class).
  • Acceptance: error_502_session_reset.json parity scenario passes. Manual UE test: trigger a 502, observe the session is usable on retry.
  • Risk: Low-Medium (adds new methods; existing call sites unchanged).

docs.title: Lesson 7 — Telemetry as a separate layer
docs.text:
• Current: Content/Python/backends/events.py (47 LOC) — seed exists but underused. Logging sprinkled across bridge + backend + handlers via UE_LOG / logging.getLogger. UI tool-call counter is mutated local state (PR #601 bug class).
  • Reference: rust/crates/telemetry/ — separate crate, one job.
  • Target:
  • Content/Python/telemetry/__init__.py — promote from single file.
  • Content/Python/telemetry/events.py — structured event types: ToolCallStarted, ToolCallCompleted, MessageReceived, MessageStreamChunk, BackendError, SessionReset, SessionCompacted.
  • Content/Python/telemetry/emitter.py — single emit(event) function backends call instead of logging.info.
  • Content/Python/telemetry/sink_log.py — default sink writes to existing log channels.
  • Content/Python/telemetry/sink_ipc.py — sink that ships events over the existing daemon→C++ pipe so the UI can consume them.
  • C++ side: a KarianaTelemetryStream subscriber that the chat panel reads from for counters / labels.
  • Acceptance: Tool-call counter reads from event count, not local mutation. Killing the daemon mid-turn produces a BackendError event the UI surfaces. Parity harness can assert on event sequences.
  • Risk: Medium (touches UI binding for counter — needs careful migration).

docs.title: Lesson 4 — Permission as a layer, with hooks as the extension point
docs.text:
• Current: KarianaApprovalController.cpp (145 LOC) exists but is too thin to gate 40 handler files. Permission decisions scattered. No hooks extension point for users.
  • Reference: rust/crates/runtime/src/{permission_enforcer.rs, hooks.rs, policy_engine.rs, trust_resolver.rs}.
  • Target:
  • Content/Python/backends/permissions_map.py — declarative {handler_name: PermissionLevel} map. Levels: auto_allow / prompt_once / prompt_each / deny.
  • Content/Python/backends/hooks.py — PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop hook dispatch. Default no-ops. User overrides via project-level .kariana/hooks.py.
  • KarianaApprovalController grows to consume the map (RPC fetches it from daemon at session start).
  • Acceptance: Adding a tool to permissions_map.py with deny causes KarianaApprovalController to reject it without code changes elsewhere. A user-provided PreToolUse hook can veto a tool call.
  • Risk: Medium (changes approval flow — must preserve existing UX for already-approved tools).

docs.title: Lesson 3 — Tool validation as separate submodules
docs.text:
• Current: 40 handler files, no validation layer. python_execution_commands.py and python_commands.py run user-provided Python with minimal guards. No symlink/path/binary-detection guards on file writes.
  • Reference: rust/crates/runtime/src/bash_validation.rs — 6 submodules: readOnlyValidation, destructiveCommandWarning, modeValidation, sedValidation, pathValidation, commandSemantics.
  • Target:
  • Content/Python/backends/validators/__init__.py
  • Content/Python/backends/validators/python_exec.py — read-only mode check, dangerous import allowlist, exec timeout enforcement.
  • Content/Python/backends/validators/file_path.py — workspace-boundary check, symlink-escape guard, path traversal.
  • Content/Python/backends/validators/file_content.py — binary detection, size limit.
  • tool_executor.py calls validators before dispatch.
  • Acceptance: Symlink-escape attempt fails with a clear error. Writing a 500 MB file is rejected pre-flight. Parity scenario validator_blocks_symlink_escape.json passes.
  • Risk: Medium (must preserve existing successful tool calls — false-positive risk).

docs.title: Lesson 5 — MCP lifecycle hardening as a named module
docs.text:
• Current: MCP code exists across Source/UnrealMCPBridge/ + Source/GenerativeAISupportEditor/Private/MCP/. Retry/timeout/dead-server-detection logic is scattered.
  • Reference: rust/crates/runtime/src/mcp_lifecycle_hardened.rs — one file, one job: edge cases.
  • Target:
  • Source/UnrealMCPBridge/Private/MCPLifecycleHardening.cpp + .h — collects connection retries, exponential backoff, dead-server probes, malformed-message handling, graceful shutdown.
  • Existing MCP files delegate to it instead of inlining hardening.
  • Acceptance: Killing the MCP server mid-call surfaces a clean error within 5 seconds (not a hang). Restarting it auto-reconnects.
  • Risk: Medium (extraction risk — easy to miss a code path).

docs.title: Lesson 1 — Split god-objects (deferred, highest risk)
docs.text:
Done last, after the additive lessons are stable, so the splits land on top of a more disciplined surface.

  • Current:
  • KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.cpp — 1331 LOC
  • bedrock_backend.py — 1661 LOC
  • tool_schema.py — 1749 LOC
  • Reference: rust/crates/runtime/src/ — ~25 single-purpose files, mostly ≤400 LOC each.
  • Target: each file split into ≤400-LOC single-purpose siblings matching the responsibilities exposed by lessons 2/4/7 above. Exact split TBD after the additive work.
  • Acceptance: no file in the touched set exceeds 400 LOC. All tests (existing unit + new parity) still green.
  • Risk: High. Mechanical but invasive. Done in its own PR, separately reviewed.

docs.title: Sequencing in this branch
docs.text: Order Lesson Why this slot 1 6 — Mock parity harness Pure additive; unlocks regression detection for everything else 2 2 — Session lifecycle methods Small, surgical; fixes PR #615 bug class; parity scenario already drafted in lesson 6 3 7 — Telemetry layer Additive; enables event-driven UI binding for lesson 4 4 4 — Hooks + permission map Builds on telemetry events 5 3 — Validators Additive; benefits from telemetry to surface rejections 6 5 — MCP lifecycle hardening Extraction; cleaner after telemetry exists 7 1 — Split god-objects Last; built on stable additive surface

docs.title: Open decisions
docs.text:
1. Should permissions_map.py ship a default that matches today's effective policy (no behaviour change), or default to stricter rules? Default: match today, change later.
  2. Telemetry events over the existing daemon pipe vs. a separate channel? Default: existing pipe with a tag prefix, to avoid pipe-multiplication.
  3. Does the Compact() operation use the local LLM (LM Studio) when available? Default: yes, falls back to Bedrock if not.
  4. Validators block by raising, or by emitting a BackendError event and returning a tool-error? Default: tool-error event, so the LLM can recover.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria for the whole experiment
docs.text:
The branch is judged successful if:

  • All 7 lessons land as described, with green tests.
  • The mock parity harness (lesson 6) is adopted as part of the regular dev cycle.
  • At least one historical bug class (PR #601 tool counter, PR #615 session poison) is provably blocked by the new structure in the harness.
  • A team member who didn't write the branch can read this doc and the resulting files and explain how a message becomes a tool call.

If those criteria fail, the branch is closed and the lessons are documented as "tried, didn't help" in docs/decisions/.

docs.title: Plan: split KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.cpp (deferred to in-editor session)
docs.text: Status: designed, not executed. Sibling to lesson 1 of the Claude Code structural imitation experiment. The split requires a UE-running session to verify the build because the seams introduce new #include resolution that the offline test suite cannot catch. See docs/plans/2026-05-20-claude-code-structural-imitation.md for the parent experiment.

docs.title: Why this is a separate doc
docs.text: The Python pieces of lesson 1 are testable offline — pytest proves nothing got broken by the split. The C++ piece sits behind UnrealBuildTool. A missing header in one of the new .cpp files is invisible until UBT actually runs. Doing the split blind in this branch would ship a likely-broken state that the parity harness can't detect.

docs.title: Current shape
docs.text:
Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.cpp — 1331 LOC, one class, four logical sections already marked with comment banners. No real interleaving; the section seams are clean.

Section banner Lines LOC Methods (no banner — class header) 1–223 223 constructor, BeginDestroy, Initialize, Shutdown, SetModel, ResetSession, SetSessionId // ===== Daemon Lifecycle ===== 224–720 497 SpawnDaemon, KillDaemon // ===== Daemon IPC ===== 721–1045 325 SendDaemonCommand, SendModeCommand, SendUndoAction, SendRedoAction, ApprovePlan, RevisePlan, SendUserQuestionResponse, SendMessage, CancelRequest // ===== Game-Thread Message Dispatch ===== 1046–1331 286 DrainMessageQueue, DispatchParsedMessage, HandleDaemonCrash

docs.title: Proposed split
docs.text:
Four .cpp files implementing the same UKarianaClaudeCodeBridge UCLASS. Header (KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.h) stays untouched. UE's build system picks up every .cpp in Private/ automatically — no Build.cs change.

Target file Methods LOC budget KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.cpp constructor, BeginDestroy, Initialize, Shutdown, model/session accessors ~230 KarianaClaudeCodeBridgeDaemon.cpp SpawnDaemon, KillDaemon ~500 KarianaClaudeCodeBridgeIPC.cpp all Send*, ApprovePlan, RevisePlan, CancelRequest ~330 KarianaClaudeCodeBridgeDispatch.cpp DrainMessageQueue, DispatchParsedMessage, HandleDaemonCrash ~290

Each new file needs:

  1. #include "KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.h" — the UCLASS declaration.
  2. #include "UnrealAssistantIntegration.h" — module-level log category.
  3. The subset of utility headers each section actually uses.

docs.title: DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY placement
docs.text: UnrealAssistantIntegration.cpp already calls DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY(LogKarianaAssistant). The new .cpp files use DECLARE_LOG_CATEGORY_EXTERN (already in UnrealAssistantIntegration.h) and must not repeat the DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY macro — duplicating it produces a UBT duplicate-symbol error.

docs.title: #include audit needed before splitting
docs.text:
Before executing the split, audit the current #include block at the top of KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.cpp and trace which headers each section actually references. Candidates:

  • Misc/Paths.h, HAL/PlatformProcess.h, Misc/FileHelper.h — used by daemon spawn
  • Serialization/JsonSerializer.h, Dom/JsonObject.h — IPC code
  • KarianaChatSession.h, KarianaConversationStore.h — used by dispatch / approval

Headers that only one section uses should move WITH the section. Headers used by two or more stay in every file that needs them.

docs.title: Static helpers
docs.text:
Search for static definitions inside the .cpp. Any file-local helper used by methods in multiple sections must either:

  • Move to an anonymous namespace in a shared header (KarianaClaudeCodeBridgePrivate.h), OR
  • Stay co-located with the section that uses it most, with the other section accessing it via a class private method.

Bias toward the first option if the helper is pure — keeps each .cpp honest.

docs.title: Verification protocol when this lands
docs.text:
1. Build clean: Build.cs untouched, but trigger a full module rebuild (Rebuild Solution in Rider/VS) to catch any missing-include errors.
  2. Editor load: the plugin must hot-reload without LogClass: Error.
  3. Behavioural smoke: open KARIANA chat, send a message, confirm the daemon spawns, IPC works, dispatch fires. Equivalent to the lesson-2 + lesson-7 parity scenarios but exercised through the C++ surface.
  4. Telemetry: the existing LogKarianaAssistant lines from lesson 2 still appear at the same call sites (proves the splits didn't accidentally drop any logging).

docs.title: Honest tradeoff
docs.text:
The split is mechanical but the verification is not mechanical for me. Doing it blind here risks introducing build breakage that the offline parity suite can't see. The cost of waiting for an in-editor session is one extra PR; the cost of pushing a broken build is a full rollback and re-review.

This document captures the design so when someone runs the editor next, the split is a 10-minute exercise instead of a re-investigation.

docs.title: Skipping this in lesson 1 was the right call
docs.text:
Per the lesson-1 commit log in the parent branch:

  • tool_schema.py: 1749 → 438 + 1307 LOC of data ✓
  • bedrock_backend.py: 1833 → 1500 + 279 + 90 LOC ✓
  • KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.cpp: 1331 LOC → deferred to in-editor session ✓ (this doc)

docs.title: Per-Turn Chat Message — Option B Refactor
docs.text: Date: 2026-05-21 Branch: refactor/per-turn-chat-message Builds on: PR #626 (merged 2026-05-21 — turn_restart protocol, BeginNextTurnSegment) Closes deeper layer of: #623 (chat UI grouping)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
PR #626 fixed multi-turn interleaving at the turn boundary: each agent turn now renders as its own Processing + Assistant pair. Within a single turn, however, tools are still stacked together followed by all the text — not the Claude Code shape of text → tool → text → tool → text.

The root cause is structural: a single response turn is represented by three sibling widgets in the scroll box (SKarianaChatMessage Processing, SKarianaStepsWidget, SKarianaChatMessage Assistant), and the controller has to keep them synchronized through swap/upgrade logic and a MoveActiveStepsWidgetToEnd reorder hack. Every recent chat-UI bug (#622, #623, parts of #601) traces back to that split.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Collapse the per-turn three-widget pattern into one widget per turn. The data model already supports this: FKarianaChatMessage.Steps[].StepText carries the text streamed before each tool call, Content carries the trailing text after the last tool. The daemon already emits tool_use{step_text, step_index} events with the right data — no protocol change needed.

docs.title: Scope (locked)
docs.text: # Item Notes 1 Branch + this plan doc — 2 FKarianaChatStep.ImagePaths Step-level images; falls back to message-level for non-tool images 3 Session state machine BeginAssistantTurn(model) replaces BeginAssistantMessage + BeginResponseSegment + BeginNextTurnSegment. Drop EKarianaChatRole::Processing and bIsIntermediateTurn. 4 Image step_index threading Daemon → bridge → session; routes image to current step's ImagePaths 5 SKarianaChatMessage rewrite Iterates Steps: StepText markdown → step row → step images. Then trailing Content. Then footer. 6 Controller simplification Delete ActiveStepsWidget, ActiveStepsContainer, ActiveStepsMessageId, StreamingAssistantContainer, StreamingAssistantMessageId, MoveActiveStepsWidgetToEnd, Processing→Assistant upgrade branch. 7 BuildStepRow factory Extract from SKarianaStepsWidget to KarianaStepRowFactory.h/cpp. Remove standalone widget if no other callers. 8 Load-time persistence migration LoadMessages merges old (Processing-with-Steps, Assistant) pairs into single Assistant turns. Drops orphan Processing. Transparent. 9 Compact default KeepRecent 6 → 4 Turns are coarser than messages 10 Session-total footer Last turn after stream-complete shows extra Total: Xs ∣ Tools: Y across N turns. Hidden while any turn is streaming. 11 Parity tests + scenarios Update for one-message-per-turn output. Existing multi_turn_agent_loop.json and tool-counter tests need adjustment. 12 Build + smoke test UnrealBuildTool compile, pytest, editor smoke

docs.title: Explicitly out of scope (v1)
docs.text:
• Daemon wire protocol changes — none required
  • Backend-specific behavior — all three backends (Claude SDK, Bedrock, OpenAI-compat) already emit the same tool_use shape
  • FKarianaConversationExchange external shape — only the inner message-array shape changes
  • SKarianaUserInputPrompt — stays a sibling widget for UserInputRequired messages
  • Step-level virtualization for 30+ tool turns — Slate handles it; revisit if performance regresses

docs.title: Edge cases handled (from analysis)
docs.text:
• Chat-only turn (zero tools): one turn widget, no step rows, Content is the full response
  • Tools but no trailing text: turn ends on last step row
  • No leading text before first tool: step row renders without empty StepText markdown
  • Mid-turn cancel: turn marked Cancelled, in-progress steps marked Cancelled, PendingText frozen as Content
  • Mid-turn error: turn marked Error, step rows preserved for debuggability
  • ExitPlanMode: trailing Content is the plan text; approval card is a sibling UserInputRequired message below
  • take_editor_screenshot: image attaches to the step that produced it via step_index
  • Old transcripts on disk: load-time migration converts to new shape
  • Anthropic SDK message_start ordering: same assumption as PR #626 — pre-existing risk

docs.title: Per-turn vs session stats
docs.text:
• Per turn: every turn widget shows Time: Xs ∣ Tools: Y on completion (no bIsIntermediateTurn suppression — every turn's stats are real)
  • Session total: below the final turn of a response cycle, append Total: Σtime ∣ Σtools across N turns once bIsStreaming == false. Removed/hidden if the session resumes (next user message starts a new cycle).

docs.title: Test plan
docs.text:
• pytest parity suite green
  • New parity scenario: single_message_per_turn.json asserts one assistant message per response cycle regardless of tool count
  • Editor smoke: send a prompt that fires 4+ tools, observe inline text/tool interleaving, copy button content, stats footer
  • Load an old transcript saved under PR #626 shape — verify migration produces single Assistant turn widgets without losing tool rows
  • Cancel mid-stream — verify step rows freeze, no orphan spinners

docs.title: Per-Turn Chat Refactor — Backend/Frontend Split Contract
docs.text:
Date: 2026-05-21 Integration branch: refactor/per-turn-chat-message Sub-branches: refactor/per-turn-backend, refactor/per-turn-frontend Parent plan: 2026-05-21-per-turn-chat-message.md

Two parallel agents land separate PRs into the integration branch. This document is the contract both agents code against — neither agent should change anything specified here without the other being notified.

docs.title: Backend agent (refactor/per-turn-backend)
docs.text: Owns: - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Public/KarianaChatSession.h - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/KarianaChatSession.cpp - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Public/KarianaChatTypes.h (struct shape, enum values) - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Public/KarianaAssistantProxy.h - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/KarianaAssistantProxy.cpp - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Public/KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.h - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/KarianaClaudeCodeBridge.cpp - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Public/DaemonIOThread.h - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/DaemonIOThread.cpp - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/KarianaConversationStore.cpp - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Public/KarianaConversationStore.h - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/UnrealAssistantIntegration.cpp (proxy→session bindings only) - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaChatPanel.cpp — only the binding block in Construct() at lines ~170-322. Frontend owns the layout/widget tree elsewhere in this file. - Content/Python/kariana_agent_daemon.py (image event step_index emit) - Content/Python/backends/bedrock_daemon_adapter.py (same) - Content/Python/tests/parity/** (test scenarios + assertions)

docs.title: Frontend agent (refactor/per-turn-frontend)
docs.text: Owns: - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaChatMessage.h - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaChatMessage.cpp - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaStepsWidget.h - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaStepsWidget.cpp - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/KarianaStepRowFactory.h (new) - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/KarianaStepRowFactory.cpp (new) - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Controllers/KarianaMessageController.h - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Controllers/KarianaMessageController.cpp - Source/UnrealAssistantIntegration/Private/Widgets/SKarianaChatPanel.cpp — only the layout/widget tree and visual code outside the binding block. Backend owns the binding block.

docs.title: Shared / coordination required
docs.text:
• SKarianaChatPanel.cpp is split. Backend touches binding code; frontend touches layout. Keep edits to disjoint line ranges. If a conflict arises, frontend agent rebases.
  • KarianaChatTypes.h is backend-owned but frontend reads. Backend must not break the public shape mid-refactor without notifying integration.

docs.title: Stable interface contract (DO NOT CHANGE without coordination)
Data shape (in KarianaChatTypes.h)
docs.text:
struct FKarianaChatStep {
    int32 StepIndex;
    FString ToolName;
    FString StepText;     // Text Claude wrote BEFORE this tool call
    FString StepPreview;
    EKarianaStepStatus Status;
    FDateTime StartTime, EndTime;
    double DurationSeconds;
    TArray<FString> ImagePaths;  // Step-attached images (from take_editor_screenshot etc)
};

struct FKarianaChatMessage {
    FGuid MessageId;
    EKarianaChatRole Role;        // User | Assistant | Error | UserInputRequired
    FString Content;              // Trailing text AFTER the last tool call (or full text if no tools)
    TArray<FKarianaChatStep> Steps;  // One entry per tool call this turn, in order
    TArray<FString> ImagePaths;   // Message-level images (non-tool-attached)
    EKarianaChatMessageState State;
    FString ModelUsed;
    FDateTime Timestamp, ResponseStartTime;
    int32 McpToolCount;
    // Backend MAY drop `bIsIntermediateTurn` and `EKarianaChatRole::Processing`
    // usage. Frontend MUST not depend on `Processing` for new code — render same
    // shape regardless of role being Processing or Assistant.
};

Invariant: One FKarianaChatMessage per assistant turn. Steps[] in arrival order. Content is everything after the last tool.

docs.title: Session API (backend)
docs.text:
// Lifecycle
FKarianaChatMessage& BeginAssistantTurn(const FString& Model);
void AppendToStreamingMessage(const FString& Chunk);  // appends to current msg's Content
void AddToolUseStep(const FString& ToolName, const FString& StepText, int32 StepIndex);
  // — appends a new Step; snaps current msg's Content into the new step's StepText
  //   if daemon StepText is empty; clears msg.Content (post-step trailing buffer).
void AddImageToCurrentStep(const FString& ImagePath, int32 StepIndex);
  // — attaches image to Steps[StepIndex].ImagePaths if step exists; falls back
  //   to message-level ImagePaths if StepIndex is INDEX_NONE or invalid.
void AddImageToCurrentMessage(const FString& ImagePath);  // legacy, message-level
void BeginNextTurn(const FString& Model);  // finalize current msg as Complete + Assistant; create new Assistant streaming msg
void CompleteStreamingMessage(const FString& FullContent);
void FailStreamingMessage(const FString& ErrorText);
void CancelStreamingMessage();

Removed (callers must update): - BeginAssistantMessage → use BeginAssistantTurn - BeginResponseSegment → no-op, remove - EndProcessingSegment → no-op, remove - BeginNextTurnSegment → use BeginNextTurn

docs.title: Delegate signatures (backend → frontend)
docs.text:
FOnChatMessageAdded     OnMessageAdded(const FKarianaChatMessage&);
FOnChatMessageUpdated   OnMessageUpdated(const FKarianaChatMessage&);
FOnChatStepAdded        OnStepAdded(const FGuid& MsgId, const FKarianaChatStep&);
FOnChatStepUpdated      OnStepUpdated(const FGuid& MsgId, const FKarianaChatStep&);
FOnChatStepImageAdded   OnStepImageAdded(const FGuid& MsgId, int32 StepIndex, const FString& Path);  // NEW
FOnChatCleared          OnCleared();
FOnChatStreamingStateChanged OnStreamingStateChanged(bool bStreaming);

Frontend hooks all of these on the controller. When OnMessageAdded fires for an Assistant-role streaming message, the controller creates ONE widget. Subsequent OnStepAdded/OnStepUpdated/OnStepImageAdded/OnMessageUpdated update the SAME widget by MessageId.

docs.title: Proxy → Session bindings (in SKarianaChatPanel.cpp binding block)
docs.text:
Backend owns the binding block. After refactor: - OnStreamingChunk → Session->AppendToStreamingMessage(chunk) (no segment routing) - OnProcessingSegmentEnd → REMOVED (no-op event, unsubscribe) - OnTurnRestart → Session->BeginNextTurn(model) - OnToolUse → Session->AddToolUseStep(tool, step_text, step_index) - OnImage(path, step_index) → Session->AddImageToCurrentStep(path, step_index) - OnResponseGenerated → Session->CompleteStreamingMessage(full) - OnError → Session->FailStreamingMessage(err)

The OnProcessingSegmentEnd delegate on the proxy itself stays (other consumers may use it) — just the session-side handler is dropped.

docs.title: Daemon wire protocol changes
docs.text:
Image events gain step_index field:

// Before
{"type": "image", "id": msg_id, "path": "/path/to.png"}
// After
{"type": "image", "id": msg_id, "path": "/path/to.png", "step_index": 3}
// step_index is the index of the step the image belongs to (0-based).
// If image is not tool-attached, omit step_index (or set to -1).

Backend agent updates daemon + bedrock adapter + ClaudeCodeBridge JSON parsing + AssistantProxy OnImage delegate signature.

docs.title: Widget contract (frontend)
docs.text:
SKarianaChatMessage::Construct for Assistant/Processing roles renders this vertical stack:

For each Step in Steps[]:
  - If Step.StepText non-empty: markdown block
  - Step row (from KarianaStepRowFactory::BuildStepRow)
  - For each ImagePath in Step.ImagePaths: SKarianaImagePreview
If Content non-empty:

docs.title: Kariana Support Bundle — Design
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-05-25
  • Author: Aristide + Claude
  • Repo / target branch: INGIPSA/KARIANA → developer (flows into KARIANA-tvn on next merge)
  • Status: Approved design, pending implementation plan

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
When a client hits a problem today there is no single artifact they can send us to troubleshoot. They can manually grab Saved/Logs/KarianaDaemon.log and the UE log and email them, but:

  • it is unstructured and inconsistent,
  • it carries no system fingerprint (GPU/VRAM/OS/backend/version), which is exactly what we need for crashes, model-load, and performance issues, and
  • the raw files leak secrets — daemon logs print Bedrock URLs in plaintext, .kariana_config holds the API key, and .kariana_token is the HMAC license token.

We want a one-action, simplest-for-the-client way to produce a single, redacted .zip they email to us (or, for offline clients like TVN, drop on a USB).

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• One action for the client; no manual file-hunting, no redaction on their side.
  • Works in the common case (app runs, something misbehaved) and the worst case (UE won't launch / daemon dead / crash).
  • Safe by default: secrets never leave the machine; the client can glance at a human-readable summary and trust what they are sending.
  • Useful by default: enough raw context for us to actually debug.

docs.title: Non-goals (YAGNI)
docs.text:
• No remote upload / telemetry endpoint. The bundle is a local file. (Also required for the air-gapped TVN constraint.)
  • No crash-dump capture / minidump integration (future work if needed).
  • No log-rotation overhaul (separate concern; we only tail logs here).

docs.title: Decisions (from brainstorming)
docs.text: Decision Choice Trigger Button in chat panel + standalone script (both), sharing one collector Secret handling Auto-redact logs + allowlist-built summary.txt the client can read First home Upstream developer first; TVN cherry-picks after its re-demo settles Support contact hello@kariana.ai Standalone form .py run by the bundled/system Python (not a compiled .exe)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
One pure-Python, stdlib-only collector is the single source of truth. Both entry points call it, so behaviour and tests live in one place.

   "Report a problem" button ─┐
   (chat panel)               │     ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                              ├────▶│ support/bundle.py            │
   kariana-support.py        │      │  collect → redact →          │──▶ kariana-support-<ts>.zip
   (standalone, double-click)┘      │  summary.txt + manifest.json │
                                    │  ┌────────────────────────┐  │
                                    │  │ collector.py           │  │
                                    │  │ redact.py (shared      │  │
                                    │  │ secret patterns)       │  │
                                    │  └────────────────────────┘  │
                                    └──────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• Content/Python/support/collector.py — gathers each section: versions, system info, log tails, safe configs, optional telemetry. No UE import, no running daemon required. Resolves the same on-disk paths the daemon uses (%LOCALAPPDATA%/KARiANA/..., project Saved/Logs/). Stdlib only.
  • Content/Python/support/redact.py — the secret-scrubbing regex patterns extracted into one tiny, dependency-free module (re + typing only). memory/privacy.py is refactored to import its patterns from here, so there is no duplicated regex and the standalone path never pulls in the memory package / SQLite.
  • Content/Python/support/bundle.py — orchestrates collect → redact → write summary.txt + manifest.json → zip → return path. Always produces a (possibly partial) zip.
  • Content/Python/support/__main__.py + a thin shipped launcher kariana-support.py — standalone entry. Auto-finds the project by walking up to the .uproject; if none found, still collects user-scope data (versions, system info, user logs). Runs when UE won't launch.
  • Chat-panel button — a "Report a problem" button in UnrealAssistantIntegration's chat panel that spawns the same collector (out-of-process Python call), then reveals the resulting zip in Explorer.
  • Bonus (near-free): register export_support_bundle as an MCP tool so the "ask in chat" path also works, reusing the same bundle.py.

docs.title: Bundle contents (the .zip)
docs.text:
Entry Contents Safety summary.txt Human-readable, allowlist-built: versions, GPU/VRAM, OS, active backend, top error lines with values stripped. Header states where to send + Support ID. Safe by construction manifest.json Machine-readable mirror: versions, system info, support_id, timestamp, collection_errors[], list of included files. Safe by construction logs/KarianaDaemon.log Tail (last N MB, default 5 MB), run through redactor. Auto-redacted logs/<Project>.log UE log tail, redacted. Auto-redacted telemetry.json export_audit_log() output — only if daemon reachable; skipped otherwise. Redacted config/models.json, config/admin_config.json Tool/model config only. No secrets

Hard-excluded, always: .kariana_token, .kariana_config, any KARIANA_BEDROCK_* env value. These are denylisted by exact path/key, independent of the redactor.

docs.title: System info collected
docs.text: OS + version, CPU, RAM, GPU model + VRAM + driver (nvidia-smi if present, else PowerShell Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController fallback), free disk on the project drive, Python version, whether the daemon is up (probe port 9877), active backend (from config / last relevant log line).

docs.title: Output & delivery
docs.text:
• Written to <Desktop>\kariana-support-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.zip, then Explorer opens with the file selected.
  • Support ID = first 8 hex chars of sha256(timestamp + machine-id); appears in the filename, summary.txt, and manifest.json for correlation.
  • summary.txt header:

    "Email this entire .zip to hello@kariana.ai (or hand it to your Kariana contact). Support ID: ………" For offline clients (TVN) the same file goes on a USB.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• Never abort. Each collector section is wrapped; a failure is appended to manifest.collection_errors[] and collection continues. A partial zip is always produced.
  • Redaction is fail-safe. An uncertain line is redacted, not emitted. summary.txt is allowlist-built, so it is clean even if the raw-log scrubber ever misses a pattern.
  • Hard excludes are path/key-based, not regex-based, so they cannot be defeated by a redactor miss.

docs.title: Testing (pytest, target 80%+)
docs.text:
• Redaction: known secrets (OpenAI sk-, GitHub ghp_, Slack xoxb-, AWS keys, key=/token=/password= forms, Bedrock URLs) are scrubbed; a planted secret in a fixture log never appears in bundle output.
  • Collector: runs against fixture log files + a fake project tree; missing files are recorded as collection_errors, not crashes.
  • Bundle assembly: zip contains exactly the expected entries; .kariana_token and .kariana_config are provably absent; summary.txt contains no raw log lines.
  • Shared patterns: memory/privacy.py still scrubs the same secrets after refactor (regression guard).
  • Manual: run kariana-support.py standalone on a real project; click the chat-panel button in-editor; confirm the zip opens in Explorer and the summary is readable + clean.

docs.title: Rollout
docs.text:
1. Build in developer behind no flag (it is opt-in by nature — only runs when invoked).
  2. Ship into the next KARIANA-tvn merge after the TVN re-demo / 05-30 GO/NO-GO, to avoid adding code to a frozen USB deliverable.
  3. Document in docs/help/troubleshooting.md (which already references a non-existent diagnostics command — this replaces that stub).
