docs.title: Support Bundle Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Give a Kariana client a one-action, auto-redacted .zip they can email to hello@kariana.ai (or drop on a USB) so we can troubleshoot — produced by a standalone script that works even when the editor/daemon is broken.

Architecture: A pure-Python, stdlib-only support package under Content/Python/support/ collects versions, system info, redacted log tails, and safe configs, then writes summary.txt + manifest.json into a timestamped zip. Both a standalone CLI (kariana-support.py) and an in-editor MCP tool (handlers/support_commands.py) call the same support.bundle.create_bundle(). Secret-scrubbing patterns live in support/redact.py; memory/privacy.py is refactored to import them (single source of truth, no duplicated regex).

Tech Stack: Python 3 (stdlib only — re, json, zipfile, pathlib, subprocess, socket, ctypes, platform, hashlib, argparse), pytest.

Scope note: This plan covers subsystem A — the Python bundle library, standalone CLI, and MCP tool. The in-editor C++ Slate "Report a problem" button (subsystem B) is deferred to a follow-up plan that requires exploring SKarianaChatPanel. The standalone CLI + MCP tool deliver a working, shippable feature on their own.

# Content/Python/support/__init__.py
"""Support-bundle package: collect redacted diagnostics for client troubleshooting.

Pure stdlib, no `unreal`, no daemon required — so it works from a standalone
script even when the editor will not launch.
"""

# Content/Python/support/redact.py
"""Canonical secret-scrubbing patterns for KARIANA.

Single source of truth: memory/privacy.py imports SECRET_PATTERNS from here so
the regex set is defined exactly once.
"""

import re
from typing import List, Pattern

REDACTION_PLACEHOLDER = "[REDACTED]"

SECRET_PATTERNS: List[Pattern] = [
    re.compile(r'(?i)(api[_-]?key|apikey)\s*[=:]\s*["\']?[\w\-]+'),
    re.compile(r'(?i)(secret|password|passwd|pwd)\s*[=:]\s*["\']?[\w\-]+'),
    re.compile(r'(?i)(token|auth|bearer)\s*[=:]\s*["\']?[\w\-]+'),
    re.compile(r'(?i)(aws|gcp|azure)[_-]?(access|secret)?[_-]?key\s*[=:]\s*["\']?[\w\-]+'),
    re.compile(r'sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}'),            # OpenAI API keys
    re.compile(r'ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}'),            # GitHub tokens
    re.compile(r'xoxb-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+'),            # Slack tokens
    # AWS API Gateway / Bedrock endpoints
    re.compile(r'(?i)https?://[a-z0-9\-]+\.execute-api\.[a-z0-9\-]+\.amazonaws\.com\S*'),
    re.compile(r'(?i)(kariana_bedrock_\w+|bedrock[_-]?url)\s*[=:]\s*\S+'),
]


def redact_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Replace every secret-pattern match with REDACTION_PLACEHOLDER.

    Fail-safe by construction: anything matching a pattern is removed. Returns
    the input unchanged when it is empty or None.
    """
    if not text:
        return text
    result = text
    for pattern in SECRET_PATTERNS:
        result = pattern.sub(REDACTION_PLACEHOLDER, result)
    return result

# Content/Python/support/paths.py
"""Resolve on-disk locations for the support bundle.

Mirrors the paths the daemon uses so the standalone collector finds the same
files. Hard-excluded secret files are listed here, never read by the collector.
"""

import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional

# Files that must NEVER enter a bundle (license token + Bedrock creds).
EXCLUDED_FILENAMES = frozenset({".kariana_token", ".kariana_config"})


def user_data_dir() -> Path:
    """Per-user KARIANA data dir, matching the daemon's resolution order."""
    if os.name == "nt":
        local = os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA")
        if local:
            return Path(local) / "KARiANA"
        return Path.home() / "AppData" / "Local" / "KARiANA"
    return Path.home() / ".config" / "KARiANA"


def models_json_path() -> Path:
    """User model-catalog override (safe to share)."""
    return user_data_dir() / "models.json"


def admin_config_path() -> Path:
    """Gradio admin dashboard config (tool/model config, no secrets)."""
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "admin_dashboard" / "config.json"


def find_project_dir(start: Optional[Path] = None) -> Optional[Path]:
    """Walk up from `start` (or this file's location) to the dir holding a
    *.uproject file. Returns None if none found."""
    current = (start or Path(__file__).resolve()).resolve()
    if current.is_file():
        current = current.parent
    for candidate in [current, *current.parents]:
        try:
            if any(candidate.glob("*.uproject")):
                return candidate
        except OSError:
            continue
    return None

    """KarianaDaemon.log under the project's Saved/Logs."""

# Content/Python/support/collector.py
"""Collect diagnostic data for a support bundle.

Pure stdlib. Every function is safe to call when the editor/daemon is down.
Top-level failures are surfaced to the caller (bundle.py) which aggregates them
into manifest.collection_errors; sub-probes (GPU/RAM) degrade to 'unknown'.
"""

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, Optional

from support import paths
from support.redact import redact_text


def collect_versions() -> dict:
    """Plugin / build / engine version from KARIANA.uplugin (best effort)."""
    try:
        from utils.plugin_version import get_plugin_version
        return dict(get_plugin_version())
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - exercised via bundle error path
        return {"plugin_version": "unknown", "build_number": 0,
                "engine_version": "unknown", "error": str(exc)}


def read_log_tail(path: Path, max_bytes: int = 5 * 1024 * 1024) -> str:
    """Return the last `max_bytes` of a log file, decoding leniently.
    Returns '' if the file is missing or unreadable."""
    try:
        if not path.is_file():
            return ""
        size = path.stat().st_size
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            if size > max_bytes:
                fh.seek(size - max_bytes)
            data = fh.read()
        return data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    except OSError:
        return ""


def collect_logs(project_dir: Optional[Path], max_bytes: int = 5 * 1024 * 1024) -> Dict[str, str]:
    """Redacted tails of the daemon log + UE project logs, keyed by filename."""
    if project_dir is None:
        return {}
    out: Dict[str, str] = {}
    for log_path in paths.unreal_log_paths(project_dir):
        tail = read_log_tail(log_path, max_bytes)
        if tail:
            out[log_path.name] = redact_text(tail)
    return out


def collect_safe_configs() -> Dict[str, str]:
    """Read known-safe config files (no secrets). Skips missing files."""
    out: Dict[str, str] = {}
    for name, path in (("models.json", paths.models_json_path()),
                       ("admin_config.json", paths.admin_config_path())):
        try:
            if path.is_file() and path.name not in paths.EXCLUDED_FILENAMES:
                out[name] = redact_text(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        except OSError:
            continue
    return out

import ctypes
import platform
import shutil
import socket
import subprocess
import sys


def parse_nvidia_smi(output: str) -> list:
    """Parse `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,driver_version
    --format=csv,noheader` output into a list of dicts."""
    gpus = []
    for line in output.strip().splitlines():
        parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split(",")]
        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0]:
            gpus.append({"name": parts[0], "memory_total": parts[1],
                         "driver_version": parts[2]})
    return gpus


def _gpu_info() -> list:
    """GPU details via nvidia-smi, falling back to Windows CIM. '[]' on failure."""
    try:
        res = subprocess.run(
            ["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=name,memory.total,driver_version",
             "--format=csv,noheader"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
        )
        if res.returncode == 0:
            parsed = parse_nvidia_smi(res.stdout)
            if parsed:
                return parsed
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        pass
    if os.name == "nt":
        try:
            res = subprocess.run(
                ["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command",
                 "Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | "
                 "Select-Object Name,AdapterRAM,DriverVersion | ConvertTo-Json"],
                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15,
            )
            if res.returncode == 0 and res.stdout.strip():
                data = json.loads(res.stdout)
                if isinstance(data, dict):
                    data = [data]
                return [{"name": d.get("Name"),
                         "memory_total": d.get("AdapterRAM"),
                         "driver_version": d.get("DriverVersion")} for d in data]
        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            pass
    return []


def _ram_gb() -> float:
    """Total physical RAM in GB, or 0.0 if undeterminable."""
    try:
        if os.name == "nt":
            class _MemStatus(ctypes.Structure):
                _fields_ = [("dwLength", ctypes.c_ulong),
                            ("dwMemoryLoad", ctypes.c_ulong),
                            ("ullTotalPhys", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                            ("ullAvailPhys", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                            ("ullTotalPageFile", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                            ("ullAvailPageFile", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                            ("ullTotalVirtual", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                            ("ullAvailVirtual", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                            ("sullAvailExtendedVirtual", ctypes.c_ulonglong)]
            stat = _MemStatus()
            stat.dwLength = ctypes.sizeof(_MemStatus)
            ctypes.windll.kernel32.GlobalMemoryStatusEx(ctypes.byref(stat))
            return round(stat.ullTotalPhys / (1024 ** 3), 1)
        pages = os.sysconf("SC_PHYS_PAGES")
        page_size = os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE")
        return round(pages * page_size / (1024 ** 3), 1)
    except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError):
        return 0.0


def _daemon_running(port: int = 9877) -> bool:
    try:
        with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as sock:
            sock.settimeout(0.5)
            return sock.connect_ex(("127.0.0.1", port)) == 0
    except OSError:
        return False


def _active_backend() -> str:
    """Best-effort active backend from admin config; 'unknown' otherwise."""
    try:
        cfg = paths.admin_config_path()
        if cfg.is_file():
            data = json.loads(cfg.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
            return str(data.get("active_profile") or data.get("backend") or "unknown")
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        pass
    return "unknown"


def _free_disk_gb(project_dir: Optional[Path]) -> float:
    try:
        target = project_dir if project_dir and project_dir.exists() else Path.home()
        return round(shutil.disk_usage(str(target)).free / (1024 ** 3), 1)
    except OSError:
        return 0.0


def collect_system_info(project_dir: Optional[Path] = None) -> dict:
    """OS, CPU, RAM, GPU, disk, Python, daemon status, active backend."""
    return {
        "os": f"{platform.system()} {platform.release()} ({platform.version()})",
        "machine": platform.machine(),
        "cpu": platform.processor() or "unknown",
        "cpu_count": os.cpu_count() or 0,
        "ram_gb": _ram_gb(),
        "free_disk_gb": _free_disk_gb(project_dir),
        "gpus": _gpu_info(),
        "python_version": sys.version.split()[0],
        "daemon_running": _daemon_running(),
        "active_backend": _active_backend(),
    }

# Content/Python/support/bundle.py
"""Assemble a redacted support bundle zip.

Orchestrates the collector, builds a safe-by-construction summary + manifest,
and writes a single timestamped zip. Never aborts: each collection step is
wrapped and failures are recorded in manifest.collection_errors.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import uuid
import zipfile
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional

from support import collector, paths
from support.redact import redact_text

SUPPORT_EMAIL = "hello@kariana.ai"


def make_support_id(timestamp: str, machine_id: str) -> str:
    """Stable 8-hex-char id from timestamp + machine id (for correlation)."""
    digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{timestamp}{machine_id}".encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    return digest[:8]


def extract_top_errors(logs: dict, limit: int = 20) -> List[str]:
    """Pull error/exception lines from redacted logs, re-redact, cap count/length."""
    keywords = ("error", "exception", "fatal", "traceback")
    found: List[str] = []
    for content in logs.values():
        for line in content.splitlines():
            low = line.lower()
            if any(k in low for k in keywords):
                found.append(redact_text(line.strip())[:300])
                if len(found) >= limit:
                    return found
    return found


def build_summary(data: dict) -> str:
    """Human-readable, ALLOWLIST-ONLY summary. Reads only curated fields — never
    raw log bodies — so it is clean even if the log scrubber misses something."""
    v = data.get("versions", {})
    s = data.get("system_info", {})
    gpu_names = ", ".join(g.get("name", "?") for g in s.get("gpus", [])) or "unknown"
    lines = [
        "KARIANA Support Bundle",
        "=" * 40,
        f"Email this entire .zip to {SUPPORT_EMAIL}",
        "(or hand it to your Kariana contact).",
        f"Support ID: {data.get('support_id', 'unknown')}",
        f"Generated:  {data.get('timestamp', 'unknown')}",
        "",
        "Versions",
        "--------",
        f"  Plugin:  {v.get('plugin_version', 'unknown')} (build {v.get('build_number', '?')})",
        f"  Engine:  {v.get('engine_version', 'unknown')}",
        "",
        "System",
        "------",
        f"  OS:      {s.get('os', 'unknown')}",
        f"  CPU:     {s.get('cpu', 'unknown')} ({s.get('cpu_count', '?')} cores)",
        f"  RAM:     {s.get('ram_gb', '?')} GB",
        f"  GPU:     {gpu_names}",
        f"  Disk:    {s.get('free_disk_gb', '?')} GB free",
        f"  Python:  {s.get('python_version', 'unknown')}",
        f"  Backend: {s.get('active_backend', 'unknown')}",
        f"  Daemon:  {'running' if s.get('daemon_running') else 'not running'}",
        "",
        "Recent errors (redacted)",
        "------------------------",
    ]
    top = data.get("top_errors", [])
    lines.extend(f"  {e}" for e in top) if top else lines.append("  (none captured)")
    errs = data.get("collection_errors", [])
    if errs:
        lines += ["", "Collection warnings", "-------------------"]
        lines.extend(f"  {e}" for e in errs)
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def build_manifest(data: dict) -> dict:
    """Machine-readable mirror of the bundle's safe metadata."""
    return {
        "support_id": data.get("support_id"),
        "timestamp": data.get("timestamp"),
        "support_email": SUPPORT_EMAIL,
        "versions": data.get("versions", {}),
        "system_info": data.get("system_info", {}),
        "included_files": data.get("included_files", []),
        "collection_errors": data.get("collection_errors", []),
    }

def _safe(step_name: str, fn, errors: List[str], default):
    """Run a collector step; on failure record it and return `default`."""
    try:
        return fn()
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - bundle must never abort
        errors.append(f"{step_name}: {exc}")
        return default


def create_bundle(output_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
                  project_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
                  audit_log_json: Optional[str] = None,
                  now: Optional[datetime] = None) -> Path:
    """Collect → redact → write summary + manifest → zip. Returns the zip path.

    Always produces a (possibly partial) zip. `output_dir` defaults to the
    Desktop. `project_dir` is auto-detected when None.
    """
    now = now or datetime.now()
    timestamp = now.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    machine_id = f"{uuid.getnode():x}"
    support_id = make_support_id(timestamp, machine_id)

    if project_dir is None:
        project_dir = paths.find_project_dir()

    errors: List[str] = []
    versions = _safe("versions", collector.collect_versions, errors, {})
    system_info = _safe("system_info",
                        lambda: collector.collect_system_info(project_dir), errors, {})
    logs = _safe("logs", lambda: collector.collect_logs(project_dir), errors, {})
    configs = _safe("configs", collector.collect_safe_configs, errors, {})

    data = {
        "support_id": support_id,
        "timestamp": timestamp,
        "versions": versions,
        "system_info": system_info,
        "logs": logs,
        "top_errors": extract_top_errors(logs),
        "collection_errors": errors,
    }

    included: List[str] = ["summary.txt", "manifest.json"]
    included += [f"logs/{name}" for name in logs]
    included += [f"config/{name}" for name in configs]
    if audit_log_json:
        included.append("telemetry.json")
    data["included_files"] = included

    if output_dir is None:
        desktop = Path.home() / "Desktop"
        output_dir = desktop if desktop.is_dir() else Path.home()
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    zip_path = output_dir / f"kariana-support-{timestamp}.zip"

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        zf.writestr("summary.txt", build_summary(data))
        zf.writestr("manifest.json", json.dumps(build_manifest(data), indent=2))
        for name, content in logs.items():
            if name not in paths.EXCLUDED_FILENAMES:
                zf.writestr(f"logs/{name}", content)
        for name, content in configs.items():
            if name not in paths.EXCLUDED_FILENAMES:
                zf.writestr(f"config/{name}", content)
        if audit_log_json:
            zf.writestr("telemetry.json", redact_text(audit_log_json))

    return zip_path

Works even when Unreal will not launch — collects user-scope data and any logs
it can find by walking up to the .uproject.
"""

import argparse

import sys
from pathlib import Path

from support import bundle


def _reveal(path: Path) -> None:
    """Open the OS file browser with the bundle selected (best effort)."""
    try:
        if os.name == "nt":
            subprocess.run(["explorer", "/select,", str(path)])
        elif sys.platform == "darwin":
            subprocess.run(["open", "-R", str(path)])
        else:
            subprocess.run(["xdg-open", str(path.parent)])
    except OSError:
        pass


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="kariana-support",
        description="Create a redacted KARIANA support bundle to email to hello@kariana.ai")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=None,
                        help="Output directory (default: Desktop)")
    parser.add_argument("--project", type=Path, default=None,
                        help="Unreal project directory (default: auto-detect)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        zip_path = bundle.create_bundle(output_dir=args.output, project_dir=args.project)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"Failed to create support bundle: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    print(f"Support bundle created:\n  {zip_path}\n")
    print(f"Email this .zip to {bundle.SUPPORT_EMAIL} (or hand it to your Kariana contact).")
    _reveal(zip_path)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Content/Python/handlers/support_commands.py
"""Support-bundle MCP command (editor side).

Thin wrapper: imports the pure `support.bundle` package and exposes it as the
`export_support_bundle` tool. When a live audit log is available it is included.
"""

import unreal
from typing import Any, Dict

from support import bundle


def handle_export_support_bundle(command: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Create a redacted support bundle zip on the user's Desktop.

    Args:
        command: {} (no parameters required)

    Returns:
        {'success': True, 'zip_path': '...', 'support_email': 'hello@kariana.ai'}
    """
    try:
        audit_log_json = None
        try:
            from deterministic_mcp import export_audit_log
            audit_log_json = export_audit_log()
        except Exception:
            audit_log_json = None

        zip_path = bundle.create_bundle(audit_log_json=audit_log_json)
        unreal.log(f"KARIANA support bundle created: {zip_path}")
        return {
            "success": True,
            "zip_path": str(zip_path),
            "support_email": bundle.SUPPORT_EMAIL,
        }
    except Exception as exc:
        unreal.log_error(f"Failed to create support bundle: {exc}")
        return {"success": False, "error": str(exc)}


def _register_support_commands():
    try:
        from command_registry import registry  # same import site as other handlers
        registry.register(
            name="export_support_bundle",
            handler=handle_export_support_bundle,
            category="diagnostics",
            description="Create a redacted support bundle zip (logs, versions, system info) "
                        "on the user's Desktop to email to KARIANA support.",
            parameters={},
            examples=[{"description": "Create a support bundle", "parameters": {}}],
            tags=["diagnostics", "support", "logs"],
        )
        unreal.log("Registered 1 support command")
    except Exception as exc:
        unreal.log_error(f"Failed to register support commands: {exc}")


_register_support_commands()

COMMANDS = {
    "export_support_bundle": handle_export_support_bundle,
}

Goal: Restructure the Kariana Assistant UI code so that any AI session (or developer) can quickly understand "where do I change X?" without deep codebase archaeology.

Phases are sequential -- each builds on the previous:

docs.title: Key Design Decisions (from brainstorming session 2026-03-21)
docs.text:
1. JSON = primary source, C++ = crash-safe fallback (not dual source of truth)
  2. Cached colors + OnThemeChanged delegate (not TAttribute lambdas every frame)
  3. Three StyleSets (Chat, Markdown, Icons) instead of one monolithic set
  4. Semantic tokens in ThemeManager's TMap with naming convention (token.AccentPrimary vs color.Pink)
  5. Sub-controllers are plain C++ classes, not widgets -- panel delegates to them

docs.title: Phase 2: Central Theme Manager
docs.text: Risk: Medium -- replaces the color loading/storage mechanism. Files touched: ~6 Depends on: Phase 1 (cleanup)

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
Replace the current pattern (inline globals + dispatch table in KarianaBrandTheme.cpp) with a singleton FKarianaThemeManager that owns all color state.

FKarianaThemeManager (Singleton)
|
+-- TMap<FName, FLinearColor> Colors      // all 72+ colors (69 existing + 3 new from Phase 1)
+-- LoadTheme(FString ThemeName)          // reads JSON, fills map
+-- GetColor(FName Key) -> FLinearColor   // lookup with fallback
+-- OnThemeChanged                        // multicast delegate
|
+-- Startup: PopulateDefaults() -> LoadJsonOverlay()

docs.title: Fallback chain
docs.text:
1. PopulateDefaults() fills the TMap with C++ default values (same values as current KarianaBrandColors.h)
  2. LoadJsonOverlay() reads Content/Config/themes.json, overwrites matching keys
  3. If JSON missing/malformed: defaults remain, warning logged
  4. Widgets read from the TMap via GetColor(), never from inline globals

docs.title: OnThemeChanged pattern (Option B -- cached + delegate)
docs.text:
• Widgets cache FLinearColor values at construction from the TMap
  • Subscribe to OnThemeChanged delegate
  • On theme change: re-read cached values from TMap, rebuild brushes
  • Zero overhead between theme changes

docs.title: Token Naming Convention
docs.text:
Tokens live in the same ThemeManager TMap with a token. prefix:

color.Pink              = (1.0, 0.494, 0.863)    // raw color
token.AccentPrimary     = alias -> color.Pink     // semantic role

JSON theme files can override at either level: - Change color.Pink -> all tokens pointing to it update - Change token.AccentPrimary -> only that role changes

docs.title: Phase 6: Panel Decomposition
docs.text: Risk: High -- restructures the central hub widget. Files touched: ~5 (new controllers + SKarianaChatPanel) Depends on: Phases 1-5. Can be deferred.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
SKarianaChatPanel handles ~14 inbound delegates and ~10 outbound direct-call targets: - Session management (load, save, clear, undo/redo) - Message rendering (create, update, scroll) - Streaming orchestration (start, stop, preview) - Mode switching (validate/teach/create) - History panel management - Attachment handling - Plan approval / user input prompts - Processing state fan-out

This makes it the single bottleneck for every UI change.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
Extract 4 sub-controllers. Each is a plain C++ class (not a widget) that holds the relevant child widget references and subscribes to the delegates it cares about.

SKarianaChatPanel (thin shell -- layout + wiring)
|
+-- FKarianaMessageController
|   Owns: MessageWidgets (TMap), MessageScrollBox, ActiveStepsWidget
|   Handles: OnMessageAdded, OnMessageUpdated, OnStreamingStateChanged
|   Methods: AddMessage, UpdateMessage, ScrollToBottom, SetFontScale
|
+-- FKarianaSessionController
|   Owns: ConversationUndoHistory, ConversationRedoBuffer, HistoryPanel
|   Handles: OnSessionCleared, OnConversationSelected/Deleted
|   Methods: Undo, Redo, NewChat, LoadConversation, SaveConversation
|
+-- FKarianaInputController
|   Owns: ChatInput, AttachmentBar, DropTarget, ModeSelector
|   Handles: OnChatInputSubmitted, OnCancelled, OnAttachmentDropped, OnModeChanged
|   Methods: Submit, Cancel, SetMode, GetAttachments
|
+-- FKarianaApprovalController
    Owns: UserInputWidgets (TMap)
    Handles: OnUserInputRequested, OnExitPlanMode, OnAskUserQuestion
    Methods: ShowApproval, RespondToApproval, ShowPlanApproval

docs.title: Panel becomes thin shell
docs.text:
void SKarianaChatPanel::Construct(const FArguments& InArgs)
{
    // Create controllers
    MessageController = MakeShared<FKarianaMessageController>(ChatSession, Proxy);
    SessionController = MakeShared<FKarianaSessionController>(ChatSession, Proxy);
    InputController = MakeShared<FKarianaInputController>(ChatSession, Proxy);
    ApprovalController = MakeShared<FKarianaApprovalController>(ChatSession, Proxy);

    // Build layout (still in the panel -- it owns the widget tree)
    ChildSlot
    [
        // ... SVerticalBox with header, toolbar, content, input, context bar
        // Child widgets are created here but managed by controllers
    ];

    // Wire controllers to their children
    MessageController->BindTo(MessageScrollBox, ContentSwitcher);
    SessionController->BindTo(HistoryPanel);
    InputController->BindTo(ChatInput, AttachmentBar, ModeSelector);
    ApprovalController->BindTo(MessageScrollBox);
}

docs.title: Requirements

WindowsmacOSLinux
  • Unreal Engine 5.7 or newer

  • Unreal Engine 5.7 or newer (built from source or Epic Games Launcher)

docs.title: Quick Install (Recommended)
docs.text:
WindowsmacOSLinux

Open PowerShell and run:

irm ingipsa.github.io/KARIANA-installer/install.ps1 | iex

The installer automatically:

  1. Detects your Unreal Engine installation(s)
  2. Lets you choose which UE version to install to (or browse manually)
  3. Installs the KARIANA plugin
  4. Installs the kariana-mcp MCP server via pip
  5. Configures Claude Desktop with both MCP servers
  6. Removes any legacy plugin versions

Open Terminal and run:

curl -fsSL https://ingipsa.github.io/KARIANA-installer/install-mac.sh | bash

The installer automatically:

  1. Checks your macOS version and architecture (Apple Silicon / Intel)
  2. Installs Python 3.9+ via Homebrew if missing
  3. Installs the kariana-mcp CLI tool via pip
  4. Detects Unreal Engine installations under /Users/Shared/Epic Games/
  5. Installs the KARIANA plugin to your engine
  6. Configures Claude Desktop with both MCP servers
  7. Removes any legacy plugin versions

Manual UE path

If Unreal Engine is not auto-detected, the installer will prompt you to enter the path manually.

Open a terminal and run:

bash <(curl -fsSL https://ingipsa.github.io/KARIANA-installer/install.sh)

The installer automatically:

  1. Detects your Linux distribution (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch)
  2. Installs required dependencies (Python, pip, git, Node.js)
  3. Clones the KARIANA repository
  4. Detects Unreal Engine installations on your system
  5. Installs the KARIANA plugin to your engine
  6. Installs npm dependencies
  7. Configures Claude Desktop with both MCP servers

Private repository access

If the repository is private, you'll need a GitHub token:

GITHUB_TOKEN="your_token" bash <(curl -fsSL https://ingipsa.github.io/KARIANA-installer/install.sh)

Or authenticate via GitHub CLI first: gh auth login

That's it!

After the installer completes, restart Claude Desktop and you're ready to use KARIANA.

docs.text: If you prefer manual setup or the quick install doesn't work:

docs.title: Step 1: Download the Plugin
docs.text: Download the latest release from GitHub Releases.

docs.title: Step 2: Install the Plugin
docs.text:
Extract the zip and copy the KARIANA folder to your Unreal Engine plugins directory:

WindowsmacOSLinux

Engine-wide installation:

C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.7\Engine\Plugins\Marketplace\KARIANA

Project-specific installation:

YourProject\Plugins\KARIANA

Engine-wide installation:

/Users/Shared/Epic Games/UE_5.7/Engine/Plugins/Marketplace/KARIANA

~/UnrealEngine/UE_5.7/Engine/Plugins/Marketplace/KARIANA

Project-specific installation:

YourProject/Plugins/KARIANA

Note

The engine path depends on where you built UE from source. Common locations include /opt/UnrealEngine/, ~/UnrealEngine/, or a custom path.

Using Symlinks

For development, use a symbolic link to keep the plugin synced with your git repository:

Windows (PowerShell as Admin)macOSLinux 
mklink /D "C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.7\Engine\Plugins\Marketplace\KARIANA" "D:\path\to\KARIANA"

docs.title: Step 3: Enable Required Plugins
docs.text:
In Unreal Engine, go to Edit > Plugins and enable:

  • Remote Control
  • Python Script Plugin
  • KARIANA

Restart Unreal Engine when prompted.

docs.title: Step 3b: Configure Remote Control Settings
docs.text:
Go to Edit > Project Settings and configure these settings for full tool access:

Remote Control Web Server:

  • Auto Start Web Server
  • Auto Start Web Socket Server
  • Remote Control HTTP Server Port: 30010

Remote Control > Security:

  • Enable Remote Python Execution
  • Allow Console Command Remote Execution
  • Enforce Passphrase for Remote Clients (leave unchecked unless you configure a passphrase)

Python Remote Execution:

  • Enable Remote Execution?

Important

Without these settings, the extended tools (cinematics, physics, PCG, patterns, etc.) will not work. The core tools (blueprints, actors, materials) work without these settings, but you'll miss ~100 additional tools.

Restart Unreal Engine after changing these settings.

docs.title: Step 4: Install the MCP Server
docs.text:
The MCP server bridges Claude Desktop and Unreal Engine. Install it via pip:

WindowsmacOSLinux 
pip install kariana-mcp

pip3 install kariana-mcp

pip3 install --user kariana-mcp

docs.title: Step 5: Configure Claude Desktop
docs.text:
KARIANA uses two MCP servers for complete engine control:

  1. Open Claude Desktop
  2. Go to Settings > Developer > MCP Servers
  3. Add this configuration:
Windows / macOSLinux

Config file location:

  • Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kariana-unreal": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["kariana-mcp"]
    },
    "kariana-remote": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["kariana-mcp", "--remote"]
    }
  }
}

Config file location: ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kariana-unreal": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["kariana-mcp"]
    },
    "kariana-remote": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["kariana-mcp", "--remote"]
    }
  }
}
  1. Restart Claude Desktop

Two Servers?

kariana-unreal provides 85 core tools (blueprints, actors, PCG) via the plugin socket. kariana-remote adds 114 extended tools (patterns, foliage, streaming) via Remote Control HTTP. Together they provide 199 tools.

docs.title: Alternative: Local AI Backends (Ollama / LM Studio) — Experimental
docs.text:
Experimental

LM Studio and Ollama support is experimental. They work best with models that have strong tool-calling capabilities (e.g., Qwen3-Coder-32B). Results may vary with smaller or older models.

KARIANA supports local AI backends via Ollama and LM Studio.

docs.title: Local Setup
docs.text:
OllamaLM Studio
  1. Download and install Ollama
  2. Pull a model with tool-calling support: ollama pull qwen3:8b
  3. Ollama runs automatically on http://localhost:11434
  4. In Unreal Engine, go to Edit > Project Settings > KARIANA Assistant
  5. Set AI Provider to Ollama (Experimental)
  6. The Server URL defaults to http://localhost:11434 — no changes needed
  1. Download and install LM Studio
  2. Load a model with tool-calling support (e.g., Qwen3-Coder, Llama 3.3)
  3. Start the local server in LM Studio (default: http://localhost:1234)
  4. In Unreal Engine, go to Edit > Project Settings > KARIANA Assistant

docs.title: Remote Setup (Using KARIANA Cloud Endpoints)
docs.text:
KARIANA provides fixed Cloudflare Tunnel endpoints so remote users can connect to a hosted AI backend without any tunnel setup on their side.

Backend Fixed URL Ollama https://ollama.kariana.ai LM Studio https://lmstudio.kariana.ai

To connect:

  1. In Unreal Engine, go to Edit > Project Settings > KARIANA Assistant
  2. Set AI Provider to Ollama (Experimental) or LM Studio (Experimental)
  3. Set Server URL to the corresponding endpoint above
  4. Open the KARIANA Assistant panel — models from the remote server will appear in the dropdown

Self-Hosted Tunnels

You can also set up your own named Cloudflare Tunnel with a custom domain. See the Configuration Guide for details.

Tool Category Filtering

Local LLMs have smaller context windows than Claude. KARIANA automatically limits tools sent per query using category filtering. You can customize active tool categories via the Gradio Admin Dashboard (python Content/Python/admin_dashboard/app.py).

docs.title: Understanding MCP
docs.text: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standardized interface that allows Claude to interact with external tools like KARIANA.

docs.title: What is MCP?
docs.text:
Think of MCP as a universal remote control for AI assistants. Instead of building custom integrations for every tool, MCP provides a standard way for AI to:

  • Discover available tools
  • Understand what each tool does
  • Call tools with the right parameters
  • Receive and process results

Analogy

MCP is like USB for AI tools - a universal standard that lets different devices (tools) work with different computers (AI models).

docs.title: How Claude Uses MCP
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Your Request] --> B{Claude}
    B --> C[Select Tool]
    C --> D[Call with Parameters]
    D --> E[KARIANA Executes]
    E --> F[Return Results]
    F --> B
    B --> G[Report to You]
  1. You make a request in natural language
  2. Claude selects the appropriate tool(s)
  3. Claude calls the tool with parameters
  4. Tool executes in Unreal Engine
  5. Results return to Claude
  6. Claude reports what happened

docs.title: Example Flow
docs.text:
Your request:

"Spawn a red cube at position 100, 0, 50"

What Claude does:

  1. Determines needed tools: control_actor (spawn), manage_asset (material), control_actor (apply)
  2. Calls control_actor to spawn a cube
  3. Calls manage_asset to create a red material
  4. Calls control_actor to apply the material
  5. Reports success

docs.title: Two Communication Channels
docs.text: KARIANA uses two separate channels for maximum capability:

docs.title: External MCP Server
docs.text:
Uses Unreal's built-in Remote Control plugin.

Property Value Protocol HTTP + WebSocket Ports 30010 (HTTP), 30020 (WS) Tools 50+ core actions Use cases Asset management, actor control, editor commands

docs.title: Plugin Socket Server
docs.text:
Uses KARIANA's direct plugin connection.

Property Value Protocol TCP Socket Port 9877 Tools 188+ specialized features Use cases Blueprints, PCG, sub-levels, World Partition, asset toolkit, advanced features

Automatic Selection

You don't need to know which channel to use - KARIANA automatically routes commands to the right channel.

docs.title: Core Tools (External MCP)
docs.text: Tool Purpose control_actor Spawn, move, delete actors manage_asset List, import, create assets control_editor Play, stop, camera control manage_level Level operations, streaming create_effect Particles, debug visualization

docs.title: Advanced Tools (Plugin)
docs.text: Tool Purpose manage_blueprint Blueprint creation and editing build_environment Landscape, foliage world_organizer Automatic organization pcg_tools Procedural generation sublevel_* Sub-level management wp_* World Partition data layers, HLOD asset_toolkit Offline .uasset search and inspection quick_actions Light creation, alignment

docs.title: Natural Language Tips
docs.text:
You don't need to know tool names. Just describe what you want:

Good Requests

  • "Create a cube"
  • "Add a red material to the sphere"
  • "Put 5 spotlights in a circle around the actor"

Less Effective

  • "Use control_actor spawn"
  • "Call manage_asset create_material"

Be specific for better results:

Instead of... Try... "Make it look nice" "Add a gold metallic material with 0.2 roughness" "Some lights" "Add 3 point lights with warm color (3000K)" "Move it" "Move the cube 500 units along the X axis"

Error Meaning Solution UE_NOT_CONNECTED No connection to UE Ensure UE is running with a project open ASSET_NOT_FOUND Asset doesn't exist Check the asset path INVALID_PARAMETERS Wrong tool parameters Claude will usually retry PERMISSION_DENIED Operation not allowed Some operations require editor mode

docs.title: What is KARIANA?
docs.text: KARIANA functions as a connection layer between AI assistants like Claude and Unreal Engine, enabling natural language control of the engine without manual interface navigation or coding.

docs.title: The Simple Explanation
docs.text:
You can issue commands such as "Spawn a red cube in the middle of the level" and have them execute directly in Unreal Engine. No menus, no code, no complexity.

Think of it like...

Having a skilled Unreal Engine developer who instantly understands and executes your creative vision.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant You
    participant Claude
    participant KARIANA
    participant Unreal Engine

    You->>Claude: "Spawn a red cube at 0, 0, 100"
    Claude->>KARIANA: Translates to MCP tool calls
    KARIANA->>Unreal Engine: Executes commands
    Unreal Engine->>KARIANA: Returns results
    KARIANA->>Claude: Sends response
    Claude->>You: "Done! Created cube with red material"
  1. You request an action from Claude in natural language
  2. Claude translates your request into MCP tool calls
  3. KARIANA sends commands to Unreal Engine
  4. Unreal Engine executes the commands
  5. Results flow back through KARIANA to Claude
  6. Claude confirms what was done

docs.title: Sequencer Camera Pipeline
docs.text: How to set up VENICE2 cameras in Level Sequences with proper hierarchy using KARIANA automation.

docs.title: Correct Structure
docs.text:
Each shot in the master sequence follows this hierarchy:

SCENE00_MASTER (master sequence)
└── SC01_SHOT0010 (shot)
    ├── Level Visibility (x5: VFX, LIGHT, ENV, CAM, ANIM)
    ├── Subsequences (x5: VFX, LIGHT, ENV, ANIM, CAM)
    └── Camera Cuts track → cross-ref to camera in CAM sub

    SC01_SHOT010_CAM (CAM subsequence)
    └── VENICE2_SH0010 binding (possessable)

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: Element Location Notes Camera binding CAM subsequence only Never at shot level Camera Cuts track Shot level only Never inside CAM sub Camera Cuts reference Cross-subsequence Uses portable binding ID

docs.title: 1. Spawn cameras and add to CAM subsequences
docs.text:
import unreal

# Spawn CineCameraActor
camera = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.spawn_actor_from_class(
    unreal.CineCameraActor,
    unreal.Vector(0, 0, 0),
    unreal.Rotator(0, 0, 0)
)
camera.set_actor_label('VENICE2_SH0010')

# Load CAM subsequence and add as possessable
cam_sub = unreal.load_asset(
    '/Game/_TATO/02_SHOTS/SCENE_00/SC00_SHOT0010/SUBSEQUENCE/SC01_SHOT010_CAM'
)
cam_sub.add_possessable(camera)

docs.title: 2. Set up Camera Cuts with cross-subsequence binding
docs.text:
The key challenge is referencing a camera binding that lives in a child subsequence (CAM sub) from the parent (shot level). UE5 uses a deterministic SequenceID hash for this.

# Get the camera binding from CAM sub
cam_binding = cam_sub.get_bindings()[0]

# Get portable binding ID — this computes the correct SequenceID
# IMPORTANT: pass (shot_seq, cam_binding) — NOT (cam_sub, cam_binding)
portable_bid = shot_seq.get_portable_binding_id(shot_seq, cam_binding)

# Create Camera Cuts track at shot level
cc_track = shot_seq.add_track(unreal.MovieSceneCameraCutTrack)
cc_section = cc_track.add_section()
cc_section.set_camera_binding_id(portable_bid)

# Set range to cover entire shot
pr = shot_seq.get_playback_range()
cc_section.set_range(pr.inclusive_start, pr.exclusive_end)

docs.title: 3. Batch apply to all shots
docs.text:
master = unreal.load_asset('/Game/_TATO/01_MASTERS/SCENE_00/SCENE00_MASTER')
shot_track = master.get_tracks()[0]  # Cinematic Shot Track

for section in shot_track.get_sections():
    shot_seq = section.get_sequence()
    if not shot_seq:
        continue

    # Find CAM subsequence
    cam_sub = None
    for track in shot_seq.get_tracks():
        if isinstance(track, unreal.MovieSceneSubTrack):
            for sub_section in track.get_sections():
                sub_seq = sub_section.get_sequence()
                if sub_seq and 'CAM' in sub_seq.get_name():
                    cam_sub = sub_seq

    if not cam_sub or len(cam_sub.get_bindings()) == 0:
        continue

    cam_binding = cam_sub.get_bindings()[0]
    portable_bid = shot_seq.get_portable_binding_id(shot_seq, cam_binding)

    # Ensure Camera Cuts track exists
    cc_track = None
    for track in shot_seq.get_tracks():
        if 'CameraCut' in type(track).__name__:
            cc_track = track
            break
    if not cc_track:
        cc_track = shot_seq.add_track(unreal.MovieSceneCameraCutTrack)

    # Clear and re-add section
    for old in cc_track.get_sections():
        cc_track.remove_section(old)

    cc_section = cc_track.add_section()
    cc_section.set_camera_binding_id(portable_bid)
    pr = shot_seq.get_playback_range()
    cc_section.set_range(pr.inclusive_start, pr.exclusive_end)

# Save
unreal.EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_dirty_packages(True, True)

docs.title: Common Mistakes
docs.text: Mistake Symptom Fix get_portable_binding_id(cam_sub, binding) SequenceID=0, "Object Binding is missing!" Use get_portable_binding_id(shot_seq, binding) get_binding_id(binding) SequenceID=0, binding not found Use get_portable_binding_id instead Camera binding at shot level Works but breaks organization Move binding to CAM sub, use cross-ref Camera Cuts inside CAM sub Camera doesn't switch between shots Camera Cuts must be at shot level

docs.text: These tools communicate via Unreal's Remote Control API (ports 30010/30020).

docs.title: manage_asset
docs.text:
Asset discovery and management.

Action Description list List assets by path or type import Import external files create_material Create new materials get_properties Read asset properties

docs.title: Using Tools
docs.text:
You don't need to know tool names - just describe what you want:

# Instead of:
"Use control_actor spawn with type cube at position 0, 0, 100"

# Just say:
"Spawn a cube at 0, 0, 100"

Claude automatically selects the right tools.
